## ISSUE 6: `changelog.js` — `appendToChangelog` has an off-by-one when appending to existing section

**File:** `agent/lib/changelog.js`, lines 68-76  
**Severity:** MEDIUM

**Problem:** When a section already exists for the current date+version:

```js
  if (existing.includes(`## v${appVersion} — ${date}`)) {
    const sectionEnd = existing.indexOf('\n## ', existing.indexOf(`## v${appVersion} — ${date}`) + 1);
    const insertPoint = sectionEnd === -1 ? existing.length : sectionEnd;

    const newLines = entries.map(e => `- **${e.category}**: ${e.description}`).join('\n');
    existing = existing.slice(0, insertPoint) + '\n' + newLines + existing.slice(insertPoint);
  }
```

The problem: `sectionEnd` finds the next `\n## ` (the start of the next section). The `insertPoint` is set to that position. Then new content is inserted at `insertPoint`. But there's no check for whether the content being appended is a duplicate of content already in the section. If the agent runs twice with the same changes, the same entries are appended again.

Additionally, the insertion creates a trailing newline issue. If `insertPoint` is at `sectionEnd`, the code inserts `'\n' + newLines` before the `'\n## '`, resulting in `...existing content\n- new entry\n## Next Section...` — which has no blank line between the end of the current section's entries and the next section header. The existing format has `\n\n` between sections.

**Fix — `agent/lib/changelog.js`**, lines 68-76:

```js
  if (existing.includes(`## v${appVersion} — ${date}`)) {
    // Find the bounds of the existing section
    const sectionStart = existing.indexOf(`## v${appVersion} — ${date}`);
    const sectionEnd = existing.indexOf('\n## ', sectionStart + 1);
    const insertPoint = sectionEnd === -1 ? existing.length : sectionEnd;

    // Get the existing section content to check for duplicates
    const existingSection = existing.slice(sectionStart, insertPoint);

    // Only add entries not already in this section
    const newLines = entries
      .map(e => `- **${e.category}**: ${e.description}`)
      .filter(line => !existingSection.includes(line));

    if (newLines.length > 0) {
      existing = existing.slice(0, insertPoint) + '\n' + newLines.join('\n') + '\n' + existing.slice(insertPoint);
    }
  }
```

---

## ISSUE 7: `changelog.js` — `updateAppChangelog` trimming logic is incorrect

**File:** `agent/lib/changelog.js`, lines 103-109  
**Severity:** HIGH

**Problem:** The code to trim the changelog to `MAX_APP_ENTRIES` entries:

```js
    const trimmed = allEntries.split('\n')
      .filter(l => l.trim().startsWith('{'))
      .slice(0, MAX_APP_ENTRIES)
      .join(',\n');
```

This splits the combined entries string by newlines and filters for lines starting with `{`. But each entry looks like:

```js
  { date: '2024-01-15', category: 'Banners', text: 'Updated Phase 2 banners' }
```

A single entry is on one line, starting with spaces then `{`. The filter `l.trim().startsWith('{')` correctly matches these. However, the entries in `allEntries` are comma-separated:

```js
const allEntries = newEntries.join(',\n') + (existingEntries ? ',\n' + existingEntries : '');
```

So `allEntries` looks like:
```
  { date: '...', ... },
  { date: '...', ... },
  { date: '...', ... }
```

When split by `\n`, each line is `  { date: '...', ... },` (with a trailing comma except the last). After filtering and slicing, `.join(',\n')` adds another comma between lines. This creates **double commas** for all lines that already have trailing commas:

```js
  { date: '...', ... },,
  { date: '...', ... },,
  { date: '...', ... },
```

This will cause a JavaScript syntax error in the output file.

**Fix — `agent/lib/changelog.js`**, lines 103-109:

```js
    // Parse existing entries and prepend new ones
    const existingEntries = existingMatch[1].trim();
    
    // Combine new + existing entries, each as a clean line without trailing commas
    const parseEntries = (str) => str.split('\n')
      .map(l => l.trim())
      .filter(l => l.startsWith('{'))
      .map(l => l.replace(/,\s*$/, '').trim()); // strip trailing commas

    const allParsed = [
      ...newEntries.map(e => e.trim()),
      ...parseEntries(existingEntries),
    ];

    // Deduplicate by content
    const seen = new Set();
    const unique = allParsed.filter(entry => {
      if (seen.has(entry)) return false;
      seen.add(entry);
      return true;
    });

    // Trim to max
    const trimmed = unique.slice(0, MAX_APP_ENTRIES);

    const newBlock = `const CHANGELOG = [\n${trimmed.map(e => '  ' + e).join(',\n')}\n];\n`;
    buf = buf.replace(existingMatch[0], newBlock);
```

## ISSUE 8: `changelog.js` — `updateAppChangelog` regex doesn't account for double-quoted strings

**File:** `agent/lib/changelog.js`, line 96  
**Severity:** MEDIUM

**Problem:** The regex to find the existing CHANGELOG:

```js
const existingMatch = buf.match(/const CHANGELOG\s*=\s*\[([\s\S]*?)\];\s*\n/);
```

This uses a *lazy* `[\s\S]*?` which will match the shortest possible string between `[` and `];\n`. If any entry in the changelog contains a `];` substring in its text field (e.g., `text: 'Fixed array parsing ];'`), the regex would match prematurely, truncating the array.

More realistically, if there's a comment like `// end of CHANGELOG];` somewhere, this could also break. The regex would match the first `];\n` it finds.

**Fix — This is a low-probability issue, but can be made more robust:**

```js
  // Match CHANGELOG array — use a more specific anchor
  const existingMatch = buf.match(/const CHANGELOG\s*=\s*\[([\s\S]*?)\];\s*\n/);
```

Actually, since entries are constructed by the agent itself and contain only controlled `date`, `category`, and `text` fields, and `text` has `'` escaped (`e.description.replace(/'/g, "\\'")`), a `];` in the content would appear as `\\'];` which won't match `];\n`. So this is acceptable.

**Verdict:** LOW risk, no fix needed.

## ISSUE 9: `.github/workflows/ww-auto-update.yml` — Evolution log commit happens after PR creation and won't be included

**File:** `.github/workflows/ww-auto-update.yml`, lines 119-124  
**Severity:** MEDIUM

**Problem:** The workflow step "Commit evolution log" runs **after** the "Create Pull Request" step:

```yaml
      - name: Create Pull Request
        if: steps.check.outputs.has_changes == 'true'
        id: create-pr
        uses: peter-evans/create-pull-request@v6
        # ...

      - name: Commit evolution log
        if: steps.check.outputs.has_changes == 'true'
        run: |
          if [ -f agent/evolution-log.md ]; then
            git add agent/evolution-log.md
            git diff --cached --quiet || git commit -m "[agent] Update evolution log"
          fi
```

The `peter-evans/create-pull-request` action creates its own branch, commits, and pushes. After it runs, the working directory state is ambiguous — the action may have checked out the new branch or stayed on the base. The subsequent `git commit` is a raw git operation that:
1. Won't be part of the PR branch (the PR is already created and pushed)
2. May commit to the base branch (e.g., `main`) directly, which could be protected
3. May fail silently if the branch state is unexpected

**Fix — `.github/workflows/ww-auto-update.yml`** — move the evolution log staging BEFORE the PR creation:

```yaml
      - name: Stage evolution log
        if: steps.check.outputs.has_changes == 'true'
        run: |
          if [ -f agent/evolution-log.md ]; then
            git add agent/evolution-log.md
          fi

      - name: Create Pull Request
        if: steps.check.outputs.has_changes == 'true'
        id: create-pr
        uses: peter-evans/create-pull-request@v6
        with:
          token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          commit-message: "[auto-update] ${{ steps.mode.outputs.mode }} update"
          title: "[Auto-Update] ${{ steps.mode.outputs.mode }} — Game Data Update"
          body: |
            ## Automated Game Data Update (${{ steps.mode.outputs.mode }} mode)

            The WW Update Agent detected changes and applied updates.

            **Mode:** `${{ steps.mode.outputs.mode }}`
            **Trigger:** ${{ github.event_name == 'schedule' && 'Scheduled cron' || 'Manual dispatch' }}

            ### Review checklist:
            - [ ] Banner characters and dates are correct
            - [ ] Event end dates match official schedule
            - [ ] New character/weapon data is accurate
            - [ ] Images are correct format and quality
            - [ ] Code changes (if any) don't break functionality
            - [ ] No data integrity issues

            ---
            *Generated by WW Update Agent*
          branch: auto-update/${{ steps.mode.outputs.mode }}
```

## ISSUE 10: `.github/workflows/ww-auto-update.yml` — Stale PR cleanup uses 12-hour window, may close valid PRs

**File:** `.github/workflows/ww-auto-update.yml`, lines 107-113  
**Severity:** MEDIUM

**Problem:**

```yaml
      - name: Close stale auto-update PRs
        if: steps.check.outputs.has_changes == 'true'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          STALE=$(gh pr list --label "auto-update" --state open --json number,createdAt -q '.[] | select((.createdAt | fromdateiso8601) < (now - 43200)) | .number')
```

The threshold `43200` seconds = 12 hours. The cron runs weekly (Mondays at 00:00 UTC). A PR created on Monday will be stale by Monday at 12:00 UTC, but a reviewer might not get to it until Tuesday. Additionally, manual runs via `workflow_dispatch` could create PRs that get auto-closed by the next manual run if it happens 12+ hours later.

**Fix:** Since the cron is weekly, increase the staleness threshold to 6 days (518400 seconds):

```yaml
      - name: Close stale auto-update PRs
        if: steps.check.outputs.has_changes == 'true'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          # Close auto-update PRs older than 6 days (superseded by this run)
          STALE=$(gh pr list --label "auto-update" --state open --json number,createdAt -q '.[] | select((.createdAt | fromdateiso8601) < (now - 518400)) | .number')
          for PR in $STALE; do
            echo "Closing stale PR #${PR}"
            gh pr close $PR --comment "Superseded by newer auto-update." || true
          done
```

## ISSUE 11: `vercel.json` — CSP blocks inline scripts that Vite injects

**File:** `whispering-wishes-replit/vercel.json`, line 8  
**Severity:** HIGH

**Problem:** The Content-Security-Policy header includes:

```
script-src 'self';
```

Vite's production build injects inline `<script>` tags with module preload hints and sometimes an inline script for dynamic imports. Without `'unsafe-inline'` or a nonce/hash, these scripts will be **blocked** by the CSP, potentially breaking the entire app on page load.

Specifically, Vite generates HTML like:
```html
<script type="module" crossorigin src="/assets/index-xxxx.js"></script>
<script type="module">/* modulepreload polyfill */</script>
```

The second `<script>` tag is inline and will be blocked.

**Fix — `whispering-wishes-replit/vercel.json`** — update the CSP to account for Vite's output. The safest approach is to use `'unsafe-inline'` for scripts (less ideal) or configure Vite to not emit inline scripts. Since configuring Vite is out of scope for this file, the pragmatic fix:

```json
{
  "headers": [
    {
      "source": "/(.*)",
      "headers": [
        {
          "key": "Content-Security-Policy",
          "value": "default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' https://i.ibb.co https://ibb.co https://i.imgur.com https://cdn.discordapp.com https://media.discordapp.net https://pbs.twimg.com https://raw.githubusercontent.com https://i.postimg.cc https://wuwa.gg https://wuwatracker.com https://*.googleapis.com data:; connect-src 'self' https://*.firebaseio.com https://*.googleapis.com https://i.ibb.co https://ibb.co https://i.imgur.com https://cdn.discordapp.com https://media.discordapp.net https://pbs.twimg.com https://raw.githubusercontent.com https://i.postimg.cc https://wuwa.gg https://wuwatracker.com; font-src 'self' https://fonts.gstatic.com; frame-ancestors 'none'"
        },
        {
          "key": "X-Frame-Options",
          "value": "DENY"
        },
        {
          "key": "X-Content-Type-Options",
          "value": "nosniff"
        },
        {
          "key": "Referrer-Policy",
          "value": "strict-origin-when-cross-origin"
        },
        {
          "key": "Permissions-Policy",
          "value": "camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=()"
        },
        {
          "key": "Strict-Transport-Security",
          "value": "max-age=63072000; includeSubDomains; preload"
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

**Note:** The better long-term fix is to configure Vite to avoid inline scripts entirely (using `build.modulePreload.polyfill: false` or generating CSP hashes). But for the immediate fix, `'unsafe-inline'` for `script-src` prevents a broken deployment.

```js
    log.warn('No banner data provided for image search');

Featured characters: ${charNames}
```

```js
const checkFirebaseRateLimit = (pathKey) => {
  const now = Date.now();
  const lastWrite = firebaseWriteTimestamps.get(pathKey) || 0;
  if (now - lastWrite < FIREBASE_WRITE_COOLDOWN_MS) return false;
  firebaseWriteTimestamps.set(pathKey, now);
  // Evict stale entries periodically to prevent memory leak
  if (firebaseWriteTimestamps.size > FIREBASE_RATE_LIMIT_MAX_ENTRIES) {
    for (const [key, ts] of firebaseWriteTimestamps) {

        firebaseWriteTimestamps.delete(key);
      }
    }
  }
  return true;
};
```

## PERF-01: Massive Base64 `HEADER_ICON` Inlined in JS Bundle (~5.4KB uncompressed)

**File:** `whispering-wishes-replit/src/appcore-data.js`, lines 10–11
**Severity:** MEDIUM

**Problem:** The `HEADER_ICON` constant is a ~4KB base64 PNG string inlined directly into the JavaScript module. This:
1. Adds ~5.4KB to the parsed JS bundle (base64 is ~33% larger than binary)
2. Cannot be cached independently of the JS bundle — every code change re-downloads this image
3. Gets parsed by the JS engine as a string literal on every page load
4. Cannot benefit from image CDN optimization, WebP conversion, or responsive sizing

Since this is a static app icon that never changes, it should be a separate file served from the public directory or imported as a URL via Vite's asset handling.

**Fix:** Move the icon to a static asset and import it as a URL.

**Step 1 — Create file `whispering-wishes-replit/public/app-icon.png`:**
Export the base64 string to a PNG file. (The actual binary is the decoded content of the base64 string.)

**Step 2 — Update `whispering-wishes-replit/src/appcore-data.js`:**

```js
// ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
// WHISPERING WISHES v3.2.3 — appcore-data.js
// Pure data, constants, game databases. No React. Leaf module (no imports).
// ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

const APP_VERSION = '3.2.3';
const MAX_IMPORT_SIZE_MB = 5;

// Header icon — served as a static asset for independent caching and smaller JS bundle.
// Falls back to empty string if the asset path is unavailable (non-breaking).
const HEADER_ICON = '/app-icon.png';
```

**Impact:** ~5.4KB removed from the JS parse/compile path. The image is now independently cacheable with a long `Cache-Control` header, and Vite can apply content-hashing for cache busting automatically if moved to `src/assets/` and imported instead.

**If the base64 approach MUST be kept** (e.g., offline-first PWA requirement where the icon must be available without a network request), at minimum move it to a separate file and lazy-load it:

```js
// appcore-data.js — keep the export but defer the actual string
let _headerIconCache = null;
const getHeaderIcon = () => {
  if (_headerIconCache) return _headerIconCache;
  // This will be tree-shaken if unused, and only parsed when called
  _headerIconCache = 'data:image/png;base64,iVBORw0KGgo...'; // full string
  return _headerIconCache;
};
// Export the getter instead of the string
const HEADER_ICON = null; // consumers should use getHeaderIcon()
```

**Recommended approach:** Use the static asset (`/app-icon.png`). The PWA service worker will cache it anyway.

## PERF-02: `buildBannerForm` Recreated on Every Render Despite `useCallback` with Empty Dependencies

**File:** `whispering-wishes-replit/src/App.jsx`, lines ~139–155
**Severity:** MEDIUM

**Problem:** `buildBannerForm` is wrapped in `useCallback` with `[]` deps, which is correct for memoization. However, it's called in the `useState` initializer for `bannerForm`:

```js
const [bannerForm, setBannerForm] = useState(() => buildBannerForm(activeBanners));
```

The `activeBanners` state is initialized from `getActiveBanners()`, and `buildBannerForm` does expensive JSON.stringify operations on the banner characters and weapons arrays. This is fine for initialization. BUT the real problem is that `buildBannerForm` creates multiple `Object.fromEntries(... .map(...))` calls that allocate many intermediate arrays on every call. When the admin saves new banners, `buildBannerForm(newBanners)` is called again, and all those intermediaries are created.

More critically, `updateBannerForm` creates a new function per render cycle that creates a new state object:

```js
const updateBannerForm = useCallback((field, value) => setBannerForm(prev => ({ ...prev, [field]: value })), []);
```

This is fine per-call, but every field keystroke in the admin banner form triggers a full spread of the `bannerForm` object, which includes the `charsJson` and `weapsJson` strings (potentially large). For rapid typing, this causes jank.

**Fix — debounce the banner form text fields and avoid spreading large objects:**

```js
// Replace the existing updateBannerForm with a debounced version for text fields:
const bannerFormTextBufferRef = useRef({});
const bannerFormFlushTimerRef = useRef(null);

const updateBannerForm = useCallback((field, value) => {
  // For large text fields (JSON editors), buffer and debounce
  const largeFields = ['charsJson', 'weapsJson'];
  if (largeFields.includes(field)) {
    bannerFormTextBufferRef.current[field] = value;
    if (bannerFormFlushTimerRef.current) {
      clearTimeout(bannerFormFlushTimerRef.current);
    }
    bannerFormFlushTimerRef.current = setTimeout(() => {
      const buffered = { ...bannerFormTextBufferRef.current };
      bannerFormTextBufferRef.current = {};
      setBannerForm(prev => ({ ...prev, ...buffered }));
    }, 300);
    return;
  }
  setBannerForm(prev => ({ ...prev, [field]: value }));
}, []);

// Cleanup timer on unmount
useEffect(() => {
  return () => {
    if (bannerFormFlushTimerRef.current) {
      clearTimeout(bannerFormFlushTimerRef.current);
    }
  };
}, []);
```

**Impact:** Eliminates ~10-20 unnecessary state updates per second during admin JSON editing, preventing re-renders of the entire `WhisperingWishesInner` component tree.

## PERF-05: `DEFAULT_VISUAL_SETTINGS` Object Spread Happens on Every Mount Unnecessarily

**File:** `whispering-wishes-replit/src/App.jsx`, lines ~92–107 and ~160–175
**Severity:** MEDIUM

**Problem:** The visual settings initialization runs two phases:

1. **Phase 1 (state init):** `useState(() => ({ ...DEFAULT_VISUAL_SETTINGS }))` — spreads the defaults
2. **Phase 2 (effect):** Reads localStorage, parses JSON, then does a `setVisualSettings(prev => { ... merge ... })` that iterates all keys

The Phase 2 effect always runs, even when there's no saved settings. The merge loop inside `setVisualSettings` creates a new object every time, triggering a re-render. When localStorage has no saved settings, the effect still calls `setVisualSettings` with a function, which React evaluates — and even though the returned object is value-identical, it's a new reference, so React schedules a re-render.

**Fix — skip the state update if there's nothing to merge:**

```js
// Load from localStorage after mount (so SSR/preview gets defaults)
useEffect(() => {
  if (!storageAvailable) return;
  try {
    const saved = localStorage.getItem(VISUAL_SETTINGS_KEY);
    if (!saved) return; // No saved settings — keep defaults, skip re-render
    const parsed = JSON.parse(saved);
    if (!parsed || typeof parsed !== 'object') return;
    
    // Check if any saved value actually differs from defaults before triggering re-render
    let hasDiff = false;
    for (const key of Object.keys(DEFAULT_VISUAL_SETTINGS)) {
      if (parsed[key] !== undefined && parsed[key] !== null && parsed[key] !== DEFAULT_VISUAL_SETTINGS[key]) {
        hasDiff = true;
        break;
      }
    }
    if (!hasDiff) return; // Saved settings match defaults — skip re-render

    setVisualSettings(prev => {
      const merged = { ...prev };
      for (const key of Object.keys(prev)) {
        if (parsed[key] !== undefined && parsed[key] !== null) merged[key] = parsed[key];
      }
      return merged;
    });
  } catch { /* corrupt localStorage — keep defaults */ }
}, []);
```

**Impact:** Eliminates 1 unnecessary re-render of the entire app on mount for users who haven't customized visual settings (which is the majority of users, especially first-time visitors).

**Impact:** Each removed unused icon saves ~1-2KB from the production bundle. If 5-10 are unused, that's 5-20KB saved.

## PERF-07: `recharts` Imports — Entire Components Loaded Eagerly for Tabs That May Never Be Viewed

**File:** `whispering-wishes-replit/src/App.jsx`, line 3
**Severity:** HIGH

```js
import { XAxis, YAxis, Tooltip as RechartsTooltip, ResponsiveContainer, AreaChart, Area, BarChart, Bar, Cell } from 'recharts';
```

**Problem:** `recharts` is the single largest dependency in the bundle. A typical recharts import adds **150-200KB** to the production bundle (gzipped: ~45-60KB). These chart components are only used in the Stats tab (`[TAB-STATS]`), which most users may never visit in a session. Loading all of recharts eagerly penalizes the initial page load for every user.

**Fix — lazy-load recharts components using React.lazy and dynamic import:**

```js
// Remove the static recharts import at line 3:
// import { XAxis, YAxis, Tooltip as RechartsTooltip, ResponsiveContainer, AreaChart, Area, BarChart, Bar, Cell } from 'recharts';

// Replace with lazy-loaded components. Create a wrapper:
const LazyRecharts = React.lazy(() =>
  import('recharts').then(mod => ({
    default: () => null, // We don't use a default export
    ...mod,
  }))
);

// Better approach — create a small wrapper component that loads recharts on demand:
// Add this near the top of App.jsx, after the React import:

const RechartsContext = React.createContext(null);

const RechartsProvider = React.memo(({ children }) => {
  const [mods, setMods] = React.useState(null);

  React.useEffect(() => {
    let cancelled = false;
    import('recharts').then(mod => {
      if (!cancelled) setMods(mod);
    });
    return () => { cancelled = true; };
  }, []);

  return React.createElement(RechartsContext.Provider, { value: mods }, children);
});

const useRecharts = () => React.useContext(RechartsContext);
```

Then in the Stats tab rendering code, guard chart rendering:

```jsx
// Inside the Stats tab section:
const recharts = useRecharts();

if (!recharts) {
  return <div className="text-center text-gray-400 py-8">Loading charts...</div>;
}

const { XAxis, YAxis, Tooltip: RechartsTooltip, ResponsiveContainer, AreaChart, Area, BarChart, Bar, Cell } = recharts;

// ... rest of chart rendering unchanged
```

**However**, this approach requires modifying the Stats tab JSX deep in the file. A simpler alternative that achieves the same bundle-splitting benefit is to extract the Stats tab into its own component file and use `React.lazy`:

```js
// In App.jsx, at the top:
const StatsTab = React.lazy(() => import('./StatsTab'));

// In the tab rendering switch:
// case 'stats':
//   return <React.Suspense fallback={<div className="text-center text-gray-400 py-8">Loading stats...</div>}>
//     <StatsTab state={state} dispatch={dispatch} ... />
//   </React.Suspense>;
```

**Since we can't create new files in this audit, the practical immediate fix is to document this as a TODO and ensure the recharts import is at least not blocking critical path rendering.**

**Minimal fix — use dynamic import at the point of use:**

Replace line 3:
```js
// REMOVED: static recharts import
// Charts are loaded on-demand when the Stats tab is first opened
```

Add a lazy-loading hook near the component body:

```js
// Inside WhisperingWishesInner, add:
const [rechartsLib, setRechartsLib] = useState(null);
const rechartsLoadedRef = useRef(false);

// Load recharts only when the Stats tab is first activated
useEffect(() => {
  if (state.activeTab === 'stats' && !rechartsLoadedRef.current) {
    rechartsLoadedRef.current = true;
    import('recharts').then(mod => setRechartsLib(mod)).catch(() => {});
  }
}, [state.activeTab]);
```

**Impact:** Removes ~150-200KB from the initial bundle. Stats tab shows a loading indicator for ~200ms on first visit while recharts loads. Subsequent visits are instant (module cached by browser).

## PERF-08: `trophyOverrides` State Initializer Runs JSON.parse Without Error Handling for Malformed Data

**File:** `whispering-wishes-replit/src/App.jsx`, lines ~135–137
**Severity:** LOW

```js
const [trophyOverrides, setTrophyOverrides] = useState(() => {
  try { const s = localStorage.getItem(TROPHY_OVERRIDES_KEY); return s ? JSON.parse(s) : {}; } catch { return {}; }
});
```

This has a `try/catch`, which is good. But the parsed result is not validated — if localStorage contains `"[]"` (an array instead of an object), the state would be an array, and any `trophyOverrides[key]` access would return `undefined` but `Object.keys(trophyOverrides)` would return numeric indices. This could cause subtle rendering bugs.

**Fix:**

```js
const [trophyOverrides, setTrophyOverrides] = useState(() => {
  try {
    const s = localStorage.getItem(TROPHY_OVERRIDES_KEY);
    if (!s) return {};
    const parsed = JSON.parse(s);
    // Ensure it's a plain object, not an array or primitive
    if (!parsed || typeof parsed !== 'object' || Array.isArray(parsed)) return {};
    return parsed;
  } catch {
    return {};
  }
});
```

## PERF-09: `CURRENT_BANNERS` Contains 11 Image URLs That Block Discovery and Preloading

**File:** `whispering-wishes-replit/src/appcore-data.js`, lines ~103–115
**Severity:** MEDIUM

**Problem:** The `CURRENT_BANNERS` object contains 11 external image URLs (ibb.co hosted). These images are critical for the Tracker and Events tabs — the first things users see. But because the URLs are buried in a JS constant, the browser cannot discover them until:
1. The JS bundle is downloaded
2. The JS is parsed and executed
3. React renders the components that reference these URLs
4. The browser starts fetching the images

This is a 4-step waterfall. For the primary banner images (character and weapon banners), this adds 500-2000ms to perceived load time on mobile.

**Fix — add `<link rel="preload">` hints for the most critical images. In the HTML template:**

**File:** `whispering-wishes-replit/index.html` (if it exists, add to `<head>`):**

```html
<!-- Preload critical banner images to eliminate discovery delay -->
<link rel="preload" as="image" href="https://i.ibb.co/Kc4nxTrD/post-lament-anthropocene-stars-intertwined-luuk-herssen-v0-b4p94ck3quag1.jpg" />
<link rel="preload" as="image" href="https://i.ibb.co/rGyhGWWd/galbrena-drip-marketing-v0-xcdhhporc2nf1.jpg" />
```

**Alternative (dynamic, works even when banners change via admin):** Add a preload effect in `App.jsx`:

```js
// Add inside WhisperingWishesInner, near the top effects:
useEffect(() => {
  // Preload critical banner images to reduce perceived load time
  const criticalImages = [
    ...activeBanners.characters?.map(c => c.imageUrl).filter(Boolean) || [],
    ...activeBanners.weapons?.map(w => w.imageUrl).filter(Boolean) || [],
  ].slice(0, 4); // Preload at most 4 images

  criticalImages.forEach(url => {
    const link = document.createElement('link');
    link.rel = 'preload';
    link.as = 'image';
    link.href = url;
    document.head.appendChild(link);
  });

  // Cleanup on banner change
  return () => {
    document.querySelectorAll('link[rel="preload"][as="image"]').forEach(el => {
      if (criticalImages.includes(el.href)) {
        el.remove();
      }
    });
  };
}, [activeBanners.characters, activeBanners.weapons]);
```

**Impact:** Saves 500-1500ms on initial banner image display by allowing the browser to start fetching images while JS is still parsing.

## PERF-11: `generateUniqueId` — Inefficient Fallback Path Creates Unnecessary Array Allocation

**File:** `whispering-wishes-replit/src/appcore-data.js`, lines ~27–36
**Severity:** LOW

```js
try {
  const arr = new Uint8Array(8);
  crypto.getRandomValues(arr);
  return `${Date.now()}-${++__uniqueIdCounter}-${Array.from(arr, b => b.toString(36)).join('')}`;
} catch {
  return `${Date.now()}-${++__uniqueIdCounter}-${Math.random().toString(36).slice(2)}`;
}
```

**Problem:** The CSPRNG fallback allocates a `Uint8Array(8)`, then `Array.from()` creates a new array of 8 strings, then `.join('')` concatenates them. This is called frequently (every toast, every dispatch ID). The `Array.from` with a map callback is slightly wasteful.

**Fix — use a loop instead of Array.from for the hot path:**

```js
try {
  const arr = new Uint8Array(8);
  crypto.getRandomValues(arr);
  let rand = '';
  for (let i = 0; i < 8; i++) rand += arr[i].toString(36);
  return `${Date.now()}-${++__uniqueIdCounter}-${rand}`;
} catch {
  return `${Date.now()}-${++__uniqueIdCounter}-${Math.random().toString(36).slice(2)}`;
}
```

**Impact:** Eliminates 1 intermediate array allocation per call. Microsecond-level improvement, but this function is on every hot path.

## ISSUE PP-01: `MaterialItem` Not Memoized — Rendered 20-40× Per Modal Open

**File:** `whispering-wishes-replit/src/appcore-components.jsx`, lines 29–38
**Severity:** MEDIUM

**Problem:** `MaterialItem` is a pure presentational component rendered inside `CharacterDetailModal` and `WeaponDetailModal` grids (6-12 instances per modal). Each modal re-render (e.g., during scroll, or parent state change) causes all `MaterialItem` instances to re-render despite receiving the same `name`/`qty` props. The `MATERIAL_IMAGES` lookup and error handler reference are stable, so memoization is safe and free.

**Fix:**
```jsx
// whispering-wishes-replit/src/appcore-components.jsx — replace lines 29–38

const MaterialItem = memo(({ name, qty }) => {
  const img = MATERIAL_IMAGES[name];
  return (
    <div className="flex items-center gap-1.5 p-1.5 rounded-lg bg-white/5 border border-white/10 min-w-0">
      {img ? <img src={img} alt={name} className="w-7 h-7 rounded object-contain flex-shrink-0" onError={hideOnError} /> : <div className="w-7 h-7 rounded bg-white/10 flex-shrink-0" />}
      <div className="min-w-0 flex-1">
        <div className="text-[9px] text-gray-300 truncate leading-tight">{name}</div>
        {qty != null && qty > 0 && <div className="text-[9px] text-yellow-400 font-bold leading-tight">&times;{qty}</div>}
      </div>
    </div>
  );
});
MaterialItem.displayName = 'MaterialItem';
```

## ISSUE PP-02: `CharacterDetailModal` Creates New Functions and Arrays on Every Render

**File:** `whispering-wishes-replit/src/appcore-components.jsx`, lines ~115–125
**Severity:** MEDIUM

**Problem:** `parseTeamMembers` is declared as a new function inside the component body on every render. While modals don't re-render as frequently as list items, this function is pure and stateless — it should be hoisted to module scope.

Additionally, the `[...Array(data.rarity)]` star array is recreated on every render. This is minor but avoidable.

**Fix:**
```jsx
// whispering-wishes-replit/src/appcore-components.jsx — hoist above CharacterDetailModal

// Hoisted: parse team strings into character names (pure function, no component dependencies)
const parseTeamMembers = (teamStr) => {
  return teamStr.split('+').map(s => s.trim()).filter(Boolean);
};

// Pre-built star arrays to avoid allocation on every render
const STAR_ARRAYS = {
  3: [0, 1, 2],
  4: [0, 1, 2, 3],
  5: [0, 1, 2, 3, 4],
};
const getStarArray = (rarity) => STAR_ARRAYS[rarity] || Array.from({ length: rarity }, (_, i) => i);
```

Then inside `CharacterDetailModal`, replace:
```jsx
// OLD:
{[...Array(data.rarity)].map((_, i) => <Star key={i} size={12} className="text-yellow-400 fill-yellow-400" />)}

// NEW:
{getStarArray(data.rarity).map(i => <Star key={i} size={12} className="text-yellow-400 fill-yellow-400" />)}
```

And inside `WeaponDetailModal`, same replacement:
```jsx
// OLD:
{[...Array(data.rarity)].map((_, i) => <Star key={i} size={12} className="text-yellow-400 fill-yellow-400" />)}

// NEW:
{getStarArray(data.rarity).map(i => <Star key={i} size={12} className="text-yellow-400 fill-yellow-400" />)}
```

Also remove the `parseTeamMembers` declaration from inside `CharacterDetailModal` body (it's now module-scoped).

## ISSUE PP-03: `generateMaskGradient` / `generateVerticalMaskGradient` Perform Expensive String Operations Without Caching

**File:** `whispering-wishes-replit/src/appcore-components.jsx`, lines 45–82
**Severity:** MEDIUM

**Problem:** These gradient generators produce identical CSS gradient strings for the same `(fadePos, fadeIntensity)` inputs. They're called on every render of collection cards and banner backgrounds — potentially 50+ calls per render with only 3-5 unique `(pos, intensity)` combinations. Each call builds 5+ intermediate strings, does `toFixed` calls, and joins them.

**Fix — add a simple memoization cache:**
```js
// whispering-wishes-replit/src/appcore-components.jsx — replace lines 45–82

// Memoization caches for gradient generators — keyed by "pos|intensity"
const _maskGradientCache = new Map();
const _vertMaskGradientCache = new Map();

const generateMaskGradient = (fadePos, fadeIntensity) => {
  if (fadePos === undefined || fadeIntensity === undefined) {
    return 'linear-gradient(to right, rgba(0,0,0,0) 0%, rgba(0,0,0,0) 10%, rgba(0,0,0,0.15) 20%, rgba(0,0,0,0.35) 30%, rgba(0,0,0,0.6) 40%, rgba(0,0,0,0.9) 50%, rgba(0,0,0,0.9) 100%)';
  }
  const cacheKey = `${fadePos}|${fadeIntensity}`;
  const cached = _maskGradientCache.get(cacheKey);
  if (cached) return cached;

  const maxOpacity = fadeIntensity / 100;
  const endPos = fadePos;
  let result;
  if (endPos <= 10) {
    result = `linear-gradient(to right, rgba(0,0,0,0) 0%, rgba(0,0,0,${maxOpacity}) ${endPos}%, rgba(0,0,0,${maxOpacity}) 100%)`;
  } else {
    const steps = [`rgba(0,0,0,0) 0%`];
    const fadeStart = Math.max(0, endPos - 40);
    if (fadeStart > 0) steps.push(`rgba(0,0,0,0) ${fadeStart}%`);
    for (let i = 1; i <= 5; i++) {
      const pos = fadeStart + (endPos - fadeStart) * (i / 5);
      const opacity = maxOpacity * (i / 5);
      steps.push(`rgba(0,0,0,${opacity.toFixed(2)}) ${pos.toFixed(0)}%`);
    }
    steps.push(`rgba(0,0,0,${maxOpacity}) 100%`);
    result = `linear-gradient(to right, ${steps.join(', ')})`;
  }

  _maskGradientCache.set(cacheKey, result);
  // Cap cache size — 50 unique gradient combos is more than enough
  if (_maskGradientCache.size > 50) {
    const firstKey = _maskGradientCache.keys().next().value;
    _maskGradientCache.delete(firstKey);
  }
  return result;
};

const generateVerticalMaskGradient = (fadePos, fadeIntensity, direction = 'bottom') => {
  const cacheKey = `${fadePos}|${fadeIntensity}|${direction}`;
  const cached = _vertMaskGradientCache.get(cacheKey);
  if (cached) return cached;

  const maxOpacity = fadeIntensity / 100;
  const endPos = fadePos;
  const dir = direction === 'top' ? 'to top' : 'to bottom';
  let result;
  if (endPos <= 10) {
    result = `linear-gradient(${dir}, rgba(0,0,0,0) 0%, rgba(0,0,0,${maxOpacity}) ${endPos}%, rgba(0,0,0,${maxOpacity}) 100%)`;
  } else {
    const steps = [`rgba(0,0,0,0) 0%`];
    const fadeStart = Math.max(0, endPos - 40);
    if (fadeStart > 0) steps.push(`rgba(0,0,0,0) ${fadeStart}%`);
    for (let i = 1; i <= 5; i++) {
      const pos = fadeStart + (endPos - fadeStart) * (i / 5);
      const opacity = maxOpacity * (i / 5);
      steps.push(`rgba(0,0,0,${opacity.toFixed(2)}) ${pos.toFixed(0)}%`);
    }
    steps.push(`rgba(0,0,0,${maxOpacity}) 100%`);
    result = `linear-gradient(${dir}, ${steps.join(', ')})`;
  }

  _vertMaskGradientCache.set(cacheKey, result);
  if (_vertMaskGradientCache.size > 50) {
    const firstKey = _vertMaskGradientCache.keys().next().value;
    _vertMaskGradientCache.delete(firstKey);
  }
  return result;
};
```

## ISSUE PP-04: `CountdownTimer` Creates New Objects in `useState` Initializer That Get Thrown Away

**File:** `whispering-wishes-replit/src/appcore-components.jsx`, lines within CountdownTimer (~line 340)
**Severity:** LOW

**Problem:** The `useState(() => getTimeRemaining(endDate))` initializer is fine. However, the four `useEffect`s that keep refs in sync (`currentEndRef`, `recalcFnRef`, `onExpireRef`) each create a new arrow function closure on every render even though they just do a single assignment. While minor, this is a hot component — every visible timer on the Events tab (6-12 instances) runs this on every render.

**Fix — merge the three ref-sync effects into one:**
```jsx
// whispering-wishes-replit/src/appcore-components.jsx — inside CountdownTimer
// Replace the three separate ref-sync useEffects:

// OLD (3 separate effects):
// useEffect(() => { currentEndRef.current = currentEnd; }, [currentEnd]);
// useEffect(() => { recalcFnRef.current = recalcFn; }, [recalcFn]);
// useEffect(() => { onExpireRef.current = onExpire; }, [onExpire]);

// NEW (single effect):
useEffect(() => {
  currentEndRef.current = currentEnd;
  recalcFnRef.current = recalcFn;
  onExpireRef.current = onExpire;
}, [currentEnd, recalcFn, onExpire]);
```

## ISSUE PP-05: `TabButton` Runs DOM Query `nav.querySelector('.tab-indicator')` on Every Active Tab Change

**File:** `whispering-wishes-replit/src/appcore-components.jsx`, lines in TabButton's useEffect
**Severity:** LOW

**Problem:** Every time the active tab changes, the `useEffect` inside `TabButton` runs `nav.querySelector('.tab-indicator')` for ALL 6 tab buttons (because `active` changes for all of them), but only the newly-active one actually needs to position the indicator. The non-active buttons do a wasted DOM query that finds the indicator but then does nothing because the `if (active && ...)` guard stops them — except the query still runs.

**Fix — move the guard before the DOM query:**
```jsx
// whispering-wishes-replit/src/appcore-components.jsx — TabButton's useEffect

useEffect(() => {
  // Guard early: only the active tab needs to position the indicator
  if (!active) return;
  try {
    if (btnRef.current && tabRef?.current) {
      requestAnimationFrame(() => {
        const btn = btnRef.current;
        const nav = tabRef?.current;
        if (!btn || !nav) return;
        const indicator = nav.querySelector('.tab-indicator');
        if (indicator) {
          indicator.style.left = `${btn.offsetLeft + btn.offsetWidth * 0.2}px`;
          indicator.style.width = `${btn.offsetWidth * 0.6}px`;
          indicator.style.background = `linear-gradient(90deg, rgba(237,175,24,0.6), rgba(237,175,24,1), rgba(237,175,24,0.6))`;
          indicator.style.boxShadow = `0 0 12px rgba(237,175,24,0.5)`;
        }
      });
    }
  } catch (e) { /* ignore indicator errors */ }
}, [active, tabRef]);
```

## ISSUE PP-06: `KuroStyles` Contains a Continuously-Running `conic-gradient` Animation on `.luck-badge::before`

**File:** `whispering-wishes-replit/src/appcore-providers.jsx`, within KuroStyles — `@keyframes badgeRotate`
**Severity:** MEDIUM

**Problem:** The `.luck-badge::before` pseudo-element runs an infinite `conic-gradient` rotation at 8s per cycle with a `blur(3px)` filter. This is a GPU-heavy operation because:
1. `conic-gradient` is not hardware-accelerated in all browsers
2. `filter: blur(3px)` on a 200%×200% element forces repeated rasterization
3. The animation runs even when the Analytics tab (where luck badges appear) is not visible

The fix is to use `will-change: transform` and `contain: strict` to hint the compositor, and add a `prefers-reduced-motion` media query.

**Fix:**
```css
/* whispering-wishes-replit/src/appcore-providers.jsx — within KuroStyles CSS string */
/* Replace the luck-badge block (~line 328 in the CSS) */

    .luck-badge {
      position: relative;
      overflow: hidden;
      padding: 1.5px;
      contain: layout style;
    }
    .luck-badge::before {
      content: '';
      position: absolute;
      top: -50%;
      left: -50%;
      width: 200%;
      height: 200%;
      background: conic-gradient(from 0deg, var(--badge-color), transparent 50%, var(--badge-color));
      animation: badgeRotate 8s linear infinite;
      opacity: 0.9;
      filter: blur(3px);
      will-change: transform;
    }
    @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
      .luck-badge::before {
        animation: none;
        opacity: 0.6;
      }
      .trophy-badge {
        animation: none;
      }
      .pulse-subtle {

      }
    }
    @keyframes badgeRotate {
      to { transform: rotate(360deg); }
    }
```

## ISSUE PP-07: `computeDistDP` Allocates a Massive 3D/4D Array Even for Small Calculations

**File:** `whispering-wishes-replit/src/appcore-engine.js`, lines within `computeDistDP`
**Severity:** HIGH

**Problem:** The DP table allocation `Array.from({length: N+1}, () => Array.from({length: MAX_PITY+1}, () => ...))` creates `(N+1) × 81` inner arrays unconditionally. For a typical calculation with N=160 pulls, character banner, 1 copy target:
- Table size: 161 × 81 × 2 × 11 = **286,902 array slots**
- Each inner-most `Array(maxCopies+1).fill(0)` creates 11 Float64 values
- Total: ~2.3MB of heap allocation per `calcStats` call

The `maxCopies` parameter defaults to 10, but for single-copy calculations (the most common case, `copies=1`), only indices 0 and 1 are ever meaningful. The DP correctly caps with `Math.min(k + 1, maxCopies)`, but allocates slots for all 11 copies regardless.

**Fix — pass `maxCopies` from `calcStats` based on actual need:**
```js
// whispering-wishes-replit/src/appcore-engine.js — in calcStats function

// OLD:
const dist = computeGachaDist(safePulls, isWeapon, safePity, startGuar, Math.max(safeCopies, 7));

// NEW: Only allocate DP table columns we actually need.
// We need at least safeCopies for the target, and +1 for overflow absorption.
// Cap at 7 for the p1-p7 display values, but no higher than necessary.
const maxCopiesNeeded = Math.max(safeCopies, 7);
const dist = computeGachaDist(safePulls, isWeapon, safePity, startGuar, maxCopiesNeeded);
```

Wait — actually this is already `Math.max(safeCopies, 7)`. The real optimization is that `calcStats` always requests at least 7 copies for p1-p7 display even when the user targets 1 copy. For the common case of `copies=1`, the DP table has 8 slots instead of the 2 that are meaningful for the probability calculation.

The bigger win is avoiding re-computation when inputs haven't changed. `calcStats` is called from render paths and produces a new object every time, causing downstream re-renders:

```js
// whispering-wishes-replit/src/appcore-engine.js — add memoization to calcStats

// Add at module scope, before calcStats:
let _calcStatsCache = { key: '', result: null };

const calcStats = (pulls, pity, guaranteed, isChar, copies) => {
  // Check cache — single-entry LRU since calc inputs change as a group
  const cacheKey = `${pulls}|${pity}|${guaranteed}|${isChar}|${copies}`;
  if (_calcStatsCache.key === cacheKey && _calcStatsCache.result) {
    return _calcStatsCache.result;
  }

  // Defensive input validation
  const safePulls = Math.max(0, Math.min(MAX_CALC_PULLS, Math.floor(pulls) || 0));
  const safePity = Math.max(0, Math.min(MAX_PITY, Math.floor(pity) || 0));
  const safeCopies = Math.max(0, Math.floor(copies) || 0);
  const isWeapon = !isChar;
  const startGuar = guaranteed ? 1 : 0;

  const dist = computeGachaDist(safePulls, isWeapon, safePity, startGuar, Math.max(safeCopies, 7));

  const pGe = (k) => getCumulativeProb(dist, k) * 100;
  const stats = computeGachaStats(dist);
  const expectedToTarget = expectedPullsToTarget(isWeapon, safeCopies, safePity, startGuar);

  const worstCase = Math.max(0, isChar
    ? (HARD_PITY * 2 * safeCopies - (guaranteed ? HARD_PITY : 0) - safePity)
    : (HARD_PITY * safeCopies - safePity));
  const successRate = pGe(safeCopies);
  const missingPulls = Math.max(0, Math.ceil(expectedToTarget) - safePulls);

  const fourStarCount = Math.floor(safePulls / HARD_PITY_4STAR);
  const featuredFourStarCount = Math.floor(fourStarCount * FEATURED_4STAR_RATE);
  const pity4 = safePulls % HARD_PITY_4STAR;

  const result = {
    successRate: successRate.toFixed(1),
    p1: pGe(1).toFixed(1),
    p2: pGe(2).toFixed(1),
    p3: pGe(3).toFixed(1),
    p4: pGe(4).toFixed(1),
    p5: pGe(5).toFixed(1),
    p6: pGe(6).toFixed(1),
    p7: pGe(7).toFixed(1),
    missingPulls,
    missingAstrite: missingPulls * ASTRITE_PER_PULL,
    fourStarCount,
    featuredFourStarCount,
    pity4,
    expectedCopies: stats.expected.toFixed(2),
    stddev: stats.stddev.toFixed(2),
    expectedPullsToTarget: Math.ceil(expectedToTarget),
    worstCase,
  };

  _calcStatsCache = { key: cacheKey, result };
  return result;
};
```

## ISSUE PP-08: `reducer` Clones Entire `teams` Array on Every Team Action Even When Only One Slot Changes

**File:** `whispering-wishes-replit/src/appcore-engine.js`, lines in `SET_TEAM_SLOT`, `CLEAR_TEAM_SLOT`, `CLEAR_TEAM`, `RENAME_TEAM`
**Severity:** LOW

**Problem:** Each team mutation action does `state.teams.map(...)`, which creates 5 new team objects (one per team) even when only 1 team changed. For React's `useReducer`, this means all components that read any team from `state.teams` will detect a new reference and re-render, even if their specific team didn't change.

**Fix — only create a new object for the modified team:**
```js
// whispering-wishes-replit/src/appcore-engine.js — replace team action handlers

    case ACTION.SET_TEAM_SLOT: {
      const team = state.teams[action.teamIndex];
      if (!team || team.slots[action.slotIndex] === action.character) return state;
      const newSlots = [...team.slots];
      newSlots[action.slotIndex] = action.character;
      const newTeams = [...state.teams];
      newTeams[action.teamIndex] = { ...team, slots: newSlots };
      return { ...state, teams: newTeams };
    }
    case ACTION.CLEAR_TEAM_SLOT: {
      const team = state.teams[action.teamIndex];
      if (!team || team.slots[action.slotIndex] === null) return state;
      const newSlots = [...team.slots];
      newSlots[action.slotIndex] = null;
      const newTeams = [...state.teams];
      newTeams[action.teamIndex] = { ...team, slots: newSlots };
      return { ...state, teams: newTeams };
    }
    case ACTION.CLEAR_TEAM: {
      const team = state.teams[action.teamIndex];
      if (!team || team.slots.every(s => s === null)) return state;
      const newTeams = [...state.teams];
      newTeams[action.teamIndex] = { ...team, slots: [null, null, null] };
      return { ...state, teams: newTeams };
    }
    case ACTION.RENAME_TEAM: {
      const team = state.teams[action.teamIndex];
      const newName = (action.name || '').slice(0, 20) || team.name;
      if (!team || team.name === newName) return state;
      const newTeams = [...state.teams];
      newTeams[action.teamIndex] = { ...team, name: newName };
      return { ...state, teams: newTeams };
    }
```

## ISSUE PP-09: `saveToStorage` Called Synchronously on Every Dispatch — Blocks Main Thread

**File:** `whispering-wishes-replit/src/appcore-engine.js`, `saveToStorage` function
**Severity:** HIGH

**Problem:** While I can't see the exact call site (it's in App.jsx), the pattern is clear: `useReducer` + `useEffect` that calls `saveToStorage(state)` on every state change. `JSON.stringify` on the full state (which includes potentially thousands of pull history entries) is a synchronous main-thread operation that takes 5-50ms depending on data size. On mobile devices during rapid interactions (e.g., slider dragging in the calculator), this causes visible jank.

**Fix — debounce saves in `saveToStorage` using a module-level timer:**
```js
// whispering-wishes-replit/src/appcore-engine.js — replace saveToStorage

let _saveTimerId = null;
let _pendingState = null;

const saveToStorage = (state) => {
  if (!storageAvailable) return true;
  
  _pendingState = state;
  
  // Debounce: wait 300ms of inactivity before writing.
  // This batches rapid state changes (slider drags, typing) into one write.
  if (_saveTimerId) clearTimeout(_saveTimerId);
  _saveTimerId = setTimeout(() => {
    _saveTimerId = null;
    if (!_pendingState) return;
    try {
      const data = JSON.stringify(_pendingState);
      if (data.length > 4 * 1024 * 1024) {
        console.warn('Storage approaching limit:', (data.length / 1024 / 1024).toFixed(1) + 'MB');
      }
      localStorage.setItem(STORAGE_KEY, data);
    } catch (e) {
      console.error('Save failed (storage full?):', e);
    }
    _pendingState = null;
  }, 300);
  
  return true;
};

// Flush any pending save immediately (call on beforeunload)
const flushPendingSave = () => {
  if (_saveTimerId && _pendingState) {
    clearTimeout(_saveTimerId);
    _saveTimerId = null;
    try {
      localStorage.setItem(STORAGE_KEY, JSON.stringify(_pendingState));
    } catch (e) {
      console.error('Flush save failed:', e);
    }
    _pendingState = null;
  }
};
```

Then update the export:
```js
export {
  getTimeRemaining, getServerAdjustedEnd,
  getRecurringEventEnd, getNextDailyReset, getNextWeeklyReset,
  initialState, STORAGE_KEY, storageAvailable,
  sanitizeStateObj, sanitizeImportedState,
  loadFromStorage, saveToStorage, flushPendingSave, reducer, calcStats,
  ACTION,
};
```

The consuming code in `App.jsx` should add a `beforeunload` listener:
```js
// In App.jsx's main component useEffect:
useEffect(() => {
  const handleBeforeUnload = () => flushPendingSave();
  window.addEventListener('beforeunload', handleBeforeUnload);
  return () => window.removeEventListener('beforeunload', handleBeforeUnload);
}, []);
```

## ISSUE PP-10: Google Fonts Request is Render-Blocking

**File:** `whispering-wishes-replit/index.html`, lines 20–22
**Severity:** MEDIUM

**Problem:** The Google Fonts CSS is loaded via a blocking `<link href="..." rel="stylesheet">`. This delays First Contentful Paint by the time it takes to:
1. DNS resolve `fonts.googleapis.com`
2. Download the CSS file
3. DNS resolve `fonts.gstatic.com`
4. Download the font files referenced in the CSS

On slow connections, this adds 500ms-2s to initial render. The `display=swap` parameter helps with text visibility but the CSS itself still blocks rendering.

**Fix — use `preload` + async pattern:**
```html
<!-- whispering-wishes-replit/index.html — replace lines 20-22 -->
    <link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com" />
    <link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.gstatic.com" crossorigin />
    <!-- Non-blocking font load: preload the CSS, then apply it -->
    <link rel="preload" as="style" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Rajdhani:wght@400;500;600;700&family=JetBrains+Mono:wght@400;500;600;700&display=swap" />
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Rajdhani:wght@400;500;600;700&family=JetBrains+Mono:wght@400;500;600;700&display=swap" media="print" onload="this.media='all'" />
    <noscript><link rel="stylesheet" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Rajdhani:wght@400;500;600;700&family=JetBrains+Mono:wght@400;500;600;700&display=swap" /></noscript>
```

## ISSUE PP-11: `ToastProvider` Leaks Timeout References — No Cleanup on Unmount

**File:** `whispering-wishes-replit/src/appcore-providers.jsx`, lines within `ToastProvider` (~line 140)
**Severity:** MEDIUM

**Problem:** `addToast` schedules a `setTimeout` to auto-dismiss each toast, but these timeout IDs are not tracked or cleaned up. If `ToastProvider` unmounts (e.g., during a hot module reload in development, or if wrapped conditionally), the timeout fires and calls `setToasts` on an unmounted component, causing a React warning. More practically, in development with HMR this will fire on every save.

**Fix:**
```jsx
// whispering-wishes-replit/src/appcore-providers.jsx — replace ToastProvider

const ToastProvider = ({ children }) => {
  const [toasts, setToasts] = useState([]);
  const timerMapRef = useRef(new Map());
  
  // Clean up all timers on unmount
  useEffect(() => {
    return () => {
      for (const timerId of timerMapRef.current.values()) {
        clearTimeout(timerId);
      }
      timerMapRef.current.clear();
    };
  }, []);
  
  const addToast = useCallback((message, type = 'info', duration = 3000) => {
    const id = generateUniqueId();
    setToasts(prev => [...prev, { id, message, type }]);
    
    const timerId = setTimeout(() => {
      setToasts(prev => prev.filter(t => t.id !== id));
      timerMapRef.current.delete(id);
    }, duration);
    timerMapRef.current.set(id, timerId);
    
    if (type === 'success') haptic.success();
    else if (type === 'error') haptic.error();
    else if (type === 'warning') haptic.warning();
    else haptic.light();
  }, []);
  
  const contextValue = useMemo(() => ({ addToast }), [addToast]);
  
  return (
    <ToastContext.Provider value={contextValue}>
      {children}
      <div className="fixed bottom-24 left-3 right-3 z-[9998] flex flex-col gap-2 pointer-events-none" role="status" aria-live="polite" aria-atomic="true">
        {toasts.map(toast => (
          <div key={toast.id} className="px-4 py-3 rounded-lg flex items-center gap-2 text-xs font-medium pointer-events-auto text-white border border-white/20" style={{
            animation: 'slideUp 0.2s ease-out',
            background: toast.type === 'success' ? 'rgba(16,185,129,0.9)' : toast.type === 'error' ? 'rgba(239,68,68,0.9)' : toast.type === 'warning' ? 'rgba(245,158,11,0.9)' : 'rgba(59,130,246,0.9)',
          }}>
            {toast.type === 'success' && <CheckCircle size={16} />}
            {toast.type === 'error' && <AlertCircle size={16} />}
            {toast.type === 'warning' && <AlertTriangle size={16} />}
            {toast.type === 'info' && <Info size={16} />}
            {toast.message}
          </div>
        ))}
      </div>
    </ToastContext.Provider>
  );
};
```

## ISSUE PP-13: `PWAProvider` Injects Meta Tags via DOM Manipulation — Duplicates Existing HTML Meta Tags

**File:** `whispering-wishes-replit/src/appcore-providers.jsx`, lines within PWAProvider useEffect + `whispering-wishes-replit/index.html`, lines 5-8
**Severity:** MEDIUM

**Problem:** `index.html` already has `<meta name="viewport">`, `<meta name="theme-color">`, and `<meta name="apple-mobile-web-app-capable">`. The `PWAProvider` then injects duplicates via JavaScript, guarded by `if (!document.querySelector(\`meta[name="${name}"]\`))`. BUT the check succeeds for tags already in the HTML, so it doesn't inject duplicates. However, the cleanup function removes ALL matching meta tags, including the ones from the static HTML:

```js
// Cleanup:
const el = document.querySelector(`meta[name="${name}"][data-ww="true"]`);
if (el) el.remove();
```

This is correctly scoped by `[data-ww="true"]`, so it only removes the JS-injected ones. But the entire meta-tag injection block is dead code for tags already in the HTML — the `if (!document.querySelector(...))` check means they're never created, so they're never cleaned up. This is ~20 lines of code that do nothing.

**Fix — remove already-present tags from the meta tags array, or better, remove the overlapping tags from `index.html` to have one source of truth:**
```js
// whispering-wishes-replit/src/appcore-providers.jsx — in PWAProvider useEffect
// Only inject meta tags that aren't already in the static HTML
const metaTags = [
  // viewport is in index.html — skip
  { name: 'mobile-web-app-capable', content: 'yes' },
  // apple-mobile-web-app-capable is in index.html — skip
  { name: 'apple-mobile-web-app-status-bar-style', content: 'black-translucent' },
  { name: 'apple-mobile-web-app-title', content: 'Whispering Wishes' },
  // theme-color is in index.html — skip
  { name: 'msapplication-TileColor', content: '#edaf18' },
  { name: 'msapplication-navbutton-color', content: '#edaf18' },
];
```

## NEW ISSUE 1: Service Worker `staleWhileRevalidate` Leaks Background Fetch Promises — Potential Memory Pressure

**File:** `whispering-wishes-replit/public/sw.js`, lines 68–80
**Severity:** MEDIUM

**Problem:** The `staleWhileRevalidate` function fires a background `fetch` on *every* cache hit. The `fetchPromise` is created unconditionally, but when `cached` exists, the promise is orphaned — it runs to completion in the background with no error boundary visible to the caller. If the fetch fails *and* no cached version exists, the catch handler returns `cached` (which is `undefined` at that point), then falls through to construct a `Response` — but this is dead logic because the outer `return cached || fetchPromise` already returned `fetchPromise` in the no-cache case.

More critically: `trimCache` is called inside the `.then()` of the fetch promise, meaning *every single image request that has a cache hit* triggers a full cache key enumeration in the background. For a page with 50+ character images, that's 50 concurrent cache scans.

**Fix — debounce trim, and don't fire background revalidation for recently-cached items:**

```js
// Strategy: Stale-while-revalidate (for images)
// Debounced trim to avoid 50+ concurrent cache scans on image-heavy pages
let _trimScheduled = false;

async function staleWhileRevalidate(request, cacheName) {
  const cache = await caches.open(cacheName);
  const cached = await cache.match(request);

  const fetchPromise = fetch(request).then(response => {
    if (response.ok) {
      cache.put(request, response.clone());
      // Debounce trim: schedule once, not per-request
      if (!_trimScheduled) {
        _trimScheduled = true;
        setTimeout(async () => {
          _trimScheduled = false;
          await trimCache(cacheName, MAX_IMG_ENTRIES);
        }, 5000);
      }
    }
    return response;
  }).catch(() => {
    // If we had a cached version, the caller already got it.
    // If not, return a 503 so the caller knows it failed.
    return cached || new Response('', { status: 503, statusText: 'Service Unavailable' });
  });

  return cached || fetchPromise;
}
```

**Impact:** On a collection page showing 50+ characters, this eliminates ~50 redundant synchronous cache key enumerations, reducing main thread contention on the SW thread.

## NEW ISSUE 2: Service Worker `networkFirst` Caches Navigation Responses Without Cache-Control Respect

**File:** `whispering-wishes-replit/public/sw.js`, lines 83–97
**Severity:** MEDIUM

**Problem:** `networkFirst` caches *every* successful GET response including the app shell HTML. For a Vite-built SPA with content-hashed assets, the `index.html` should use network-first (correct), but the cache-put doesn't set any expiry. If the user goes offline after a successful fetch, they'll get the cached version forever — even months later when the app has been updated. There's no mechanism to invalidate these entries apart from the full cache purge on version bump.

More importantly, Vite injects versioned script tags into `index.html` (e.g., `/assets/index-abc123.js`). If the cached `index.html` references old hashes but the old JS files have been purged from the CDN, the user gets a broken page.

**Fix — add `Cache-Control` header awareness and a max-age for app shell entries:**

```js
// Strategy: Network-first with cache fallback (for app/API)
async function networkFirst(request, cacheName) {
  try {
    const response = await fetch(request);
    if (response.ok) {
      const cache = await caches.open(cacheName);
      // Clone before caching
      cache.put(request, response.clone());
    }
    return response;
  } catch {
    const cached = await caches.match(request);
    if (cached) {
      // For navigation requests, check if cached response is too old (>24h)
      // If so, still return it (better than nothing) but log a warning
      const dateHeader = cached.headers.get('date');
      if (request.mode === 'navigate' && dateHeader) {
        const age = Date.now() - new Date(dateHeader).getTime();
        if (age > 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000) {
          console.warn('[SW] Serving stale app shell (>24h old). User should reconnect.');
        }
      }
      return cached;
    }
    if (request.mode === 'navigate') {
      // Fall back to cached index.html for SPA routing
      return caches.match('/') || new Response('Offline', { status: 503 });
    }
    return new Response('Offline', { status: 503 });
  }
}
```

**Impact:** Prevents users from being stuck on stale app shells indefinitely when offline.

## NEW ISSUE 3: Service Worker `cacheFirst` Returns Empty 503 Body — Breaks Image Fallback Logic

**File:** `whispering-wishes-replit/public/sw.js`, lines 56–66
**Severity:** LOW

**Problem:** When a CDN fetch fails, `cacheFirst` returns `new Response('', { status: 503 })`. This is an opaque response with no `statusText`, which means `response.ok` is `false` but there's no useful information for debugging. More importantly, if this response is for a CSS or font file from a CDN (cdnjs, Google Fonts), the calling page receives a 503 with an empty body, which will silently break styles/fonts with no visible error to the user.

**Fix — return a more descriptive error response:**

```js
// Strategy: Cache-first (for CDN assets)
async function cacheFirst(request, cacheName) {
  const cached = await caches.match(request);
  if (cached) return cached;
  try {
    const response = await fetch(request);
    if (response.ok) {
      const cache = await caches.open(cacheName);
      cache.put(request, response.clone());
    }
    return response;
  } catch (err) {
    return new Response('', {
      status: 503,
      statusText: 'CDN Unavailable',
      headers: { 'X-SW-Error': err.message || 'fetch failed' }
    });
  }
}
```

## NEW ISSUE 4: `trimCache` Deletes From the Start (Oldest by Insertion) But Cache API Doesn't Guarantee Insertion Order

**File:** `whispering-wishes-replit/public/sw.js`, lines 47–52
**Severity:** LOW

**Problem:** `cache.keys()` returns requests in the order they were added. The code deletes `keys.slice(0, keys.length - maxEntries)` to keep the newest entries. However, `staleWhileRevalidate` *re-puts* entries when revalidating — which moves them to the end of the insertion list. This means frequently-accessed images float to the end (kept) while rarely-accessed ones drift to the start (evicted). This is actually good LRU-like behavior by accident. **No fix needed, but the comment should reflect this.**

**Fix — documentation only:**

```js
// Trim image cache to MAX_IMG_ENTRIES.
// cache.keys() returns insertion order; staleWhileRevalidate re-puts on
// revalidation, giving pseudo-LRU behavior (frequently accessed = newest).
async function trimCache(cacheName, maxEntries) {
  const cache = await caches.open(cacheName);
  const keys = await cache.keys();
  if (keys.length > maxEntries) {
    await Promise.all(keys.slice(0, keys.length - maxEntries).map(k => cache.delete(k)));
  }
}
```

## NEW ISSUE 5: Agent `_sourceCache` Never Cleared — Stale Data Across Task Boundaries

**File:** `agent/index.js`, lines ~159–164
**Severity:** MEDIUM

**Problem:** The `_sourceCache` Map caches fetched web sources within a run. This is explicitly intentional ("Cache fetched sources within a single run to avoid duplicate requests"). However, the cache key is `sourceKey` (e.g., `'banners'`, `'events'`), not the URL. If a task modifies state that would change which URLs are fetched (e.g., new character added → new build sources needed), subsequent tasks within the same run use stale data.

More concretely: `doRoster()` fetches `'builds'` sources. Later, `doEnrich()` also fetches `'builds'` sources. If `doRoster` added a new character, `doEnrich` should see updated context — but because the cache returns the same HTML pages, this is actually fine since the pages themselves haven't changed during the run. **The cache is correct for web scraping dedup.**

However, the cache persists across the entire `main()` scope. If `main()` were ever called twice in the same process (e.g., a test harness), it would serve stale data. **Low risk but easy to fix:**

```js
// Cache fetched sources within a single run to avoid duplicate requests.
// Cleared at the start of main() to ensure freshness in test/multi-run scenarios.
const _sourceCache = new Map();

async function fetchCached(sourceKey) {
  if (_sourceCache.has(sourceKey)) return _sourceCache.get(sourceKey);
  const results = await fetchAll(SOURCES[sourceKey]);
  const ok = results.filter(s => s.ok);
  _sourceCache.set(sourceKey, ok);
  return ok;
}
```

And at the top of `main()`, add:

```js
async function main() {
  log.section(`WW UPDATE AGENT v2 [${MODE.toUpperCase()}]`);
  log.info(`Mode: ${MODE} | Dry run: ${DRY_RUN} | Only: ${ONLY || 'all'}`);
  
  // Clear source cache in case of multi-run scenarios
  _sourceCache.clear();
  
  // ... rest of main()
```

**File:** `agent/index.js`, lines ~104–118
**Severity:** LOW

**Problem:** `fullCycle` runs all tasks sequentially with `await`. Several tasks are independent — e.g., `doEvents()` and `doRoster()` don't depend on each other's results. Running them in parallel would reduce total wall-clock time. However, this is correctly sequential because:
1. They share the source buffer (global mutable state)
2. They share the Claude API rate limit
3. The checkpoint system assumes sequential execution

**Verdict:** Sequential is correct for this architecture. **No fix needed.** A future optimization would be to parallelize the *fetch* phase (web scraping) while keeping the *apply* phase sequential, but that's a structural change beyond this pass.

## NEW ISSUE 7: `validate.js` String-Based Brace Counter Doesn't Handle Template Literals Correctly

**File:** `agent/lib/validate.js`, lines ~88–112
**Severity:** HIGH

**Problem:** The `checkSyntax` function tracks string state with `inString` and `stringChar`. When it encounters a backtick, it treats everything until the next unescaped backtick as "inside a string" — but template literals can contain `${...}` expressions which themselves contain braces, brackets, and even nested template literals. The counter will *exit* the string state at the closing backtick of the expression `${...}`, then count all subsequent template text as code.

Example:
```js
const x = `Hello ${world}!`;
//         ^               ^
//         enters string    exits at ${... } — WRONG, counter sees }! as code
```

This means the brace counter produces false positives on any file using template literals with expressions — which includes `appcore-data.js` (all the `'${name}...'` URL patterns), `appcore-components.jsx` (JSX template strings), and agent code.

The `shell-swap.js` function `checkBalanced` has the identical bug.

**Fix for `agent/lib/validate.js`:**

```js
/**
 * Basic syntax checks — look for common JS problems.
 * NOTE: Template literal expressions (${...}) are handled by tracking nesting depth.
 */
function checkSyntax(source, errors) {
  let braces = 0, brackets = 0, parens = 0;
  let inString = false, stringChar = '';
  let templateDepth = 0; // Track nested template literal depth

  for (let i = 0; i < source.length; i++) {
    const c = source[i];
    const prev = i > 0 ? source[i - 1] : '';

    // Inside a regular string (' or ")
    if (inString && stringChar !== '`') {
      if (c === stringChar && prev !== '\\') inString = false;
      continue;
    }

    // Inside a template literal
    if (inString && stringChar === '`') {
      if (c === '`' && prev !== '\\') {
        inString = false;
        stringChar = '';
        continue;
      }
      // Check for ${...} expression start
      if (c === '$' && i + 1 < source.length && source[i + 1] === '{') {
        templateDepth++;
        inString = false;
        stringChar = '';
        i++; // skip the '{'
        braces++; // count the opening brace from ${
        continue;
      }
      continue; // still inside template string text
    }

    // Not inside any string
    if (c === "'" || c === '"') {
      inString = true;
      stringChar = c;
      continue;
    }

    if (c === '`') {
      inString = true;
      stringChar = '`';
      continue;
    }

    if (c === '{') braces++;
    else if (c === '}') {
      braces--;
      // If we were in a template expression and braces match, re-enter template string
      if (templateDepth > 0 && braces >= 0) {
        // Check: is this the closing brace of a template expression?
        // We track this via templateDepth — when a } brings us back to the
        // depth where we entered the expression, we re-enter the template.
        // This simplified approach works for non-nested templates.
        // For full correctness, we'd need a stack. This handles 95%+ of real code.
        templateDepth--;
        inString = true;
        stringChar = '`';
      }
    }
    else if (c === '[') brackets++;
    else if (c === ']') brackets--;
    else if (c === '(') parens++;
    else if (c === ')') parens--;
  }

  if (braces !== 0) errors.push(`Unbalanced braces: ${braces > 0 ? braces + ' unclosed' : Math.abs(braces) + ' extra closing'}`);
  if (brackets !== 0) errors.push(`Unbalanced brackets: ${brackets > 0 ? brackets + ' unclosed' : Math.abs(brackets) + ' extra closing'}`);
  if (parens !== 0) errors.push(`Unbalanced parentheses: ${parens > 0 ? parens + ' unclosed' : Math.abs(parens) + ' extra closing'}`);
}
```

**Impact:** Without this fix, the validator produces false syntax errors on files with template literal expressions, which could cause the agent to reject valid patches or fail validation on legitimate code updates. The `shell-swap.js` `checkBalanced` function and the `evolution.js` `checkBraces` function have the same bug and need the same fix (see Issue 8).

**Severity:** HIGH

Since they are in three different files and serve different purposes (evolution self-test, shell-swap validation, data validation), they should all be fixed.

```js

 * Handles template literal expressions (${...}).
 */

  let braces = 0, brackets = 0, parens = 0;
  let inString = false, stringChar = '';
  let templateDepth = 0;

    const c = source[i];

    if (inString && stringChar !== '`') {

      continue;
    }

      if (c === '`' && prev !== '\\') {
        inString = false;
        stringChar = '';
        continue;
      }
      if (c === '$' && i + 1 < source.length && source[i + 1] === '{') {
        templateDepth++;
        inString = false;
        stringChar = '';
        i++;
        braces++;
        continue;
      }
      continue;
    }

    if (c === "'" || c === '"') { inString = true; stringChar = c; continue; }
    if (c === '`') { inString = true; stringChar = '`'; continue; }

    if (c === '{') braces++;
    else if (c === '}') {

      if (templateDepth > 0) {

    }
    else if (c === '[') brackets++;
    else if (c === ']') brackets--;
```

```js
function checkBalanced(source) {
  let braces = 0, brackets = 0, parens = 0;
  let inString = false, stringChar = '';
  let templateDepth = 0;

  for (let i = 0; i < source.length; i++) {
    const c = source[i];
    const prev = i > 0 ? source[i - 1] : '';

    if (inString && stringChar !== '`') {
      if (c === stringChar && prev !== '\\') inString = false;
      continue;
    }

    if (inString && stringChar === '`') {
      if (c === '`' && prev !== '\\') {
        inString = false;
        stringChar = '';
        continue;
      }
      if (c === '$' && i + 1 < source.length && source[i + 1] === '{') {
        templateDepth++;
        inString = false;

        i++;
        braces++;
        continue;
      }
      continue;
    }

    if (c === "'" || c === '"') { inString = true; stringChar = c; continue; }
    if (c === '`') { inString = true; stringChar = '`'; continue; }

    if (c === '{') braces++;
    else if (c === '}') {
      braces--;
      if (templateDepth > 0) {
        templateDepth--;
        inString = true;
        stringChar = '`';
      }
    }
    else if (c === '[') brackets++;
    else if (c === ']') brackets--;
    else if (c === '(') parens++;
```

## NEW ISSUE 9: `multi-pass-audit.js` Section Splitter Regex Misses Most Real Section Headers

**File:** `agent/lib/multi-pass-audit.js`, lines ~99–106
**Severity:** MEDIUM

**Problem:** The `splitIntoSections` function looks for section markers matching:
```js
/\/\/\s*\[SECTION:([^\]]+)\]|\/\/\s*═{3,}\s*(.+?)\s*═{3,}|\/\/\s*-{3,}\s*(.+?)\s*-{3,}/i
```

Looking at the actual app code (`AppCore.jsx`, `appcore-data.js`, etc.), section headers typically look like:
```js
// ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
// WHISPERING WISHES v3.2.3 — appcore-data.js
// Pure data, constants, game databases. No React. Leaf module (no imports).
// ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
```

The regex requires the section *name* to be on the SAME LINE as the `═` characters, between them. But the real headers have the `═` line as a standalone line with the description on the *next* line. So the regex's second alternation `\/\/\s*═{3,}\s*(.+?)\s*═{3,}` requires text BETWEEN the `═` runs on a single line, which doesn't match the two-line header pattern.

It also misses patterns like:
```js
// --- appcore-data.js ---
```
because this *does* match the third alternation `\/\/\s*-{3,}\s*(.+?)\s*-{3,}`, but only if there are 3+ dashes on both sides.

**Fix — enhance the section detection regex to match real header patterns:**

```js
function splitIntoSections(content, fileName, maxChars) {
  const lines = content.split('\n');
  const sections = [];

  // Try to find section markers
  const sectionStarts = [];
  for (let i = 0; i < lines.length; i++) {
    const line = lines[i];
    
    // Pattern 1: // [SECTION:NAME]
    // Pattern 2: // ═══ SECTION NAME ═══ (name between decorators on same line)
    // Pattern 3: // --- section name --- 
    const sameLineMatch = line.match(
      /\/\/\s*\[SECTION:([^\]]+)\]|\/\/\s*═{3,}\s+(.+?)\s+═{3,}|\/\/\s*-{3,}\s+(.+?)\s+-{3,}/i
    );
    if (sameLineMatch) {
      const label = (sameLineMatch[1] || sameLineMatch[2] || sameLineMatch[3]).trim();
      sectionStarts.push({ line: i, label });
      continue;
    }

    // Pattern 4: Multi-line header — a line of pure ═══ followed by a description line
    // Matches the actual header style used in appcore-*.js files
    if (/^\/\/\s*═{10,}\s*$/.test(line) && i + 1 < lines.length) {
      const nextLine = lines[i + 1];
      const descMatch = nextLine.match(/^\/\/\s*(.+)/);
      if (descMatch) {
        const label = descMatch[1].replace(/^[═\-\s]+|[═\-\s]+$/g, '').trim();
        if (label.length > 3 && label.length < 120) {
          sectionStarts.push({ line: i, label });
        }
      }
    }

    // Pattern 5: Large export blocks (export const X_DATA = {)
    const exportMatch = line.match(/^export\s+const\s+([A-Z][A-Z_0-9]+)\s*=/);
    if (exportMatch) {
      sectionStarts.push({ line: i, label: exportMatch[1] });
    }
  }

  // ... rest of function unchanged
```

**Impact:** Without this fix, the multi-pass audit falls back to `splitByLineCount` for every app source file, producing arbitrarily-split chunks that cut through the middle of functions and objects. This makes Claude's audit less accurate because it sees broken code at chunk boundaries.

## NEW ISSUE 11: `AppCore.jsx` Barrel File Has No Tree-Shaking Benefit Due to Named Re-exports

**File:** `whispering-wishes-replit/src/AppCore.jsx`, entire file
**Severity:** LOW

**Problem:** `AppCore.jsx` is a barrel/re-export file. Every export from the four sub-modules is explicitly listed. This is correct and does NOT prevent tree-shaking (contrary to a common misconception — named re-exports are tree-shakeable). However, the issue is that `App.jsx` imports from `AppCore.jsx`, which means Vite must resolve all four sub-modules at bundle time even if only a subset is used.

The real performance concern: this file uses the `.jsx` extension but contains zero JSX. The Vite build will run the React transform on it unnecessarily.

**Fix — rename to `AppCore.js` (no JSX transform needed):**

This is a trivial file rename. However, since `App.jsx` imports from `'./AppCore.jsx'` (or possibly without extension), the import path in `App.jsx` would need to be updated if it uses the explicit `.jsx` extension. With Vite's default resolution, omitting the extension works:

```js
// In App.jsx, ensure the import is:
import { ... } from './AppCore';
// (without .jsx extension — Vite resolves both .js and .jsx)
```

**Impact:** Saves ~1ms of build time. Negligible in practice. Mentioning for code hygiene only.

## NEW ISSUE 12: Agent Evolution Prompt Sends 12K Per File But Truncation Logic Is Wrong

**File:** `agent/lib/evolution.js`, lines ~181–188
**Severity:** MEDIUM

**Problem:**
```js
const content = info.content.length > 12000
  ? info.content.slice(0, 6000) + `\n\n// [...${info.lines - 200} lines omitted...]\n\n` + info.content.slice(-6000)
  : info.content;
```

The `info.lines - 200` calculation is wrong. It subtracts a hardcoded `200` assuming 6000 chars ≈ 100 lines on each side. But the actual lines-per-6000-chars varies wildly — dense config files might have 150+ lines per 6K, while sparse code has ~80. The displayed omission count is inaccurate, which misleads Claude about how much code it's missing.

**Fix:**

```js
const content = info.content.length > 12000
  ? (() => {
      const head = info.content.slice(0, 6000);
      const tail = info.content.slice(-6000);
      const headLines = head.split('\n').length;
      const tailLines = tail.split('\n').length;
      const omittedLines = info.lines - headLines - tailLines;
      return head + `\n\n// [...${Math.max(0, omittedLines)} lines omitted...]\n\n` + tail;
    })()
  : info.content;
```
