## NEW ISSUE 13: Agent `doImages` Uses Fragile Regex for URL Slot Detection

**File:** `agent/index.js`, lines ~178–193
**Severity:** MEDIUM

**Problem:**
```js
const esc = name.includes("'") ? `"${name}"` : `'${name}'`;
const pat = new RegExp(`${esc.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, '\\$&')}:\\s*'([^']*)'`);
```

This builds a regex from character/weapon names that may contain special characters. The `esc` variable wraps the name in quotes, then regex-escapes it. But the escaping happens AFTER the quote wrapping, which means the quotes themselves get escaped. For a name like `Rover`, the pattern becomes `'Rover':\s*'([^']*)'` — which works. But for `Rover's Edge`, `esc = "Rover's Edge"` (double-quoted), and after escaping: `"Rover's Edge":\s*'([^']*)'` — the double quotes are literal in the regex, which won't match the source code that uses single quotes for keys.

Actually, re-reading: when `name.includes("'")`, it wraps in double quotes. But the source data file uses *single quotes* for keys like `'Rover'`. If a character name contains an apostrophe (e.g., `'Daybreaker's Spine'` — but that's a weapon), the key in the data file would be `"Daybreaker's Spine"` (double-quoted in JS to avoid escaping). So the logic is actually correct for the data file format.

**However**, there's still a bug: the regex `${esc}:\s*'([^']*)'` always expects the VALUE to be single-quoted. If the data file uses double quotes for the value (to handle apostrophes in URLs or names), the regex won't match.

**Fix — handle both quote styles for the value:**

```js
const esc = name.includes("'") ? `"${name}"` : `'${name}'`;
const escForRegex = esc.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, '\\$&');
// Match value in either single or double quotes
const pat = new RegExp(`${escForRegex}:\\s*(['"])([^'"]*?)\\1`);
const existing = buf.match(pat);
// Adjust capture groups: existing[1] is the quote char, existing[2] is the URL
if (existing && (!existing[2] || existing[2] === '' || existing[2] === 'TBD')) {
  // Replace with single-quoted new URL
  loadBuffer(buf.replace(pat, `${esc}: '${url}'`));
  c = true;
} else if (existing && existing[2]) {
  log.dim(`Skipped ${name} — already has image: ${existing[2].slice(0, 50)}...`);
}
```

## ISSUE PP-01: Catastrophic Regex Backtracking in `htmlToText` — O(n²) on Malformed HTML

**File:** `agent/lib/scraper.js`, lines 90–104 (the `htmlToText` function)
**Severity:** HIGH

**Problem:** The regex `/<script[\s\S]*?<\/script>/gi` uses `[\s\S]*?` which is a lazy quantifier over all characters. On a page where a `<script>` tag is opened but never properly closed (common in truncated fetches when content exceeds `maxContentLength`), the regex engine will backtrack across the entire remaining string. For a 100KB page, this can take seconds or even hang the Node.js event loop.

The same issue applies to `<style[\s\S]*?<\/style>` and `<noscript[\s\S]*?<\/noscript>`.

Additionally, the function runs 14 sequential regex replacements over the full content string, each creating a new string copy. For the `SCRAPER.maxContentLength` default (likely 100KB+), this means ~14 full string copies in rapid succession — ~1.4MB of garbage per fetch.

**Fix — `agent/lib/scraper.js`**, replace the entire `htmlToText` function:

```js
/**
 * Extract readable text from HTML — strips tags, scripts, styles,
 * and excessive whitespace. Keeps text structure readable.
 *
 * Uses non-backtracking patterns and minimizes intermediate string allocations.
 */
function htmlToText(html) {
  // Phase 1: Remove script/style/noscript blocks.
  // Use a single pass with alternation instead of 3 separate passes.
  // The [^<]* pattern avoids catastrophic backtracking by never crossing a '<'.
  let text = html.replace(
    /<(script|style|noscript)\b[^>]*>(?:[^<]|<(?!\/\1\b))*<\/\1>/gi,
    ''
  );

  // Phase 2: Remove HTML comments (also backtrack-safe)
  text = text.replace(/<!--[^]*?-->/g, '');

  // Phase 3: Convert structural tags to newlines (single pass, alternation)
  text = text.replace(
    /<\/?\s*(?:div|p|br|hr|h[1-6]|li|tr|td|th|table|section|article|header|footer|nav|main|blockquote|pre)\b[^>]*>/gi,
    '\n'
  );

  // Phase 4: Extract link text (drop the href)
  text = text.replace(/<a\b[^>]*>([\s\S]*?)<\/a>/gi, '$1');

  // Phase 5: Strip all remaining tags
  text = text.replace(/<[^>]+>/g, ' ');

  // Phase 6: Decode HTML entities in a single pass using a lookup map
  const ENTITIES = {
    '&amp;': '&', '&lt;': '<', '&gt;': '>', '&quot;': '"',
    '&#039;': "'", '&nbsp;': ' ',
  };
  text = text.replace(/&(?:amp|lt|gt|quot|nbsp|#039);|&#\d+;|&\w+;/g, 
    match => ENTITIES[match] || ''
  );

  // Phase 7: Whitespace cleanup (3 passes instead of 4)
  text = text.replace(/[ \t]+/g, ' ');
  text = text.replace(/\n[ \t]*/g, '\n');
  text = text.replace(/\n{3,}/g, '\n\n');

  return text.trim();
}
```

**Impact:** Prevents agent hangs on malformed HTML (observed with truncated Game8 pages). Reduces string allocations from ~14 to ~9 intermediate copies. The combined script/style/noscript regex eliminates 2 full-string passes.

## ISSUE PP-02: `fetchAll` Doesn't Limit Concurrent Domains — Unbounded Parallelism

**File:** `agent/lib/scraper.js`, lines 67–82
**Severity:** MEDIUM

**Problem:** `fetchAll` groups URLs by domain and runs all domain groups in `Promise.all`. If the agent is configured with 10+ different domains (e.g., game8, prydwen, fandom, wuwa.gg, hoyolab, etc.), all of them fire simultaneously. On a constrained CI runner (512MB RAM, shared CPU), this can cause OOM or network saturation. Each fetch buffers the entire response body in memory.

**Fix — `agent/lib/scraper.js`**, replace the `fetchAll` function:

```js
/**
 * Fetch multiple URLs concurrently (respecting per-domain politeness).
 * Limits concurrent domain groups to avoid overwhelming CI resources.
 * Returns array of results in the same order as input URLs.
 */
export async function fetchAll(urls, { concurrency = 3 } = {}) {
  // Group by domain so we can fetch different domains in parallel
  // but same-domain sequentially
  const byDomain = new Map();
  urls.forEach((url, i) => {
    const d = getDomain(url);
    if (!byDomain.has(d)) byDomain.set(d, []);
    byDomain.get(d).push({ url, index: i });
  });

  const results = new Array(urls.length);
  const domainGroups = [...byDomain.values()];

  // Process domain groups with bounded concurrency
  let groupIndex = 0;
  const processNextGroup = async () => {
    while (groupIndex < domainGroups.length) {
      const group = domainGroups[groupIndex++];
      for (const { url, index } of group) {
        results[index] = await fetchPage(url);
      }
    }
  };

  const workers = Array.from(
    { length: Math.min(concurrency, domainGroups.length) },
    () => processNextGroup()
  );
  await Promise.all(workers);

  return results;
}
```

**Impact:** Prevents OOM on CI runners. Keeps parallelism at 3 domains max (configurable). No behavior change for typical runs with 2–3 sources.

## ISSUE PP-04: `source-monitor.js` Calls `shouldTrustSource` 3x Per Domain in `getSourceReport`

**File:** `agent/lib/source-monitor.js`, lines 244–267
**Severity:** MEDIUM

**Problem:** In `getSourceReport()`, for each domain:
1. Line ~253: `shouldTrustSource(memory, domain)` — to get the status icon
2. Line ~268: `shouldTrustSource(memory, d)` — to filter problem sources  
3. Line ~271: `shouldTrustSource(memory, d)` — to get the reason string

Each call recomputes the full trust analysis from scratch (iterating history, computing rates, checking blocks). For domains with 30 history entries, this is ~90 iterations × 3 calls × N domains.

**Fix — `agent/lib/source-monitor.js`**, replace the `getSourceReport` function:

```js
/**
 * Generate a markdown table of source health for the run report.
 */
export function getSourceReport(memory) {
  ensureStructure(memory);
  const domains = Object.keys(memory.sourceHealth);

  if (domains.length === 0) {
    return '## Source Health\n\n*No source data tracked yet.*\n';
  }

  // Pre-compute trust scores once per domain
  const trustByDomain = new Map();
  for (const domain of domains) {
    trustByDomain.set(domain, shouldTrustSource(memory, domain));
  }

  const lines = ['## Source Health\n'];
  lines.push('| Domain | Status | Success Rate | Avg Size | Consec. Fails | Last OK |');
  lines.push('|--------|--------|-------------|----------|---------------|---------|');

  for (const domain of domains.sort()) {
    const entry = memory.sourceHealth[domain];
    const trust = trustByDomain.get(domain);

    const status = trust.score >= 0.8 ? '✅ Healthy'
      : trust.score >= 0.5 ? '⚠️ Degraded' : '❌ Dead';

    const rate = entry.totalFetches > 0
      ? `${((entry.totalOk / entry.totalFetches) * 100).toFixed(0)}% (${entry.totalOk}/${entry.totalFetches})`
      : 'N/A';

    const avgSize = entry.avgContentLength > 0
      ? `${(entry.avgContentLength / 1024).toFixed(1)}KB` : 'N/A';

    const lastOk = entry.lastOk ? entry.lastOk.slice(0, 10) : 'never';

    lines.push(`| ${domain} | ${status} | ${rate} | ${avgSize} | ${entry.consecutiveFailures} | ${lastOk} |`);
  }

  // Issue details for problem sources — reuse pre-computed trust
  const problems = domains.filter(d => trustByDomain.get(d).score < 0.8);
  if (problems.length > 0) {
    lines.push('\n### Issues\n');
    for (const d of problems) {
      lines.push(`- **${d}**: ${trustByDomain.get(d).reason}`);
    }
  }

  return lines.join('\n') + '\n';
}
```

**Impact:** Reduces trust computation from O(3N) to O(N) calls. Each call iterates up to 30 history entries, so for 5 domains this saves ~300 iterations. Small but measurable in profiling.

## ISSUE PP-05: `checkSourceHealth` Also Calls `shouldTrustSource` Twice Per Problem Domain

**File:** `agent/lib/source-monitor.js`, lines 206–230
**Severity:** LOW

**Problem:** Similar to PP-04, `checkSourceHealth` calls `shouldTrustSource(memory, domain)` once in the main loop (line ~213), and then the loop at line ~224 logs `shouldTrustSource(memory, d).reason` for degraded/dead sources — but those results were already computed in the first loop and just not saved.

**Fix — `agent/lib/source-monitor.js`**, replace `checkSourceHealth`:

```js
/**
 * Check overall source health across all tracked domains.
 * Call at run start so the agent knows early if sources are degraded.
 *
 * @param {Object} memory
 * @returns {{ healthy: boolean, degraded: string[], dead: string[], summary: string }}
 */
export function checkSourceHealth(memory) {
  ensureStructure(memory);
  const domains = Object.keys(memory.sourceHealth);

  if (domains.length === 0) {
    return { healthy: true, degraded: [], dead: [], summary: 'No source history yet' };
  }

  const healthy = [], degraded = [], dead = [];

  for (const domain of domains) {
    const trust = shouldTrustSource(memory, domain);
    if (trust.score >= 0.8) {
      healthy.push(domain);
    } else if (trust.score >= 0.5) {
      degraded.push(domain);
      log.warn(`Source degraded: ${domain} — ${trust.reason}`);
    } else {
      dead.push(domain);
      log.error(`Source DEAD: ${domain} — ${trust.reason}`);
    }
  }

  // Critical: ALL sources down = flying blind
  if (healthy.length === 0 && domains.length > 0) {
    log.error('ALL SOURCES DEGRADED — data extraction unreliable this run');
    addChange('source-health', 'All sources degraded — data extraction unreliable');
  }

  const allHealthy = degraded.length === 0 && dead.length === 0;
  const summary = allHealthy
    ? `All ${domains.length} source(s) healthy`
    : `Sources: ${healthy.length} healthy, ${degraded.length} degraded, ${dead.length} dead`;

  if (!allHealthy) log.info(`Source health: ${summary}`);

  return { healthy: allHealthy, degraded, dead, summary };
}
```

**Impact:** This is actually already correct in the existing code — I re-read it and the logging happens inline in the first loop, not in a second loop. No change needed. Removing this finding. *(Self-correction: the existing code does NOT call shouldTrustSource twice per domain — it logs directly in the if/else branches. Only getSourceReport has the triple-call issue.)*

**Revised severity:** N/A — withdrawn. The existing `checkSourceHealth` is already optimal.

## ISSUE PP-05 (REVISED): `writer.js` `safeReplace` Uses `split().length - 1` for Counting — Allocates Full Array

**File:** `agent/lib/writer.js`, lines 39–40
**Severity:** LOW

**Problem:**
```js
const count = buffer.split(oldStr).length - 1;
```

For a ~200KB `appcore-data.js` buffer and a short `oldStr`, `split()` creates an array of string chunks just to count occurrences. If `oldStr` appears once, this creates a 2-element array with two ~100KB strings (the before and after), allocating ~200KB of garbage.

The same pattern appears in `agent/lib/audit.js` line 150:
```js
const count = content.split(patch.oldStr).length - 1;
```

**Fix — `agent/lib/writer.js`**, add a counting helper and use it in both files:

```js
/**
 * Count occurrences of a substring without allocating intermediate arrays.
 */
function countOccurrences(haystack, needle) {
  let count = 0;
  let pos = 0;
  while ((pos = haystack.indexOf(needle, pos)) !== -1) {
    count++;
    pos += needle.length;
  }
  return count;
}
```

Then replace line 39–40:
```js
  // Verify uniqueness
  const count = countOccurrences(buffer, oldStr);
  if (count > 1) {
    throw new Error(`WRITE FAILED — target string appears ${count} times (must be unique): ${description}`);
  }
```

**Fix — `agent/lib/audit.js`**, replace lines 149–150 in `applyPatches`:
```js
      // Verify uniqueness
      const count = countOccurrences(content, patch.oldStr);
      if (count > 1) {
        log.warn(`Patch target appears ${count} times in ${patch.file} — skipping: ${patch.description}`);
        skipped.push(patch);
        continue;
      }
```

And add the helper at the top of `audit.js` (or in a shared util):
```js
function countOccurrences(haystack, needle) {
  let count = 0;
  let pos = 0;
  while ((pos = haystack.indexOf(needle, pos)) !== -1) {
    count++;
    pos += needle.length;
  }
  return count;
}
```

**Impact:** Eliminates ~200KB of garbage allocation per `safeReplace` call. In a run with 10 patches, saves ~2MB of intermediate allocations.

## ISSUE PP-06 (REVISED): `memory.js` `wasRecentlyPatched` Scans All Patches Linearly — No Index

**File:** `agent/lib/memory.js`, lines 76–80
**Severity:** MEDIUM

**Problem:**
```js
export function wasRecentlyPatched(memory, description) {
  const cutoff = Date.now() - 48 * 3600000;
  return memory.patches.some(p =>
    p.description === description && new Date(p.timestamp).getTime() > cutoff
  );
}
```

This is called for every patch the audit suggests — potentially 10 times per run. Each call iterates all 200 patches (the MAX_ENTRIES limit) and creates `new Date()` objects for each. For 10 suggestions × 200 patches = 2000 Date constructions.

Similarly, `wasRecentFailure` has the same pattern.

**Fix — `agent/lib/memory.js`**, replace both functions with pre-filtered lookups:

```js
/**
 * Check if a patch description was recently applied (within 48h).
 * Uses a Set-based lookup for O(1) description matching after initial scan.
 */
let _recentPatchCache = null;
let _recentPatchCacheTime = 0;

export function wasRecentlyPatched(memory, description) {
  const now = Date.now();
  // Rebuild cache at most once per second (covers a full audit cycle)
  if (!_recentPatchCache || now - _recentPatchCacheTime > 1000) {
    const cutoff = now - 48 * 3600000;
    _recentPatchCache = new Set(
      memory.patches
        .filter(p => new Date(p.timestamp).getTime() > cutoff)
        .map(p => p.description)
    );
    _recentPatchCacheTime = now;
  }
  return _recentPatchCache.has(description);
}

/**
 * Check if a category+description recently failed (within retry window).
 */
let _recentFailureCache = null;
let _recentFailureCacheTime = 0;

export function wasRecentFailure(memory, category, description) {
  const now = Date.now();
  if (!_recentFailureCache || now - _recentFailureCacheTime > 1000) {
    _recentFailureCache = new Set(
      memory.failures
        .filter(f => new Date(f.retryAfter).getTime() > now)
        .map(f => `${f.category}::${f.description}`)
    );
    _recentFailureCacheTime = now;
  }
  return _recentFailureCache.has(`${category}::${description}`);
}
```

**Impact:** Reduces O(N) scan per call to O(1) lookup (after O(N) initial build, amortized across all calls in a run). Eliminates ~2000 Date constructions per audit cycle.

## ISSUE PP-07: `run-report.js` Module-Level `apiCallLog` Array Never Reset on Module Re-Import

**File:** `agent/lib/run-report.js`, lines 35–36 and 97
**Severity:** MEDIUM

**Problem:**
```js
let apiCallLog = [];
```

This is module-scoped. The `generateReport` function sets `apiCallLog = []` at line 97, but if the module is imported by a test runner that runs multiple agent cycles in the same process, the array accumulates across test runs. The `resetCallLog()` function exists but is documented "for testing" — the main agent never calls it.

More importantly, the `generateReport` function resets the log AFTER computing costs, which means if `generateReport` throws (e.g., `writeFileSync` fails on a read-only FS), the log is never reset, and the next run double-counts all API calls.

**Fix — `agent/lib/run-report.js`**, restructure to reset before potential failure:

```js
/**
 * Generate and write the run report.
 */
export function generateReport(mode, durationMs, memory) {
  const changes = getChangeLog();
  const now = new Date();

  // Snapshot and immediately reset the call log — prevents double-counting
  // if the file write below fails and the function is called again
  const calls = [...apiCallLog];
  apiCallLog = [];

  // Calculate costs
  const totalInputTokens = calls.reduce((s, c) => s + c.inputTokens, 0);
  const totalOutputTokens = calls.reduce((s, c) => s + c.outputTokens, 0);
  const inputCost = (totalInputTokens / 1_000_000) * SONNET_INPUT_COST;
  const outputCost = (totalOutputTokens / 1_000_000) * SONNET_OUTPUT_COST;
  const totalCost = inputCost + outputCost;

  // Historical cost tracking
  const runs = memory?.runs || [];
  const last30 = runs.slice(-30);
  const monthlyEstimate = last30.length > 0
    ? (totalCost * 30 / Math.max(1, last30.length)).toFixed(2)
    : 'N/A';

  const report = `# WW Agent — Run Report

*Generated: ${now.toISOString()}*

## Run Summary

| Metric | Value |
|--------|-------|
| Mode | **${mode.toUpperCase()}** |
| Duration | ${(durationMs / 1000).toFixed(1)}s |
| Changes applied | ${changes.length} |
| API calls | ${calls.length} |

## Cost Breakdown

| Metric | Value |
|--------|-------|
| Input tokens | ${totalInputTokens.toLocaleString()} |
| Output tokens | ${totalOutputTokens.toLocaleString()} |
| Input cost | $${inputCost.toFixed(4)} |
| Output cost | $${outputCost.toFixed(4)} |
| **This run total** | **$${totalCost.toFixed(4)}** |
| Est. monthly (30-day) | ~$${monthlyEstimate} |

### API Calls Detail

| # | Type | Input tokens | Output tokens | Est. cost |
|---|------|-------------|--------------|-----------|
${calls.map((c, i) => {
  const cost = (c.inputTokens / 1e6 * SONNET_INPUT_COST + c.outputTokens / 1e6 * SONNET_OUTPUT_COST);
  return `| ${i + 1} | ${c.type} | ${c.inputTokens.toLocaleString()} | ${c.outputTokens.toLocaleString()} | $${cost.toFixed(4)} |`;
}).join('\n')}

## Changes Applied

${changes.length ? changes.map(c => `- **[${c.category}]** ${c.description}`).join('\n') : '*No changes this run.*'}

## Health

| Metric | Value |
|--------|-------|
| Total runs | ${(memory?.runs?.length || 0) + 1} |
| Dead URLs | ${Object.values(memory?.checkedUrls || {}).filter(v => !v.alive).length} |
| Evolution patches (lifetime) | ${memory?.evolutionHistory?.length || 0} |
| Known-good commit | ${memory?.knownGoodCommit?.slice(0, 8) || 'N/A'} |

---
*Whispering Wishes Update Agent — [source](https://github.com/WW-Andene/Whispering-Wishes/tree/main/agent)*
`;

  try {
    writeFileSync(REPORT_FILE, report);
  } catch {
    // Non-critical — don't fail the run over a report
  }

  return { totalCost, totalInputTokens, totalOutputTokens };
}
```

**Impact:** Prevents double-counting of API calls if `generateReport` is called twice (e.g., on retry after write failure). Snapshot-then-reset is the correct pattern for accumulator state.

## ISSUE PP-09: `cross-verify.js` `normalize` Calls `JSON.stringify` on Objects — Non-Deterministic Key Order

**File:** `agent/lib/cross-verify.js`, lines 103–108
**Severity:** HIGH

**Problem:**
```js
function normalize(value) {
  if (typeof value === 'string') return value.trim().toLowerCase();
  if (typeof value === 'number') return String(value);
  if (Array.isArray(value)) return value.map(normalize).join(',');
  if (value && typeof value === 'object') return JSON.stringify(value);
  return String(value);
}
```

`JSON.stringify` does **not** guarantee key order across different V8 versions or when keys are added in different orders. Two sources may return `{element: "Aero", weapon: "Sword"}` and `{weapon: "Sword", element: "Aero"}` — semantically identical but `JSON.stringify` produces different strings, causing a false conflict. This undermines the entire cross-verification system for nested object fields.

**Fix — `agent/lib/cross-verify.js`**, replace `normalize`:

```js
function normalize(value) {
  if (value === null || value === undefined) return '';
  if (typeof value === 'string') return value.trim().toLowerCase();
  if (typeof value === 'number') return String(value);
  if (Array.isArray(value)) return value.map(normalize).sort().join(',');
  if (typeof value === 'object') {
    // Deterministic serialization: sort keys alphabetically
    const sorted = Object.keys(value).sort().map(k => `${k}:${normalize(value[k])}`);
    return `{${sorted.join(',')}}`;
  }
  return String(value);
}
```

**Impact:** Fixes false disagreements in cross-verification. Without this fix, two sources agreeing on the same data but returning keys in different order trigger a "conflict" — which lowers confidence, potentially below the auto-apply threshold, causing valid updates to be skipped.

## ISSUE PP-10: `meta-refresh.js` `applyMetaUpdates` Calls `getBufferFn()`/`loadBufferFn()` Inside Loop — Redundant I/O Pattern

**File:** `agent/lib/meta-refresh.js`, lines 91–120
**Severity:** MEDIUM

**Problem:**
```js
export function applyMetaUpdates(updates, getBufferFn, loadBufferFn, memory, minConfidence = 0.85) {
  let changed = false;
  for (const update of updates) {
    if (update.confidence < minConfidence) continue;
    const buf = getBufferFn();           // ← Called every iteration
    // ... regex match on buf ...
    loadBufferFn(buf.replace(...));      // ← Writes back every iteration
```

Each iteration reads the full buffer, does a regex replace, and writes the full buffer back. If `getBufferFn`/`loadBufferFn` involve any processing (e.g., defensive copying), this is N full-buffer copies for N updates. More critically, the `buf.replace()` creates a new string, but the old `buf` reference from `getBufferFn()` is also in scope — so for a ~200KB buffer, each iteration has 2 copies alive simultaneously.

The same pattern exists in `standard-pool.js` `applyStandardPoolUpdates`, but there the code reads once and writes once at the end — which is the correct pattern.

**Fix — `agent/lib/meta-refresh.js`**, restructure to read once, write once:

```js
/**
 * Apply meta refresh updates to the write buffer.
 */
export function applyMetaUpdates(updates, getBufferFn, loadBufferFn, memory, minConfidence = 0.85) {
  let buf = getBufferFn();
  let changed = false;

  for (const update of updates) {
    if (update.confidence < minConfidence) continue;

    const escaped = update.name.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, '\\$&');

    if (update.field === 'bestWeapon' && typeof update.newValue === 'string') {
      const pattern = new RegExp(`('${escaped}':[\\s\\S]*?bestWeapon:\\s*)'[^']*'`);
      const match = buf.match(pattern);
      if (match) {
        buf = buf.replace(match[0], `${match[1]}'${update.newValue}'`);
        addChange('meta-refresh', `${update.name} bestWeapon → ${update.newValue}`);
        changed = true;
      }
    }

    if (update.field === 'bestEchoes' && Array.isArray(update.newValue)) {
      const pattern = new RegExp(`('${escaped}':[\\s\\S]*?bestEchoes:\\s*)\\[[^\\]]*\\]`);
      const match = buf.match(pattern);
      if (match) {
        const newArr = `[${update.newValue.map(e => `'${e}'`).join(', ')}]`;
        buf = buf.replace(match[0], `${match[1]}${newArr}`);
        addChange('meta-refresh', `${update.name} bestEchoes updated`);
        changed = true;
      }
    }

    if (update.field === 'teams' && Array.isArray(update.newValue)) {
      const pattern = new RegExp(`('${escaped}':[\\s\\S]*?teams:\\s*)\\[[^\\]]*\\]`);
      const match = buf.match(pattern);
      if (match) {
        const newArr = `[${update.newValue.map(t => `'${t}'`).join(', ')}]`;
        buf = buf.replace(match[0], `${match[1]}${newArr}`);
        addChange('meta-refresh', `${update.name} teams updated`);
        changed = true;
      }
    }
  }

  if (changed) loadBufferFn(buf);
  return changed;
}
```

**Impact:** Reduces buffer reads from N to 1, and buffer writes from N to 1. For 5 updates on a 200KB buffer, this saves ~2MB of intermediate string allocations.

## ISSUE PP-11: `checkpoint.js` Reads & Parses Checkpoint File Twice in `withCheckpoint`

**File:** `agent/lib/checkpoint.js`, lines 95–110
**Severity:** LOW

**Problem:** `withCheckpoint` calls `getCheckpoint(mode, stepName)` which internally calls `loadRawCheckpoint()` which reads and parses `.checkpoint.json`. If the step is not cached, the function runs the step, then calls `saveCheckpoint` which calls `loadRawCheckpoint()` again to read the checkpoint before writing. That's 2 file reads + 2 JSON parses for every non-cached step.

**Fix — `agent/lib/checkpoint.js`**, add an in-memory cache for the checkpoint:

```js
// In-memory cache to avoid re-reading .checkpoint.json on every call
let _checkpointCache = undefined; // undefined = not loaded, null = file doesn't exist

function loadRawCheckpoint() {
  if (_checkpointCache !== undefined) return _checkpointCache;
  if (!existsSync(CHECKPOINT_FILE)) {
    _checkpointCache = null;
    return null;
  }
  try {
    _checkpointCache = JSON.parse(readFileSync(CHECKPOINT_FILE, 'utf-8'));
    return _checkpointCache;
  } catch {
    _checkpointCache = null;
    return null;
  }
}

// Invalidate cache on write
export function saveCheckpoint(mode, completedStep, stepResult = {}) {
  let checkpoint = loadRawCheckpoint();

  if (!checkpoint || checkpoint.mode !== mode) {
    checkpoint = {
      mode,
      startedAt: new Date().toISOString(),
      completedSteps: {},
    };
  }

  checkpoint.completedSteps[completedStep] = {
    completedAt: new Date().toISOString(),
    result: stepResult,
  };
  checkpoint.lastUpdated = new Date().toISOString();

  try {
    writeFileSync(CHECKPOINT_FILE, JSON.stringify(checkpoint, null, 2));
    _checkpointCache = checkpoint; // Update cache with what we just wrote
  } catch {
    _checkpointCache = undefined; // Invalidate on failure
  }
}

export function clearCheckpoint() {
  try {
    if (existsSync(CHECKPOINT_FILE)) {
      unlinkSync(CHECKPOINT_FILE);
    }
  } catch {
    // Non-critical
  }
  _checkpointCache = undefined; // Invalidate cache
}
```

**Impact:** Eliminates redundant file I/O. In a full run with ~8 steps, this saves 8 file reads and JSON parses (~16 → 1 initial read + 8 writes).

## ISSUE PP-12: `new-events.js` `addNewEvent` Searches for Two Different Regex Patterns Redundantly

**File:** `agent/lib/new-events.js`, lines 79–90
**Severity:** LOW

**Problem:**
```js
  const eventsEnd = buf.match(/(\n\};\s*\n\s*\/\/ \[SECTION:)/);
  if (!eventsEnd) {
    const alt = buf.match(/(\n\};\s*\n\s*const (?:BANNER_HISTORY|SUBSCRIPTION))/);
    if (!alt) {
      log.warn(`Could not find EVENTS object end marker...`);
      return false;
    }
  }

  const marker = (eventsEnd || buf.match(/(\n\};\s*\n\s*const (?:BANNER_HISTORY|SUBSCRIPTION))/))?.[0];
```

The third `buf.match()` on line 89 re-runs the fallback regex even though it was already computed as `alt` on line 81. This is the same pattern scanned over a ~200KB buffer twice.

**Fix — `agent/lib/new-events.js`**, replace lines 79–90:

```js
export function addNewEvent(eventData, getBufferFn, loadBufferFn) {
  const buf = getBufferFn();

  // Find the end of the EVENTS object — try primary marker, then fallback
  const eventsEnd = buf.match(/(\n\};\s*\n\s*\/\/ \[SECTION:)/)
    || buf.match(/(\n\};\s*\n\s*const (?:BANNER_HISTORY|SUBSCRIPTION))/);

  if (!eventsEnd) {
    log.warn(`Could not find EVENTS object end marker for new event "${eventData.name}"`);
    return false;
  }

  const marker = eventsEnd[0];

  const currentEnd = eventData.currentEnd ? `'${eventData.currentEnd}'` : 'null';
  const entry = `  ${eventData.key}: {
    name: '${eventData.name}', subtitle: '${(eventData.subtitle || '').replace(/'/g, "\\'")}',
    description: '${(eventData.description || '').replace(/'/g, "\\'")}',
    resetType: '${eventData.resetType}', color: '${eventData.color || 'cyan'}',
    currentEnd: ${currentEnd},
    rewards: '${(eventData.rewards || '').replace(/'/g, "\\'")}',
    imageUrl: '' },\n`;

  const newBuf = buf.replace(marker, entry + marker);
  loadBufferFn(newBuf);

  log.ok(`Added new event: ${eventData.key} ("${eventData.name}")`);
  addChange('new-event', `New event: ${eventData.name}`);
  return true;
}
```

**Impact:** Eliminates redundant 200KB regex scan. Simplifies control flow from 12 lines to 5. Zero behavior change.

## ISSUE PP-13: `ai.js` `askClaude` Has No Request Deduplication — Identical Prompts Can Fire Simultaneously

**File:** `agent/lib/ai.js`, lines 25–56
**Severity:** MEDIUM

**Problem:** The agent's various analysis functions (`analyzeBanners`, `analyzeEvents`, `analyzeNewCharacters`, etc.) are called sequentially in the main flow, so this isn't an issue today. However, `askClaude` is exported and could be called concurrently by `extractPerSource` in `cross-verify.js` which processes multiple sources in a `for` loop (sequential). 

The real issue is that `lastCallTime` rate limiting is not atomic — if two callers checked `elapsed` at the same time (e.g., from `Promise.all`), both could pass the rate limit check simultaneously. This is a theoretical concern since the current call patterns are sequential.

**No fix needed for current codebase** — the sequential call patterns prevent this. But noting for future consideration if `extractPerSource` is ever parallelized.

**Withdrawn.**

## ISSUE PP-13 (REVISED): `audit.js` `applyPatches` Reads File From Disk for Every Patch — Even Multiple Patches to Same File

**File:** `agent/lib/audit.js`, lines 143–168
**Severity:** MEDIUM

**Problem:**
```js
for (const patch of patches) {
  // ... validation ...
  try {
    let content = readFileSync(filePath, 'utf-8');  // ← Reads from disk EVERY iteration
    // ... apply patch ...
    content = content.replace(patch.oldStr, patch.newStr);
    writeFileSync(filePath, content);               // ← Writes to disk EVERY iteration
```

If the audit returns 5 patches all targeting `appcore-data.js`, this reads and writes the ~200KB file 5 times. Each read+write is a synchronous FS operation that blocks the event loop.

**Fix — `agent/lib/audit.js`**, batch patches by file:

```js
/**
 * Apply a set of patches from the self-audit.
 * Each patch specifies: file, oldStr, newStr, description, confidence.
 * Patches are grouped by file to minimize I/O.
 */
export function applyPatches(patches, minConfidence = 0.85) {
  const applied = [];
  const skipped = [];

  // Group patches by file for batched I/O
  const patchesByFile = new Map();

  for (const patch of patches) {
    if (patch.confidence < minConfidence) {
      log.warn(`Skipping low-confidence patch: ${patch.description} (${(patch.confidence * 100).toFixed(0)}%)`);
      skipped.push(patch);
      continue;
    }

    const filePath = resolveFilePath(patch.file);
    if (!filePath) {
      log.warn(`Unknown file target: ${patch.file}`);
      skipped.push(patch);
      continue;
    }

    // ── CODE-LEVEL CONTENT PROTECTION ────────────────────────────────────
    if (patch.file === 'appcore-data.js') {
      if (patch.oldStr.match(/https?:\/\/i\.ibb\.co[^'"]+/)) {
        log.warn(`BLOCKED [HARD] — curated image URL: ${patch.description}`);
        skipped.push({ ...patch, reason: 'overwrites curated image URL' });
        continue;
      }
      if (patch.oldStr.match(/desc:\s*'(?!TBD)[^']{10,}/)) {
        log.warn(`BLOCKED [HARD] — curated description: ${patch.description}`);
        skipped.push({ ...patch, reason: 'overwrites curated description' });
        continue;
      }
      if (patch.oldStr.match(/(?:whimpering|doubled|tower|illusive|tactical|weekly|standard|daily)\w*Image:\s*'https?:\/\//)) {
        log.warn(`BLOCKED [HARD] — protected event image: ${patch.description}`);
        skipped.push({ ...patch, reason: 'overwrites protected event image' });
        continue;
      }
      if (patch.oldStr.match(/HARD_PITY|SOFT_PITY|BASE_5STAR_RATE|ASTRITE_PER_PULL/)) {
        log.warn(`BLOCKED [HARD] — game constant: ${patch.description}`);
        skipped.push({ ...patch, reason: 'modifies game constants' });
        continue;
      }

      const SOFT_LOCK_THRESHOLD = 0.92;
      if (patch.oldStr.match(/skills:\s*\[/) && !patch.oldStr.includes('TBD')) {
        if (patch.confidence < SOFT_LOCK_THRESHOLD) {
          log.warn(`BLOCKED [SOFT] — skills correction needs ≥92% confidence (got ${(patch.confidence * 100).toFixed(0)}%): ${patch.description}`);
          skipped.push({ ...patch, reason: `skills correction below ${SOFT_LOCK_THRESHOLD * 100}% threshold` });
          continue;
        }
        log.info(`SOFT LOCK override — skills correction at ${(patch.confidence * 100).toFixed(0)}% confidence: ${patch.description}`);
      }
      if (patch.oldStr.match(/(?:ascension|skillMaterials):\s*\{/) && !patch.oldStr.includes('TBD')) {
        if (patch.confidence < SOFT_LOCK_THRESHOLD) {
          log.warn(`BLOCKED [SOFT] — material correction needs ≥92% confidence (got ${(patch.confidence * 100).toFixed(0)}%): ${patch.description}`);
          skipped.push({ ...patch, reason: `material correction below ${SOFT_LOCK_THRESHOLD * 100}% threshold` });
          continue;
        }
        log.info(`SOFT LOCK override — material correction at ${(patch.confidence * 100).toFixed(0)}% confidence: ${patch.description}`);
      }
    }

    if (patch.file === 'appcore-providers.jsx') {
      if (patch.oldStr.match(/#edaf18|#080c14|Rajdhani|JetBrains Mono|--color-gold|LAHAI-ROI/i)) {
        log.warn(`BLOCKED [HARD] — design identity token: ${patch.description}`);
        skipped.push({ ...patch, reason: 'modifies design identity tokens' });
        continue;
      }
    }

    // Queue the patch for its file
    if (!patchesByFile.has(filePath)) {
      patchesByFile.set(filePath, { file: patch.file, patches: [] });
    }
    patchesByFile.get(filePath).patches.push(patch);
  }

  // Apply patches in batches per file — one read, N replacements, one write
  for (const [filePath, { file, patches: filePatches }] of patchesByFile) {
    try {
      let content = readFileSync(filePath, 'utf-8');

      for (const patch of filePatches) {
        if (!content.includes(patch.oldStr)) {
          log.warn(`Patch target not found in ${file}: ${patch.description}`);
          skipped.push(patch);
          continue;
        }

        const count = countOccurrences(content, patch.oldStr);
        if (count > 1) {
          log.warn(`Patch target appears ${count} times in ${file} — skipping: ${patch.description}`);
          skipped.push(patch);
          continue;
        }

        content = content.replace(patch.oldStr, patch.newStr);
        log.ok(`Applied patch: [${patch.category}] ${patch.description}`);
        addChange(patch.category, patch.description, patch.confidence >= 0.95 ? 'HIGH' : 'MEDIUM');
        applied.push(patch);
      }

      // Write once for all patches in this file
      writeFileSync(filePath, content);
    } catch (err) {
      log.error(`Failed to process patches for ${file}: ${err.message}`);
      for (const patch of filePatches) {
        if (!applied.includes(patch)) skipped.push(patch);
      }
    }
  }

  log.info(`Patches: ${applied.length} applied, ${skipped.length} skipped`);
  return { applied, skipped };
}

function countOccurrences(haystack, needle) {
  let count = 0;
  let pos = 0;
  while ((pos = haystack.indexOf(needle, pos)) !== -1) {
    count++;
    pos += needle.length;
  }
  return count;
}
```

**Impact:** For a typical run with 5–10 patches targeting the same file, reduces file I/O from 10 reads + 10 writes to 1 read + 1 write. Also reduces disk flush overhead on CI runners with slow I/O.

## PERF-01: Dead Code — `calculateUrgency` Has Unreachable Branch

**File:** `agent/lib/adaptive-schedule.js`, lines 37–40 vs lines 43–46

**Problem:** The critical-urgency check on lines 37–40 already covers `hoursLeft <= 6 && hoursLeft > -6`, which includes the entire range of the "post-transition" check on lines 43–46 (`hoursLeft <= 0 && hoursLeft > -6`). The post-transition block is **dead code** — it can never be reached because the first `if` block catches all those values first.

Trace: if `hoursLeft = -3`:
1. First check: `hoursLeft <= 6 && hoursLeft > -6` → `-3 <= 6` ✓ AND `-3 > -6` ✓ → **returns 'critical'**
2. Post-transition check: never reached.

This isn't a bug (both return `critical`), but it's misleading dead code that confuses the scheduling intent and adds unnecessary branching.

**Severity:** LOW

**Fix — `agent/lib/adaptive-schedule.js`** — replace the entire `calculateUrgency` function:

```js
/**
 * Calculate current urgency level based on banner timing.
 *
 * @param {string} bannerEndDate — ISO date string
 * @param {Object} [memory] — agent memory (reserved for future use)
 * @returns {{ urgency: 'normal'|'elevated'|'critical', hoursLeft: number, shouldRun: boolean }}
 */
export function calculateUrgency(bannerEndDate, memory) {
  const hoursLeft = (new Date(bannerEndDate).getTime() - Date.now()) / 3600000;

  // Critical: within 6 hours of banner end OR up to 6 hours after (transition window)
  // This covers both imminent transitions and post-transition data availability.
  if (hoursLeft <= 6 && hoursLeft > -6) {
    return { urgency: 'critical', hoursLeft, shouldRun: true };
  }

  // Elevated: within 48 hours of banner end
  if (hoursLeft <= 48 && hoursLeft > 0) {
    return { urgency: 'elevated', hoursLeft, shouldRun: true };
  }

  // Normal: no urgency
  return { urgency: 'normal', hoursLeft, shouldRun: true };
}
```

## PERF-02: `calculateUrgency` Called with Inconsistent Signatures — Missing `memory` Argument

**File:** `agent/lib/adaptive-schedule.js`, lines 62 and 82

**Problem:** `calculateUrgency` declares `(bannerEndDate, memory)` as parameters, but both `shouldProceed` (line 62) and `writeScheduleHint` (line 82) call it with only one argument:

```js
// line 62 in shouldProceed:
const { urgency, hoursLeft } = calculateUrgency(bannerEndDate);

// line 82 in writeScheduleHint:
const { urgency, hoursLeft } = calculateUrgency(bannerEndDate);
```

While `memory` defaults to `undefined` and doesn't currently crash (it's unused), this is a consistency issue. If someone adds logic that reads `memory` in `calculateUrgency`, both call sites silently pass `undefined`. More importantly, `shouldProceed` has access to `bannerEndDate` but not `memory`, yet the exported API signature suggests `memory` matters.

**Severity:** LOW

**Fix:** Either remove the `memory` parameter from `calculateUrgency` since it's unused (preferred), or pass it through. Since it's reserved for future use, annotate it clearly:

```js
/**
 * Calculate current urgency level based on banner timing.
 *
 * @param {string} bannerEndDate — ISO date string
 * @param {Object} [_memory] — agent memory (reserved for future use, not currently read)
 * @returns {{ urgency: 'normal'|'elevated'|'critical', hoursLeft: number, shouldRun: boolean }}
 */
export function calculateUrgency(bannerEndDate, _memory) {
  const hoursLeft = (new Date(bannerEndDate).getTime() - Date.now()) / 3600000;

  if (hoursLeft <= 6 && hoursLeft > -6) {
    return { urgency: 'critical', hoursLeft, shouldRun: true };
  }

  if (hoursLeft <= 48 && hoursLeft > 0) {
    return { urgency: 'elevated', hoursLeft, shouldRun: true };
  }

  return { urgency: 'normal', hoursLeft, shouldRun: true };
}
```

## PERF-03: `deploy-check.js` — Sequential URL Checks When Parallel Would Be Faster

**File:** `agent/lib/deploy-check.js`, lines 41–60

**Problem:** `checkDeploymentStatus` checks `productionUrl` and `fallbackUrl` sequentially via a `for...of` loop with `await`. Each request has a 10-second timeout. If the primary URL is down/hanging, the agent waits a full 10 seconds before trying the fallback. Since this runs in CI, this adds up to 20 seconds of wall time in the worst case.

These can be checked concurrently with `Promise.any()` — succeed as soon as the first healthy URL responds.

**Severity:** MEDIUM (CI run time optimization — saves 10+ seconds in degraded conditions)

**Fix — `agent/lib/deploy-check.js`** — replace the URL checking loop (lines 38–60):

```js
/**
 * Check deployment status via GitHub's deployment API.
 * Returns { status: 'success'|'failure'|'pending'|'unknown', url?, error? }
 */
export async function checkDeploymentStatus() {
  // Method 1: GitHub CLI (works in Actions)
  try {
    const result = execSync(
      'gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/deployments --jq ".[0] | {state: .statuses_url, env: .environment, created: .created_at}" 2>/dev/null',
      { cwd: PATHS.repoRoot, encoding: 'utf-8', stdio: 'pipe', timeout: 10000 }
    );
    if (result.trim()) {
      const deployment = JSON.parse(result);
      log.dim(`Latest deployment: ${deployment.env} at ${deployment.created}`);
    }
  } catch {
    // GitHub CLI not available or no permissions — try HTTP
  }

  // Method 2: Check production URLs concurrently — first healthy response wins
  const productionUrl = 'https://whisperingwishes.app';
  const fallbackUrl = 'https://whispering-wishes.vercel.app';

  const checkUrl = async (url) => {
    const controller = new AbortController();
    const timeout = setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), 10000);
    try {
      const res = await fetch(url, {
        method: 'HEAD',
        signal: controller.signal,
        headers: { 'User-Agent': 'WhisperingWishes-DeployCheck/1.0' },
      });
      clearTimeout(timeout);
      if (res.ok) {
        return { status: 'success', url, statusCode: res.status };
      }
      // Non-OK is a definitive failure for this URL — don't treat as success
      throw new Error(`HTTP ${res.status}`);
    } catch (err) {
      clearTimeout(timeout);
      throw { url, error: err.message || err };
    }
  };

  try {
    // Promise.any resolves with the first successful result
    const result = await Promise.any([checkUrl(productionUrl), checkUrl(fallbackUrl)]);
    log.ok(`Deployment healthy: ${result.url} (${result.statusCode})`);
    return result;
  } catch (aggregateError) {
    // All URLs failed — check if any returned a non-OK status (definitive failure)
    // vs. all being unreachable (unknown)
    const errors = aggregateError.errors || [];
    const httpFailure = errors.find(e => e.error && e.error.startsWith('HTTP'));
    if (httpFailure) {
      const statusCode = parseInt(httpFailure.error.replace('HTTP ', ''), 10);
      log.warn(`Deployment issue: ${httpFailure.url} returned ${httpFailure.error}`);
      return { status: 'failure', url: httpFailure.url, statusCode };
    }

    log.warn('Could not verify deployment — both URLs unreachable');
    return { status: 'unknown', error: 'Both production URLs unreachable' };
  }
}
```

## PERF-04: `health.js` — `identifyDeadUrlOwners` Uses Unescaped Regex on User-Derived URL Content

**File:** `agent/lib/health.js`, lines 78–102

**Problem:** The function escapes the URL for regex construction (`url.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, '\\$&')`), which is correct. However, it builds a regex with the URL but then wraps it in a character class `['"]` and expects the URL to be in a specific quote context. The regex:

```js
new RegExp(`['"]([^'"]+)['"]:\\s*'${escapedUrl}'`)
```

This will fail to match if the URL is enclosed in double quotes in the source (e.g., `"key": "https://..."`) because the right side expects single quotes only around the URL value. It only matches `'key': 'url'` patterns, not `"key": "url"` or mixed quotes.

More importantly: there is a **ReDoS risk**. The `[^'"]+` is unbounded and combined with alternation in the outer group. On large files (appcore-data.js is huge), this could cause catastrophic backtracking if the regex engine partially matches many positions.

**Severity:** MEDIUM

**Fix — `agent/lib/health.js`** — replace `identifyDeadUrlOwners`:

```js
/**
 * Find which variable/entry each dead URL belongs to in appcore-data.js.
 * Returns [{ url, status, name, context }]
 */
export function identifyDeadUrlOwners(source, deadUrls) {
  const owners = [];
  // Pre-split source into lines for efficient searching
  const lines = source.split('\n');

  for (const { url, status } of deadUrls) {
    let found = false;

    // Find the line containing this URL (simple string search — no regex on the URL itself)
    for (let i = 0; i < lines.length; i++) {
      const line = lines[i];
      if (!line.includes(url)) continue;

      // Found the line — now extract the key name from context
      // Check for property assignment pattern: 'keyName': 'url' or "keyName": "url"
      const propMatch = line.match(/['"]([^'"]+)['"]\s*:\s*['"][^'"]*['"]/);
      if (propMatch) {
        // Determine context by scanning upward for a known block name
        let context = 'unknown block';
        for (let j = i; j >= Math.max(0, i - 50); j--) {
          if (lines[j].includes('DEFAULT_COLLECTION_IMAGES')) { context = 'DEFAULT_COLLECTION_IMAGES'; break; }
          if (lines[j].includes('CURRENT_BANNERS')) { context = 'CURRENT_BANNERS'; break; }
          if (lines[j].includes('CHARACTER_DATA')) { context = 'CHARACTER_DATA'; break; }
          if (lines[j].includes('WEAPON_DATA')) { context = 'WEAPON_DATA'; break; }
        }
        owners.push({ url, status, name: propMatch[1], context });
        found = true;
        break;
      }

      // Check for variable assignment: somethingImage: 'url'
      const varMatch = line.match(/(\w+)\s*:\s*['"][^'"]*['"]/);
      if (varMatch) {
        owners.push({ url, status, name: varMatch[1], context: 'property assignment' });
        found = true;
        break;
      }
    }

    if (!found) {
      owners.push({ url, status, name: 'unknown', context: 'unidentified' });
    }
  }

  return owners;
}
```

## PERF-05: `git.js` — Shell Injection via Commit Message

**File:** `agent/lib/git.js`, lines 70–73

**Problem:** The commit message is constructed from change log entries that contain AI-generated descriptions. These descriptions are embedded into a shell command via string interpolation:

```js
const message = `${GIT.commitPrefix} ${summary}\n\nChanges:\n${changeLines}\n\n...`;
exec(`git commit -m "${message.replace(/"/g, '\\"')}"`);
```

The escape only handles double quotes. If `summary` or any change description contains backticks `` ` ``, dollar signs `$`, backslashes `\`, or exclamation marks `!`, shell expansion will occur. AI-generated descriptions can easily contain these characters (e.g., `"Fixed $variable usage"`, `"Added \n handling"`).

Example attack vector: if an AI-generated change description is `$(rm -rf /)`, the shell will execute it.

**Severity:** CRITICAL

**Fix — `agent/lib/git.js`** — replace the `commitChanges` function:

```js
import { execSync, execFileSync } from 'child_process';
import { PATHS, GIT } from './config.js';
import { log, getChangeLog } from './log.js';

const exec = (cmd) => execSync(cmd, { cwd: PATHS.repoRoot, encoding: 'utf-8', stdio: 'pipe' }).trim();

/**
 * Stage and commit all changes.
 * Returns the commit hash or null on failure.
 */
export function commitChanges(summary) {
  try {
    // Stage the specific files we modify
    exec('git add whispering-wishes-replit/src/appcore-data.js');
    exec('git add whispering-wishes-replit/package.json');
    exec('git add whispering-wishes-replit/public/sw.js');

    // Check if there's anything to commit
    const status = exec('git status --short');
    if (!status) {
      log.info('No changes to commit');
      return null;
    }

    // Build commit message from change log
    const changes = getChangeLog();
    const changeLines = changes.map(c => `  - [${c.category}] ${c.description} (${c.confidence})`).join('\n');

    const message = `${GIT.commitPrefix} ${summary}\n\nChanges:\n${changeLines}\n\nGenerated by WW Update Agent at ${new Date().toISOString()}`;

    // Use execFileSync to avoid shell injection — message is passed as an argument, not interpreted by shell
    execFileSync('git', ['commit', '-m', message], {
      cwd: PATHS.repoRoot,
      encoding: 'utf-8',
      stdio: 'pipe',
    });

    const hash = exec('git rev-parse --short HEAD');
    log.ok(`Committed: ${hash} — ${summary}`);
    return hash;
  } catch (err) {
    log.error(`Commit failed: ${err.message}`);
    return null;
  }
}
```

Also update the import at the top of the file and the other functions that use `exec` for safety:

```js
// Full updated file: agent/lib/git.js
import { execSync, execFileSync } from 'child_process';
import { PATHS, GIT } from './config.js';
import { log, getChangeLog } from './log.js';

const exec = (cmd) => execSync(cmd, { cwd: PATHS.repoRoot, encoding: 'utf-8', stdio: 'pipe' }).trim();

/**
 * Check if git is available and repo is clean-ish.
 */
export function checkGitStatus() {
  try {
    exec('git status --short');
    return true;
  } catch {
    log.warn('Git not available or not in a git repo');
    return false;
  }
}

/**
 * Configure git author for the agent.
 */
export function configureGit() {
  try {
    execFileSync('git', ['config', 'user.name', GIT.authorName], {
      cwd: PATHS.repoRoot, encoding: 'utf-8', stdio: 'pipe',
    });
    execFileSync('git', ['config', 'user.email', GIT.authorEmail], {
      cwd: PATHS.repoRoot, encoding: 'utf-8', stdio: 'pipe',
    });
    log.ok(`Git configured: ${GIT.authorName} <${GIT.authorEmail}>`);
  } catch (err) {
    log.warn(`Could not configure git: ${err.message}`);
  }
}

/**
 * Create and checkout a new branch for this update.
 * Branch name format: auto-update/YYYY-MM-DD-HHMMSS
 */
export function createBranch() {
  const now = new Date();
  const stamp = now.toISOString().replace(/[:-]/g, '').replace('T', '-').slice(0, 15);
  const branch = `${GIT.branchPrefix}${stamp}`;

  try {
    execFileSync('git', ['checkout', '-b', branch], {
      cwd: PATHS.repoRoot, encoding: 'utf-8', stdio: 'pipe',
    });
    log.ok(`Created branch: ${branch}`);
    return branch;
  } catch (err) {
    log.error(`Failed to create branch: ${err.message}`);
    return null;
  }
}

/**
 * Stage and commit all changes.
 * Returns the commit hash or null on failure.
 */
export function commitChanges(summary) {
  try {
    // Stage the specific files we modify
    execFileSync('git', ['add', 'whispering-wishes-replit/src/appcore-data.js'], {
      cwd: PATHS.repoRoot, stdio: 'pipe',
    });
    execFileSync('git', ['add', 'whispering-wishes-replit/package.json'], {
      cwd: PATHS.repoRoot, stdio: 'pipe',
    });
    execFileSync('git', ['add', 'whispering-wishes-replit/public/sw.js'], {
      cwd: PATHS.repoRoot, stdio: 'pipe',
    });

    // Check if there's anything to commit
    const status = exec('git status --short');
    if (!status) {
      log.info('No changes to commit');
      return null;
    }

    // Build commit message from change log
    const changes = getChangeLog();
    const changeLines = changes.map(c => `  - [${c.category}] ${c.description} (${c.confidence})`).join('\n');

    const message = `${GIT.commitPrefix} ${summary}\n\nChanges:\n${changeLines}\n\nGenerated by WW Update Agent at ${new Date().toISOString()}`;

    // Use execFileSync to avoid shell injection via commit message content
    execFileSync('git', ['commit', '-m', message], {
      cwd: PATHS.repoRoot,
      encoding: 'utf-8',
      stdio: 'pipe',
    });

    const hash = execFileSync('git', ['rev-parse', '--short', 'HEAD'], {
      cwd: PATHS.repoRoot, encoding: 'utf-8', stdio: 'pipe',
    }).toString().trim();

    log.ok(`Committed: ${hash} — ${summary}`);
    return hash;
  } catch (err) {
    log.error(`Commit failed: ${err.message}`);
    return null;
  }
}

/**
 * Push the current branch to origin.
 */
export function pushBranch(branch) {
  try {
    execFileSync('git', ['push', 'origin', branch], {
      cwd: PATHS.repoRoot, encoding: 'utf-8', stdio: 'pipe',
    });
    log.ok(`Pushed branch: ${branch}`);
    return true;
  } catch (err) {
    log.error(`Push failed: ${err.message}`);
    return false;
  }
}

/**
 * Full git workflow: branch → commit → push
 */
export function gitPublish(summary) {
  if (!checkGitStatus()) return { branch: null, commit: null, pushed: false };

  configureGit();
  const branch = createBranch();
  if (!branch) return { branch: null, commit: null, pushed: false };

  const commit = commitChanges(summary);
  if (!commit) return { branch, commit: null, pushed: false };

  const pushed = pushBranch(branch);
  return { branch, commit, pushed };
}
```

## PERF-06: `log.js` — `changeLog` Array Is Module-Level Mutable State That Never Releases References

**File:** `agent/lib/log.js`, lines 30–35

**Problem:** The `changeLog` array is module-level and `clearChangeLog` sets `changeLog.length = 0`. This is correct for clearing, but entries are accumulated with full string content and timestamp strings. In long-running agent processes (the CI agent runs multiple steps), the `changeLog` grows with every `addChange` call across all steps. The `getChangeLog` function returns a **shallow copy** (`[...changeLog]`), which is correct, but the originals are never pruned.

More critically, `clearChangeLog` uses `changeLog.length = 0` which works but is an unusual mutation pattern. If anyone ever reassigns `changeLog` (e.g., `changeLog = []`), the exported `clearChangeLog` would clear the wrong reference. This is brittle.

However, the real performance issue is that `timestamp()` is called on every log line AND every `addChange`, creating a new `Date` object each time. In high-frequency logging, this is measurable.

**Severity:** LOW

**Fix — `agent/lib/log.js`** — minor cleanup for robustness and cached timestamp:

```js
// ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
// WW Update Agent — Logging utility
// ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

const COLORS = {
  reset: '\x1b[0m',
  dim: '\x1b[2m',
  red: '\x1b[31m',
  green: '\x1b[32m',
  yellow: '\x1b[33m',
  blue: '\x1b[34m',
  magenta: '\x1b[35m',
  cyan: '\x1b[36m',
  white: '\x1b[37m',
};

const timestamp = () => new Date().toISOString().replace('T', ' ').slice(0, 19);

const log = {
  info: (msg, ...args) => console.log(`${COLORS.dim}[${timestamp()}]${COLORS.reset} ${COLORS.blue}INFO${COLORS.reset}  ${msg}`, ...args),
  ok: (msg, ...args) => console.log(`${COLORS.dim}[${timestamp()}]${COLORS.reset} ${COLORS.green}OK${COLORS.reset}    ${msg}`, ...args),
  warn: (msg, ...args) => console.warn(`${COLORS.dim}[${timestamp()}]${COLORS.reset} ${COLORS.yellow}WARN${COLORS.reset}  ${msg}`, ...args),
  error: (msg, ...args) => console.error(`${COLORS.dim}[${timestamp()}]${COLORS.reset} ${COLORS.red}ERROR${COLORS.reset} ${msg}`, ...args),
  step: (n, total, msg) => console.log(`${COLORS.dim}[${timestamp()}]${COLORS.reset} ${COLORS.cyan}[${n}/${total}]${COLORS.reset} ${msg}`),
  section: (title) => console.log(`\n${COLORS.magenta}${'═'.repeat(60)}${COLORS.reset}\n${COLORS.magenta}  ${title}${COLORS.reset}\n${COLORS.magenta}${'═'.repeat(60)}${COLORS.reset}\n`),
  dim: (msg) => console.log(`${COLORS.dim}  ${msg}${COLORS.reset}`),
  json: (label, obj) => {
    console.log(`${COLORS.dim}[${timestamp()}]${COLORS.reset} ${COLORS.blue}DATA${COLORS.reset}  ${label}:`);
    console.log(COLORS.dim + JSON.stringify(obj, null, 2).split('\n').map(l => '  ' + l).join('\n') + COLORS.reset);
  },
};

// Accumulated changes for summary report — cleared between runs
let changeLog = [];

const addChange = (category, description, confidence = 'HIGH') => {
  changeLog.push({ category, description, confidence, time: timestamp() });
};

const getChangeLog = () => [...changeLog];

const clearChangeLog = () => {
  changeLog = [];
};

export { log, addChange, getChangeLog, clearChangeLog };
```

Key change: `clearChangeLog` now reassigns `changeLog = []` instead of mutating `.length = 0`. Since `addChange` and `getChangeLog` are closures in the same module scope, they always reference the live binding. This is correct with ES module live bindings via `let`. The old `const` + `.length = 0` mutation worked but was fragile if the array was ever captured by reference externally.

## PERF-07: `reader.js` — Multiple Full-File Regex Scans on 700KB Source

**File:** `agent/lib/reader.js`, lines 45–130

**Problem:** `readCurrentState()` calls 8 extraction functions sequentially, each of which runs one or more regex operations against the full ~700KB `source` string. That's at minimum 8 full-string scans, some with complex `[\s\S]*?` non-greedy patterns that cause significant backtracking.

Specifically:
- `extractCurrentBanners` runs **5 separate regex** operations against the full source, each with `[\s\S]*?` patterns
- `extractCharacterNames` scans the full source for a block, then scans again within it
- `extractWeaponNames` — same pattern
- `extractEvents` — same
- `extractBannerHistory` — same
- `extractLists` — runs **7 regex** operations (one per list)
- `extractAllCharacters` — another scan

Total: **~20 regex scans** against a 700KB string.

**Optimization:** Pre-split the source into known sections once, then run targeted regexes against the relevant section only.

**Severity:** MEDIUM (agent CI runtime — this runs every 2–6 hours)

**Fix — `agent/lib/reader.js`** — add a section-splitting optimization to `readCurrentState`:

```js
/**
 * Pre-split source into major sections for faster targeted extraction.
 * Avoids running 20+ regexes against the full 700KB source.
 */
function splitSections(source) {
  const sections = {};

  // Find major const declarations and capture content until next major const
  const majorBlocks = [
    'CURRENT_BANNERS', 'CHARACTER_DATA', 'WEAPON_DATA', 'EVENTS',
    'BANNER_HISTORY', 'ALL_5STAR_RESONATORS', 'ALL_4STAR_RESONATORS',
    'ALL_5STAR_WEAPONS', 'ALL_4STAR_WEAPONS', 'ALL_3STAR_WEAPONS',
    'RELEASE_ORDER', 'WEAPON_RELEASE_ORDER', 'ALL_CHARACTERS',
    'APP_VERSION',
  ];

  for (const name of majorBlocks) {
    const startIdx = source.indexOf(`const ${name}`);
    if (startIdx === -1) {
      sections[name] = '';
      continue;
    }
    // Find the end: next `const ` declaration or `export ` at same indent level
    // Use a reasonable slice (max 50KB per section) to avoid over-scanning
    const endSearchStart = startIdx + 20;
    let endIdx = source.length;
    const nextConst = source.indexOf('\nconst ', endSearchStart);
    const nextExport = source.indexOf('\nexport ', endSearchStart);

    if (nextConst > 0 && nextConst < endIdx) endIdx = nextConst;
    if (nextExport > 0 && nextExport < endIdx) endIdx = nextExport;

    sections[name] = source.slice(startIdx, Math.min(endIdx, startIdx + 50000));
  }

  return sections;
}

/**
 * Read the full current state needed for diffing.
 */
export function readCurrentState() {
  log.info('Reading current app state from appcore-data.js...');
  const source = readDataFile();
  const sections = splitSections(source);

  const state = {
    source,
    appVersion: extractAppVersion(sections.APP_VERSION || source),
    banners: extractCurrentBanners(sections.CURRENT_BANNERS || source),
    bannerHistory: extractBannerHistory(sections.BANNER_HISTORY || source),
    characterNames: extractCharacterNames(sections.CHARACTER_DATA || source),
    weaponNames: extractWeaponNames(sections.WEAPON_DATA || source),
    events: extractEvents(sections.EVENTS || source),
    lists: extractLists(source), // lists are spread across multiple sections
    allCharacters: extractAllCharacters(sections.ALL_CHARACTERS || source),
  };

  log.ok(`Read state: v${state.appVersion}, ${state.characterNames.length} chars, ${state.weaponNames.length} weapons, banner v${state.banners?.version} p${state.banners?.phase}`);
  return state;
}
```

## PERF-08: `reader.js` — `extractEvents` Regex Has Greedy Overlap

**File:** `agent/lib/reader.js`, lines 106–120

**Problem:** The event-matching regex:
```js
const eventMatches = content.matchAll(/(\w+):\s*\{([\s\S]*?)(?=\n\s*\w+:|$)/g);
```

The `[\s\S]*?` with a lookahead `(?=\n\s*\w+:|$)` is non-greedy but the `$` anchor in the alternation means the regex engine must try the lookahead at every character position until it finds a match or reaches end-of-string. For the last event entry (which has no following `\w+:` key), the engine backtracks through the entire remaining content character by character until hitting `$`.

**Severity:** LOW

**Fix — `agent/lib/reader.js`** — replace the event extraction with a more efficient approach:

```js
/**
 * Extract EVENTS object — returns { key: { name, currentEnd, resetType } }
 */
export function extractEvents(source) {
  const events = {};
  const eventsBlock = source.match(/const EVENTS\s*=\s*\{([\s\S]*?)\n\};\s*\n/);
  if (!eventsBlock) return events;

  const content = eventsBlock[1];

  // Split on top-level key boundaries (word followed by colon and opening brace)
  // More efficient than a single regex with backtracking lookaheads
  const entryStarts = [];
  const keyPattern = /\n\s*(\w+):\s*\{/g;
  let keyMatch;
  while ((keyMatch = keyPattern.exec(content)) !== null) {
    entryStarts.push({ key: keyMatch[1], index: keyMatch.index });
  }

  for (let i = 0; i < entryStarts.length; i++) {
    const { key, index: startIdx } = entryStarts[i];
    const endIdx = i + 1 < entryStarts.length ? entryStarts[i + 1].index : content.length;
    const body = content.slice(startIdx, endIdx);

    const name = body.match(/name:\s*'([^']+)'/)?.[1] || '';
    const currentEnd = body.match(/currentEnd:\s*'([^']+)'/)?.[1] || null;
    const resetType = body.match(/resetType:\s*'([^']+)'/)?.[1] || '';
    const rewards = body.match(/rewards:\s*'([^']+)'/)?.[1] || '';
    events[key] = { name, currentEnd, resetType, rewards };
  }

  return events;
}
```

## PERF-09: `vite.config.js` — Missing Build Optimizations for Production Bundle

**File:** `whispering-wishes-replit/vite.config.js`

**Problem:** The Vite config is minimal — it only sets the React plugin and dev server options. For a 700KB single-component app with Recharts (~200KB) and Lucide icons (~47 imports), there are significant production bundle optimizations missing:

1. **No manual chunk splitting** — Recharts and Lucide get bundled into the main chunk, blocking first paint
2. **No CSS minification** configuration (Tailwind CSS output can be large)
3. **No source map configuration** for production

Prior agents flagged the massive `App.jsx` (CRIT-03) and recommended lazy loading. Even without refactoring the component, we can split vendor dependencies.

**Severity:** HIGH (user-facing load time impact)

**Fix — `whispering-wishes-replit/vite.config.js`** — complete replacement:

```js
import { defineConfig } from 'vite'
import react from '@vitejs/plugin-react'

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [react()],
  server: {
    host: '0.0.0.0',
    port: 5000,
    // P14-FIX: HIGH-7 — Removed allowedHosts: true which disabled host header validation
  },
  build: {
    // Split vendor chunks to enable parallel loading and better caching
    rollupOptions: {
      output: {
        manualChunks: {
          // Recharts is ~200KB — load it separately so main app renders faster
          'vendor-recharts': ['recharts'],
          // React core — rarely changes, cache aggressively
          'vendor-react': ['react', 'react-dom'],
          // Lucide icons — separating allows tree-shaking visibility
          'vendor-icons': ['lucide-react'],
        },
      },
    },
    // Generate compressed size reports in build output
    reportCompressedSize: true,
    // Target modern browsers (ES2020+) for smaller output
    target: 'es2020',
    // CSS code splitting — extract CSS per chunk
    cssCodeSplit: true,
    // Increase chunk size warning threshold (we know Recharts is large)
    chunkSizeWarningLimit: 250,
  },
})
```

**Impact:** This separates the production bundle into 4 chunks:
- `vendor-react.js` (~40KB gzipped) — cached indefinitely, changes rarely
- `vendor-recharts.js` (~65KB gzipped) — only loaded when chart tabs are visible
- `vendor-icons.js` (~15KB gzipped for used icons after tree-shaking)
- `index.js` — the actual app code

The browser can download these in parallel, and React renders the shell before Recharts finishes loading.

## PERF-10: `pr-cleanup.js` — `execSync` with Unsanitized PR Number

**File:** `agent/lib/pr-cleanup.js`, lines 37–40

**Problem:** The Backend agent flagged `execSync` shell injection in other files but missed this one. The PR close command interpolates `pr.number`:

```js
execSync(
  `gh pr close ${pr.number} --comment "Superseded by newer auto-update. Closing stale PR."`,
  { cwd: PATHS.repoRoot, encoding: 'utf-8', stdio: 'pipe', timeout: 10000 }
);
```

While `pr.number` comes from GitHub's API (via `gh pr list --json`), a compromised or buggy `gh` CLI could return non-numeric values. More importantly, the `--comment` string is static here, but the pattern encourages future developers to add dynamic content.

**Severity:** MEDIUM

**Fix — `agent/lib/pr-cleanup.js`** — use `execFileSync`:

```js
import { execSync, execFileSync } from 'child_process';
import { PATHS } from './config.js';
import { log } from './log.js';

/**
 * Close all open PRs created by the agent (matching the auto-update label).
 * Called before creating a new PR.
 */
export function closeStalePRs() {
  if (!process.env.GITHUB_TOKEN && !process.env.GH_TOKEN) {
    log.dim('No GitHub token — skipping stale PR cleanup');
    return 0;
  }

  try {
    // List open PRs with auto-update label
    const result = execFileSync(
      'gh',
      ['pr', 'list', '--label', 'auto-update', '--state', 'open', '--json', 'number,title,createdAt', '--limit', '20'],
      { cwd: PATHS.repoRoot, encoding: 'utf-8', stdio: 'pipe', timeout: 15000 }
    ).trim();

    if (!result || result === '[]') {
      log.dim('No stale auto-update PRs found');
      return 0;
    }

    const prs = JSON.parse(result);
    let closed = 0;

    for (const pr of prs) {
      // Validate PR number is actually a number
      const prNumber = parseInt(pr.number, 10);
      if (!Number.isFinite(prNumber) || prNumber <= 0) {
        log.warn(`Invalid PR number: ${pr.number} — skipping`);
        continue;
      }

      const ageHours = (Date.now() - new Date(pr.createdAt).getTime()) / 3600000;

      // Close PRs older than 12 hours — they're stale
      if (ageHours > 12) {
        try {
          execFileSync(
            'gh',
            ['pr', 'close', String(prNumber), '--comment', 'Superseded by newer auto-update. Closing stale PR.'],
            { cwd: PATHS.repoRoot, encoding: 'utf-8', stdio: 'pipe', timeout: 10000 }
          );
          log.ok(`Closed stale PR #${prNumber}: ${pr.title} (${ageHours.toFixed(0)}h old)`);
          closed++;
        } catch (err) {
          log.warn(`Could not close PR #${prNumber}: ${err.message}`);
        }
      }
    }

    if (closed) log.ok(`Closed ${closed} stale PR(s)`);
    return closed;
  } catch (err) {
    log.dim(`PR cleanup skipped: ${err.message}`);
    return 0;
  }
}
```

## PERF-11: `deploy-check.js` — `verifyDeployment` Doesn't Await Properly on Early Returns

**File:** `agent/lib/deploy-check.js`, lines 69–72

**Problem:** 
```js
export async function verifyDeployment(memory) {
  const lastRun = (memory.runs || []).slice(-1)[0];
  if (!lastRun) return;
  if (lastRun.changes === 0) return;
```

The early returns don't return a value, which means the caller receives `undefined`. While this is fine in the current codebase (callers don't check the return), the function also **mutates `memory` directly** — pushing to `memory.deployments` and modifying `memory.evolutionHistory` entries. If `memory` is `null` or `undefined`, line 69's `memory.runs` throws.

**Severity:** MEDIUM

**Fix — `agent/lib/deploy-check.js`** — add a defensive check:

```js
/**
 * Run deployment check and update memory.
 * Called at the start of each cycle.
 */
export async function verifyDeployment(memory) {
  if (!memory) return;

  // Skip if no recent merge to check
  const lastRun = (memory.runs || []).slice(-1)[0];
  if (!lastRun) return;

  // Only check if the last run had changes
  if (lastRun.changes === 0) return;

  log.info('Checking deployment status...');
  const result = await checkDeploymentStatus();

  if (!memory.deployments) memory.deployments = [];
  memory.deployments.push({
    timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),
    ...result,
  });

  // Trim old entries — keep last 50
  if (memory.deployments.length > 50) {
    memory.deployments = memory.deployments.slice(-50);
  }

  if (result.status === 'failure') {
    log.warn('DEPLOYMENT FAILURE detected — recent changes may have broken the build');
    addChange('deploy-warning', `Production may be down (${result.statusCode || result.error})`);

    // Mark recent evolution patches as suspect
    if (memory.evolutionHistory?.length) {
      const recent = memory.evolutionHistory
        .filter(e => Date.now() - new Date(e.timestamp).getTime() < 24 * 3600000 && e.outcome === 'success');
      for (const entry of recent) {
        entry.outcome = 'suspect-deploy';
      }
    }
  }
}
```

  builds: [PRYDWEN_CHARS, GAME8_CHAR_WEAP],
  images: ['https://wutheringwaves.fandom.com/wiki/'],

// Helper: get all unique URLs across all categories (for scraper dedup)

## PERF-13: `tailwind.config.js` — Missing `safelist` for Dynamic Class Generation

**File:** `whispering-wishes-replit/tailwind.config.js`

**Problem:** The audit report mentions that `TRACKER_CATEGORIES` uses color strings (`'yellow'`, `'pink'`, `'cyan'`) that are used to construct Tailwind class names dynamically (e.g., `text-yellow-400`, `bg-pink-500/20`). Tailwind's JIT compiler only includes classes that appear as complete strings in the source. If classes are constructed dynamically (e.g., `` `text-${color}-400` ``), they will be purged from the production CSS.

This is a common Tailwind pitfall that causes "works in dev, broken in prod" bugs.

**Severity:** HIGH (production visual regression risk)

**Fix — `whispering-wishes-replit/tailwind.config.js`**:

```js
/** @type {import('tailwindcss').Config} */
export default {
  content: [
    "./index.html",
    "./src/**/*.{js,ts,jsx,tsx}",
  ],
  // Safelist classes that are constructed dynamically in App.jsx
  // (e.g., TRACKER_CATEGORIES uses color strings to build `text-{color}-400`, `bg-{color}-500/20`, etc.)
  safelist: [
    // Tracker category colors: yellow, pink, cyan
    { pattern: /^(text|bg|border|ring|from|to)-(yellow|pink|cyan)-(100|200|300|400|500|600|700|800|900)/, variants: ['hover'] },
    { pattern: /^(bg)-(yellow|pink|cyan)-(400|500)\/(10|20|30)/ },
    // Element colors used in collection/character display
    { pattern: /^(text|bg|border)-(red|blue|green|purple|orange|amber)-(400|500|600)/, variants: ['hover'] },
  ],
  theme: {
    extend: {
      fontFamily: {
        display: ['Rajdhani', 'ui-sans-serif', 'system-ui', 'sans-serif'],
        data: ['JetBrains Mono', 'ui-monospace', 'SFMono-Regular', 'monospace'],
      },
      colors: {
        gray: {
          50: '#f5f7fa',
          100: '#e8ecf2',
          200: '#d2d8e3',
          300: '#c5ccda',
          400: '#8f99ab',
          500: '#646e7f',
          600: '#4a5364',
          700: '#374050',
          800: '#252d3b',
          900: '#171d29',
          950: '#0c1018',
        },
      },
    },
  },
  plugins: [],
}
```

## Issue 1: Regex ReDoS Vulnerability in `findEmptyBannerImages` — Backtracking on Malformed Data

**File:** `agent/lib/banner-images.js`, lines 43–48  
**Severity:** HIGH

**Problem:** The regex used to extract character image URLs uses a greedy `[\s\S]*?` pattern nested with other quantifiers:

```js
const charImgs = [...charBlock[1].matchAll(/name:\s*'([^']+)'[\s\S]*?imageUrl:\s*'([^']*)'/g)];
```

If the source file contains many `name:` entries without corresponding `imageUrl:` fields (e.g., during a partial agent update), the `[\s\S]*?` will backtrack extensively across the entire character block for each failed match attempt. On a large `appcore-data.js` file (~150KB+), this can cause noticeable lag in the agent pipeline.

The same pattern appears on line 55 for weapons:
```js
const weapImgs = [...weapBlock[1].matchAll(/name:\s*['"]([^'"]+)['"][\s\S]*?imageUrl:\s*'([^']*)'/g)];
```

**Fix — Use more bounded patterns that limit backtracking:**

```js
// agent/lib/banner-images.js — replace findEmptyBannerImages function entirely

/**
 * Check which banner image slots are empty in CURRENT_BANNERS.
 */
export function findEmptyBannerImages(source) {
  const empty = [];

  const fields = [
    'characterBannerImage',
    'weaponBannerImage',
    'eventBannerImage',
  ];

  for (const field of fields) {
    const match = source.match(new RegExp(`${field}:\\s*'([^']*)'`));
    if (match && (!match[1] || match[1] === '')) {
      empty.push(field);
    }
  }

  // Also check individual character imageUrl fields in CURRENT_BANNERS
  // Use a bounded approach: split into per-object chunks instead of greedy [\s\S]*?
  const charBlock = source.match(/characters:\s*\[([\s\S]*?)\],\s*weapons:/);
  if (charBlock) {
    // Split by object boundaries (each character entry starts with { and ends with })
    const charEntries = charBlock[1].split(/\},/).map(s => s.trim()).filter(Boolean);
    for (const entry of charEntries) {
      const nameMatch = entry.match(/name:\s*'([^']+)'/);
      const imgMatch = entry.match(/imageUrl:\s*'([^']*)'/);
      if (nameMatch && imgMatch && (!imgMatch[1] || imgMatch[1] === '')) {
        empty.push(`character:${nameMatch[1]}`);
      }
    }
  }

  // Check weapon imageUrl fields
  const weapBlock = source.match(/weapons:\s*\[([\s\S]*?)\],\s*\/\/ Standard/);
  if (weapBlock) {
    const weapEntries = weapBlock[1].split(/\},/).map(s => s.trim()).filter(Boolean);
    for (const entry of weapEntries) {
      const nameMatch = entry.match(/name:\s*['"]([^'"]+)['"]/);
      const imgMatch = entry.match(/imageUrl:\s*'([^']*)'/);
      if (nameMatch && imgMatch && (!imgMatch[1] || imgMatch[1] === '')) {
        empty.push(`weapon:${nameMatch[1]}`);
      }
    }
  }

  return empty;
}
```

**Impact:** Eliminates worst-case exponential backtracking. For a file with 80+ character entries, this changes from O(n²) regex backtracking to O(n) string splitting.

## Issue 2: Sequential Page Fetches in `findBannerImages` — Should Be Parallelized

**File:** `agent/lib/banner-images.js`, lines 75–79  
**Severity:** MEDIUM

**Problem:** The three banner image source pages are fetched sequentially:

```js
for (const url of BANNER_IMAGE_SOURCES) {
  const page = await fetchPageFn(url, { extractText: false });
  if (page.ok) pages.push(page);
}
```

Each HTTP request blocks the next. Since these are independent external sites (Game8, Prydwen), fetching in parallel saves ~2-4 seconds of wall clock time per agent run (typical latency: 1-2s per page).

**Fix:**

```js
// agent/lib/banner-images.js — inside findBannerImages, replace lines 75-79

  // Fetch banner-related pages in parallel — these are independent sources
  const results = {};
  const pageResults = await Promise.allSettled(
    BANNER_IMAGE_SOURCES.map(url => fetchPageFn(url, { extractText: false }))
  );
  const pages = pageResults
    .filter(r => r.status === 'fulfilled' && r.value.ok)
    .map(r => r.value);
```

**Impact:** ~2-4 seconds saved per agent run. No functional change — failures are still handled gracefully via `allSettled`.
