## Issue 3: Redundant Regex Compilation in `applyBannerImages` — Same Pattern Built Multiple Times

**File:** `agent/lib/banner-images.js`, lines 143–186  
**Severity:** LOW

**Problem:** Inside the `applyBannerImages` loop, for `character:` and `weapon:` slots, the same escaped name is computed twice — once for the "already has image" check and once for the actual replacement. The same regex pattern is also rebuilt:

```js
// Line 150: First construction
const escapedName = itemName.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, '\\$&');
const existingMatch = buf.match(new RegExp(`name:\\s*['"]${escapedName}['"][\\s\\S]*?imageUrl:\\s*'([^']*)'`));
// ...
// Line 175: Same construction again
const escapedName = itemName.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, '\\$&');
const pattern = new RegExp(`(name:\\s*['"]${escapedName}['"][\\s\\S]*?imageUrl:\\s*)'([^']*)'`);
```

This also has the same `[\s\S]*?` ReDoS risk identified in Issue 1.

**Fix — refactor to compute once and use bounded matching:**

```js
// agent/lib/banner-images.js — replace applyBannerImages function entirely

/**
 * Upload found banner images to imgbb and update the source buffer.
 * Returns true if any images were updated.
 */
export async function applyBannerImages(foundImages, getBufferFn, loadBufferFn) {
  if (!Object.keys(foundImages).length) return false;
  if (!process.env.IMGBB_API_KEY) {
    log.warn('IMGBB_API_KEY not set — cannot upload banner images');
    return false;
  }

  let changed = false;

  for (const [slot, sourceUrl] of Object.entries(foundImages)) {
    const buf = getBufferFn();
    const isItemSlot = slot.startsWith('character:') || slot.startsWith('weapon:');

    // ── Check if slot already has a real URL ──────────────────────────
    if (isItemSlot) {
      const itemName = slot.split(':')[1];
      const escapedName = itemName.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, '\\$&');

      // Use bounded search: find the name, then search within the next 500 chars for imageUrl
      const nameIdx = buf.search(new RegExp(`name:\\s*['"]${escapedName}['"]`));
      if (nameIdx === -1) {
        log.dim(`Skipped ${slot} — not found in source`);
        continue;
      }
      const searchWindow = buf.slice(nameIdx, nameIdx + 500);
      const imgInWindow = searchWindow.match(/imageUrl:\s*'([^']*)'/);

      if (imgInWindow && imgInWindow[1] && imgInWindow[1].startsWith('http')) {
        log.dim(`Skipped ${slot} — already has image`);
        continue;
      }

      // Slot is empty — upload and fill
      const imgName = slot.replace(/[:/]/g, '-').replace(/\s+/g, '-');
      const imgbbUrl = await uploadToImgbb(sourceUrl, imgName);
      if (!imgbbUrl) continue;

      if (imgInWindow) {
        // Replace empty imageUrl within the bounded window
        const fullMatch = buf.slice(nameIdx, nameIdx + searchWindow.indexOf(imgInWindow[0]) + imgInWindow[0].length);
        const replacement = fullMatch.replace(/imageUrl:\s*'([^']*)'/, `imageUrl: '${imgbbUrl}'`);
        loadBufferFn(buf.slice(0, nameIdx) + replacement + buf.slice(nameIdx + fullMatch.length));
        log.ok(`Banner image: ${slot} → ${imgbbUrl}`);
        addChange('banner-images', `Filled ${slot} image`);
        changed = true;
      }
    } else {
      // Top-level field (characterBannerImage, weaponBannerImage, etc.)
      if (isProtectedImageField(slot)) {
        const existingMatch = buf.match(new RegExp(`${slot}:\\s*'([^']*)'`));
        if (existingMatch && existingMatch[1] && existingMatch[1].startsWith('http')) {
          log.dim(`Skipped protected field ${slot} — already has custom image`);
          continue;
        }
      }

      const existingMatch = buf.match(new RegExp(`${slot}:\\s*'([^']*)'`));
      if (existingMatch && existingMatch[1] && existingMatch[1].startsWith('http')) {
        log.dim(`Skipped ${slot} — already has image`);
        continue;
      }

      // Slot is empty — upload and fill
      const imgName = slot.replace(/[:/]/g, '-').replace(/\s+/g, '-');
      const imgbbUrl = await uploadToImgbb(sourceUrl, imgName);
      if (!imgbbUrl) continue;

      const pattern = new RegExp(`(${slot}:\\s*)'([^']*)'`);
      const match = buf.match(pattern);
      if (match) {
        loadBufferFn(buf.replace(match[0], `${match[1]}'${imgbbUrl}'`));
        log.ok(`Banner image: ${slot} → ${imgbbUrl}`);
        addChange('banner-images', `Filled ${slot}`);
        changed = true;
      }
    }
  }

  return changed;
}
```

**Impact:** Eliminates redundant regex construction per slot, removes `[\s\S]*?` backtracking risk by using bounded 500-char search windows, and reduces code duplication.

## Issue 4: `appendToChangelog` Has a Double-Write Bug When Section Already Exists

**File:** `agent/lib/changelog.js`, lines 74–86  
**Severity:** MEDIUM

**Problem:** When appending to an existing date+version section, the code searches for the end of that section:

```js
const sectionEnd = existing.indexOf('\n## ', existing.indexOf(`## v${appVersion} — ${date}`) + 1);
const insertPoint = sectionEnd === -1 ? existing.length : sectionEnd;

const newLines = entries.map(e => `- **${e.category}**: ${e.description}`).join('\n');
existing = existing.slice(0, insertPoint) + '\n' + newLines + existing.slice(insertPoint);
```

The problem is that on subsequent runs on the same day, this code **does not check for duplicate entries**. If the agent runs twice in the same day with the same changes (e.g., a retry after a partial failure), every entry gets duplicated. Over time, the changelog balloons with repeated lines.

**Fix:**

```js
// agent/lib/changelog.js — replace appendToChangelog function entirely

/**
 * Append entries to CHANGELOG.md.
 * Deduplicates entries within the same date+version section.
 */
export function appendToChangelog(entries, appVersion) {
  if (!entries.length) return;

  const date = entries[0].date;

  let existing = '';
  if (existsSync(CHANGELOG_FILE)) {
    existing = readFileSync(CHANGELOG_FILE, 'utf-8');
  } else {
    existing = `# Whispering Wishes — Changelog\n\nAuto-generated by the WW Update Agent.\n\n`;
  }

  const newLines = entries.map(e => `- **${e.category}**: ${e.description}`);

  // Check if we already have an entry for this date+version
  const sectionHeader = `## v${appVersion} — ${date}`;
  if (existing.includes(sectionHeader)) {
    // Find the section boundaries
    const sectionStart = existing.indexOf(sectionHeader);
    const sectionEnd = existing.indexOf('\n## ', sectionStart + 1);
    const sectionContent = sectionEnd === -1
      ? existing.slice(sectionStart)
      : existing.slice(sectionStart, sectionEnd);

    // Filter out entries that already exist in the section (deduplicate)
    const uniqueNewLines = newLines.filter(line => !sectionContent.includes(line));

    if (uniqueNewLines.length === 0) {
      log.dim('Changelog: all entries already present, skipping');
      return;
    }

    const insertPoint = sectionEnd === -1 ? existing.length : sectionEnd;
    existing = existing.slice(0, insertPoint) + '\n' + uniqueNewLines.join('\n') + existing.slice(insertPoint);
  } else {
    // New section — insert after the header
    const section = `${sectionHeader}\n\n${newLines.join('\n')}\n\n`;
    const headerEnd = existing.indexOf('\n\n', existing.indexOf('# '));
    if (headerEnd !== -1) {
      existing = existing.slice(0, headerEnd + 2) + section + existing.slice(headerEnd + 2);
    } else {
      existing += section;
    }
  }

  writeFileSync(CHANGELOG_FILE, existing);
  log.ok(`Changelog updated: ${entries.length} entries`);
}
```

**Impact:** Prevents changelog file bloat from repeated agent runs. Without this fix, a changelog can grow by hundreds of duplicate lines over a few weeks of daily runs.

## Issue 5: `updateAppChangelog` Fragile Trimming Logic — Splits on Newlines but Entries Can Be Multi-Line

**File:** `agent/lib/changelog.js`, lines 105–112  
**Severity:** MEDIUM

**Problem:**

```js
const trimmed = allEntries.split('\n')
  .filter(l => l.trim().startsWith('{'))
  .slice(0, MAX_APP_ENTRIES)
  .join(',\n');
```

This assumes each entry occupies exactly one line. But the entry template is:

```js
`  { date: '${e.date}', category: '${e.category}', text: '${e.description.replace(/'/g, "\\'")}' }`
```

If `e.description` contains a newline (possible if `cleanDescription` doesn't strip them, and descriptions come from AI-generated changelogs), the split-on-newline approach will corrupt the array — partial objects appear, and the resulting JavaScript is syntactically invalid.

**Fix:**

```js
// agent/lib/changelog.js — replace updateAppChangelog function entirely

/**
 * Update the CHANGELOG array in appcore-data.js for in-app display.
 * If no CHANGELOG constant exists, creates one.
 */
export function updateAppChangelog(entries, getBufferFn, loadBufferFn) {
  if (!entries.length) return false;

  let buf = getBufferFn();

  // Sanitize descriptions: strip newlines and limit length to prevent malformed JS
  const newEntries = entries.map(e => {
    const safeDesc = e.description
      .replace(/'/g, "\\'")
      .replace(/[\r\n]+/g, ' ')
      .replace(/\s+/g, ' ')
      .trim()
      .slice(0, 120);
    return `  { date: '${e.date}', category: '${e.category}', text: '${safeDesc}' }`;
  });

  // Check if CHANGELOG constant exists
  const existingMatch = buf.match(/const CHANGELOG\s*=\s*\[([\s\S]*?)\];\s*\n/);

  if (existingMatch) {
    // Parse existing entries by matching complete object literals
    const existingContent = existingMatch[1].trim();
    const existingEntryMatches = [...existingContent.matchAll(/\{[^}]+\}/g)];
    const existingEntries = existingEntryMatches.map(m => '  ' + m[0].trim());

    // Combine new + existing, deduplicate by text content
    const seen = new Set();
    const combined = [];
    for (const entry of [...newEntries, ...existingEntries]) {
      const textMatch = entry.match(/text:\s*'([^']*)'/);
      const key = textMatch ? textMatch[1] : entry;
      if (!seen.has(key)) {
        seen.add(key);
        combined.push(entry);
      }
    }

    // Trim to MAX_APP_ENTRIES
    const trimmed = combined.slice(0, MAX_APP_ENTRIES);
    const newBlock = `const CHANGELOG = [\n${trimmed.join(',\n')}\n];\n`;
    buf = buf.replace(existingMatch[0], newBlock);
  } else {
    // Create CHANGELOG constant before the exports
    const exportMarker = '\n// ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n// EXPORTS';

    if (buf.includes(exportMarker)) {
      const changelogBlock = `\n// [SECTION:CHANGELOG]\nconst CHANGELOG = [\n${newEntries.join(',\n')}\n];\n`;
      buf = buf.replace(exportMarker, changelogBlock + exportMarker);

      // Also add to exports
      const exportMatch = buf.match(/(export \{[\s\S]*?)(};)/);
      if (exportMatch && !exportMatch[1].includes('CHANGELOG')) {
        buf = buf.replace(exportMatch[0], `${exportMatch[1]}  CHANGELOG,\n${exportMatch[2]}`);
      }
    }
  }

  loadBufferFn(buf);
  return true;
}
```

**Impact:** Prevents corrupted JavaScript output in `appcore-data.js` from multi-line descriptions, and adds deduplication to prevent the in-app changelog from showing the same entry multiple times.

## Issue 6: GitHub Workflow — Missing Concurrency Control Allows Overlapping Runs

**File:** `.github/workflows/ww-auto-update.yml`, top level  
**Severity:** MEDIUM

**Problem:** The workflow has no `concurrency` key. If a scheduled run is in progress and someone triggers a `workflow_dispatch`, both run simultaneously. Both will try to create/update the same branch `auto-update/full`, leading to race conditions where one run's `create-pull-request` step overwrites the other's changes.

**Fix — add concurrency control at the top of the workflow file:**

```yaml
# .github/workflows/ww-auto-update.yml — add after "on:" block, before "jobs:"

concurrency:
  group: ww-auto-update
  cancel-in-progress: true
```

Complete corrected top section:

```yaml
name: Auto-Update Game Data

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '0 0 * * 1'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      mode:
        description: 'Update mode'
        required: false
        default: 'full'
        type: choice
        options:
          - 'full'
          - 'micro'
          - 'audit'
          - 'images'
          - 'dry-run'
      only:
        description: 'Only update specific category (full mode)'
        required: false
        default: 'all'
        type: choice
        options:
          - 'all'
          - 'banners'
          - 'events'
          - 'characters'
          - 'images'
          - 'audit'

concurrency:
  group: ww-auto-update
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  update:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
```

**Impact:** Prevents overlapping agent runs from creating conflicting PRs or corrupting each other's file modifications.

## Issue 7: GitHub Workflow — Evolution Log Commit Step Has No Author and May Fail

**File:** `.github/workflows/ww-auto-update.yml`, lines 117–122  
**Severity:** LOW

**Problem:**

```yaml
- name: Commit evolution log
  if: steps.check.outputs.has_changes == 'true'
  run: |
    if [ -f agent/evolution-log.md ]; then
      git add agent/evolution-log.md
      git diff --cached --quiet || git commit -m "[agent] Update evolution log"
    fi
```

This step runs AFTER `peter-evans/create-pull-request@v6` has already committed and pushed. At this point:
1. The working directory may have been reset by the create-pull-request action.
2. There's no `git config user.name` or `user.email` set, so the commit may fail with "Please tell me who you are."
3. Even if it succeeds, the commit goes to the wrong branch (the default branch, not the PR branch).

**Fix — either remove this step (the create-pull-request action should include the evolution log) or move it before the PR creation:**

```yaml
# .github/workflows/ww-auto-update.yml — replace the "Commit evolution log" step
# and move the git add into the "Check for changes" step

      - name: Check for changes
        id: check
        run: |
          # Stage agent report files that may have been generated
          git add agent/run-report.md agent/CHANGELOG.md agent/evolution-log.md 2>/dev/null || true
          if [ -n "$(git status --porcelain)" ]; then
            echo "has_changes=true" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
            echo "Changed files:"
            git status --porcelain
          else
            echo "has_changes=false" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          fi

      # Remove the old "Commit evolution log" step entirely — it's now handled above
      # and the create-pull-request action will include evolution-log.md in its commit
```

Then remove the entire "Commit evolution log" step (lines 115–122).

**Impact:** Prevents silent workflow failures and ensures the evolution log is included in the PR rather than committed to the wrong branch.

## Issue 8: Vercel CSP Header Missing `wasm-unsafe-eval` for Potential Future Recharts/Vite HMR

**File:** `whispering-wishes-replit/vercel.json`, line 8  
**Severity:** LOW

**Problem:** The `script-src 'self'` directive is extremely strict — it blocks inline scripts and `eval`. This is good for security but may break Vite's HMR in development if the Vercel config is ever used for preview deployments. More importantly, if Recharts or any dependency ever uses Web Workers with blob URLs, the CSP will block them silently, causing charts to fail without any console error on some browsers.

This is not a current bug but a resilience concern. **No fix needed now** — documenting for awareness.

## Issue 10: `findBannerImages` Sends Excessive Content to Claude — 8000 Chars × 3 Pages + All Image URLs

**File:** `agent/lib/banner-images.js`, lines 83–97  
**Severity:** MEDIUM

**Problem:** The prompt to Claude includes up to 50 image URLs per page (150 total) plus 8000 chars of page text per page (24000 chars total), all in one prompt. This consumes ~8000-10000 tokens per call. Most of this content is irrelevant — the function is looking for ~3-5 specific banner images.

**Fix — reduce the content sent to Claude by pre-filtering image URLs:**

```js
// agent/lib/banner-images.js — replace the allContent construction (lines 83-97)

  // Build a combined content with relevant image URLs only
  // Pre-filter: only include URLs that might be banner art (usually contain
  // character names, "banner", "wish", "convene", or version numbers)
  const bannerKeywords = [
    ...bannerData.characters.map(c => c.name.toLowerCase().replace(/\s+/g, '')),
    ...bannerData.weapons.map(w => w.name.toLowerCase().replace(/\s+/g, '')),
    'banner', 'wish', 'convene', 'gacha', 'featured', 'event',
    bannerData.version?.replace('.', ''),
  ].filter(Boolean);

  const allContent = pages.map(p => {
    // Extract all image URLs from raw HTML
    const allImgUrls = [...p.content.matchAll(/(?:src|data-src|href)="(https?:\/\/[^"]+\.(?:webp|png|jpg|jpeg|avif)[^"]*)"/gi)]
      .map(m => m[1])
      .filter(url => !url.includes('thumbnail') && !url.includes('icon') && !url.includes('20px'));

    // Prioritize URLs containing banner-related keywords
    const relevantUrls = allImgUrls.filter(url => {
      const lower = url.toLowerCase();
      return bannerKeywords.some(kw => lower.includes(kw));
    });

    // Include relevant URLs first, then fill with others up to a cap
    const urls = [...new Set([...relevantUrls, ...allImgUrls])].slice(0, 30);

    // Reduce page text to 4000 chars — enough for context without token waste
    return `--- ${p.url} ---\nImage URLs (${urls.length}):\n${urls.join('\n')}\n\nPage text (excerpt):\n${p.content.replace(/<[^>]+>/g, ' ').replace(/\s+/g, ' ').slice(0, 4000)}`;
  }).join('\n\n');
```

**Impact:** Reduces Claude API token usage by ~40-50% per banner image search call (from ~10K tokens to ~5-6K tokens), saving ~$0.01-0.03 per agent run. Over weekly runs, this adds up. More importantly, smaller prompts get faster and more accurate responses.
